questions.explanation: An appeal (before a cour d'appel) and a pourvoi en cassation are voies de recours. "L'astreinte" is a daily penalty a court adds to an order; "la clause résolutoire" ends a contract; "le dispositif" is the operative part of the decision.

questions.stem: Name the numbered parts of this judgment.

image.alt: The first page of an invented judgment with its text blurred, divided into five numbered zones from top to bottom.

choices: l'en-tête : la juridiction et les parties
les faits et la procédure
les motifs
le dispositif
la voie de recours
la clause résolutoire
l'état des lieux
questions.explanation: A decision opens with the court, the date and the parties; then the facts and procedure so far; then the reasons ("les motifs"); then the operative part ("le dispositif", after "Par ces motifs"); and finally a mention of the possible remedy, here a pourvoi only, because the judgment was given en dernier ressort.

questions.stem: In a French research article, where do you expect "l'état de l'art" (the review of what is already known)?
choices: In the results
In the methods section
In the introduction
In the references only
questions.explanation: The introduction sets out "l'état de l'art" and the question. The methods ("matériel et méthodes") say how the work was done, the results what was measured, and the references list the sources.

questions.stem: Which section of an IMRaD article exists mainly so that another team can repeat the work?
choices: Introduction
Discussion
Résumé
Matériel et méthodes
questions.explanation: "Matériel et méthodes" describes the protocol in enough detail for the work to be reproductible: another team must be able to repeat it and get the same result.

questions.stem: Complete as a report would: "Il a été montré que la pile ___ un rendement de 48 % à charge nominale."
choices: atteint
atteigne
atteindre
atteignît
questions.explanation: "Il a été montré que" presents a result as established, so it takes the indicative: "atteint". "Atteigne" (present subjunctive) and "atteignît" (imperfect subjunctive) would mark doubt or follow a verb that needs the subjunctive; "atteindre" is an infinitive.

questions.stem: In an engineering report, what does "le rendement global" of a traction system measure?
choices: How fast the train can go
How much of the energy put in comes out as useful work
How much the fuel costs per kilometre
How many passengers the train can carry
questions.explanation: "Le rendement" here is efficiency: useful energy out divided by energy in. It is never "la performance". In farming it means yield, and in finance return.

questions.stem: Which line follows French typographic conventions?
choices: La ligne mesure 3.5 km et le rendement atteint 25%.
La ligne mesure 3,5 kms et le rendement atteint 25 %.
La ligne mesure 3,5 km et le rendement atteint 25 %.
La ligne mesure 3.5km et le rendement atteint 25 %.
questions.explanation: French uses a decimal comma, a space before a unit symbol and before %, and no plural "s" on symbols: "3,5 km", "25 %".

questions.stem: The report says one solution consumes "un ordre de grandeur de plus" than another. Roughly how much more is that?
choices: About twice as much
About 10 % more
Exactly as much
About ten times more
questions.explanation: An order of magnitude is a power of ten: "un ordre de grandeur de plus" is about ten times more. "Du même ordre de grandeur" means comparable.

questions.stem: What does this noun chain say? "La mise en service de la ligne est subordonnée à l'homologation du matériel roulant."
choices: The line can open only once the authority has approved the trains.
The trains will be approved only once the line has opened.
The line is already open, and the trains have been approved.
The authority has refused to approve the line's rails.
questions.explanation: Unpack each noun: "la mise en service" (the line starts running) depends on ("est subordonnée à") "l'homologation" (official approval) of "le matériel roulant" (the trains).

questions.stem: Complete the technical description: "Une batterie ___ la fonction de tampon."
choices: permet
assure
sert
constitue
questions.explanation: The fixed phrase is "assurer la fonction de" (to act as). "Permettre" needs "de" + infinitive ("permet de stocker"); "servir" needs "à" ("sert à stocker"); "constituer" means "to make up".

questions.stem: In paragraph 2 of the reading, how does the hydrogen chain compare with a train powered by a catenary?
choices: 48 % against 26 %: hydrogen is nearly twice as efficient
The same efficiency, but hydrogen is cheaper
26 % overall efficiency against about 80 %: roughly three times as much electricity for the same service
80 % against 26 %: hydrogen is three times more efficient
questions.explanation: Paragraph 2: the whole hydrogen chain gives "26 %, contre environ 80 % pour un train alimenté par caténaire", so "à service égal, la traction hydrogène consommerait environ trois fois plus d'électricité". 48 % is the fuel cell alone.

questions.stem: According to paragraph 4 of the reading, what decides whether hydrogen is worth it?
choices: The mass of the trainset
How often the trains run
The number of stops on the line
The price of hydrogen: above 9 euros per kilo, partial electrification is cheaper
questions.explanation: Paragraph 4: "la variable déterminante est le prix de l'hydrogène". The frequency of trains and the mass of the trainset are parameters with only "une influence marginale".

questions.stem: According to paragraph 5 of the reading, what must happen before commercial service starts?
choices: The trains must be approved after at least twelve months of trials on the line
The signalling and points must be replaced
A catenary must be installed on part of the line
The test bench must be fitted with more sensors
questions.explanation: Paragraph 5: no change to signalling or points is needed, but "la mise en service commerciale reste toutefois subordonnée à l'homologation du matériel", which "exigera des essais en ligne sur au moins douze mois".

questions.stem: Where did hydrogen trains first enter regular passenger service, according to their maker?
choices: In French Guiana, in 1968
In Lower Saxony, Germany, in September 2018
In the Netherlands, in 2024
In Switzerland, in 2012
questions.explanation: Two Alstom Coradia iLint trains entered regular service on 17 September 2018 in Lower Saxony, between Cuxhaven and Buxtehude, according to Alstom.

questions.stem: Which sentence belongs to the written report rather than to the radio interview?
choices: On perd beaucoup en route.
Sur le banc d'essai, oui, très bien.
Le rendement global s'établit à 26 %.
Tout dépendra du prix de l'hydrogène, hein.
questions.explanation: The report states a figure with a formal verb ("s'établit à"). "On perd beaucoup en route", "très bien" after "oui", and the tag "hein" belong to the engineer's spoken explanation.

questions.stem: Which statement about a fuel cell is true?
choices: It stores electricity, like a battery.
It takes its power from the overhead line.
It recovers energy when the train brakes.
It produces electricity for as long as it is supplied with hydrogen.
questions.explanation: "Une pile à combustible" converts a fuel (hydrogen) into electricity as long as fuel is supplied; "une batterie" stores electricity; the pantograph takes power from the catenary; regenerative braking recovers energy.

questions.stem: Listen to the test engineer. How does she judge the train?

audio.text: Journaliste : Alors, le train est-il prêt ? Ingénieure : Sur le banc, il a tenu toutes ses promesses. Mais je me garderai bien de crier victoire : un banc d'essai ne reproduit ni le froid de l'hiver, ni les pentes de la ligne.

choices: Cautiously: it did well on the bench, but real conditions haven't been tested
Triumphantly: the train is ready for passengers
Negatively: the bench tests failed
Indifferently: she has no opinion
questions.explanation: "Il a tenu toutes ses promesses" is positive, but "je me garderai bien de crier victoire" (I won't claim victory) and the winter cold and slopes the bench can't reproduce make her judgement cautious.

questions.stem: Listen to Paul and Léa. What is Léa's point?

audio.text: Paul : L'hydrogène, c'est l'avenir : zéro émission ! Léa : Zéro émission à l'échappement, oui. Mais tout dépend de la façon dont on produit l'hydrogène.

choices: Hydrogen trains pollute more than diesel trains
Hydrogen trains emit nothing at the exhaust, but their real impact depends on how the hydrogen is produced
Hydrogen is the only clean solution for railways
Hydrogen trains can't run on single-track lines
questions.explanation: Léa grants the point only in part ("Zéro émission à l'échappement, oui") and then shifts it: "tout dépend de la façon dont on produit l'hydrogène". She neither condemns hydrogen nor endorses it.

questions.stem: Listen to the science chronicler. What does he suggest about the press release?

audio.text: Chroniqueur : Le communiqué parle d'une « rupture technologique majeure ». Traduisons : le prototype a roulé quarante kilomètres sans tomber en panne. C'est encourageant. C'est aussi ce qu'on attend d'un train.

choices: That it hides a serious accident
That it understates a major breakthrough
That it inflates a modest result
That it was written by the chronicler himself
questions.explanation: He "translates" the press release's "rupture technologique majeure" as forty kilometres without breaking down, and adds that this is "ce qu'on attend d'un train": irony that deflates the claim.

questions.stem: Reformulation: rewrite in the passive, as a report would. "Nous avons réalisé les mesures sur un banc d'essai." → "Les mesures ___ sur un banc d'essai."
questions.explanation: The passive hides the team: "Les mesures ont été réalisées sur un banc d'essai." "Réalisées" agrees with "les mesures" (feminine plural).

questions.stem: Reformulation: replace the noun with a verb. "La ligne ouvrira après homologation du matériel." → "La ligne ouvrira une fois que le matériel ___ homologué."
questions.explanation: After "une fois que", French uses the futur antérieur for an action completed before the future one: "une fois que le matériel aura été homologué". "Sera homologué" is also correct.

questions.stem: Write "three and a half kilometres" in French notation, with figures and the unit symbol.
questions.explanation: A decimal comma, a space, and the symbol without a plural: "3,5 km".

questions.stem: Put the parts of a scientific article in the usual French order.
choices: Résumé
Introduction
Matériel et méthodes
Résultats
Discussion
Conclusion
questions.explanation: The IMRaD order: an abstract, then Introduction, Methods ("matériel et méthodes"), Results, Discussion, and a conclusion (then the references).

questions.stem: Match each railway term with its meaning.
choices: the overhead line
the points that switch a train to another track
a train that runs as one fixed unit
a device that measures a quantity
the vehicle that carries the motors
the driver's ticket machine
questions.explanation: "La caténaire" feeds power through the pantographe; "l'aiguillage" sends a train onto another track; "la rame" is a trainset (also an oar and a ream of paper); "le capteur" is a sensor; "la motrice" is the power car.

questions.stem: Which of these are typical of the French scientific voice? Select all that apply.
choices: the passive (les mesures ont été réalisées)
the impersonal il (il apparaît que)
the nous of the authors
first-person anecdotes (j'ai eu une idée un matin)
exclamations (quel résultat !)
questions.explanation: French science writing hides the person who acts: passives, the impersonal "il", "on", and the modest "nous" of the authors. Personal anecdotes and exclamations belong to other genres.

questions.stem: Name the numbered parts of the two trains.

image.alt: An electric train under overhead wires and a two-car hydrogen train, with five numbered markers and no labels.

choices: la caténaire
le pantographe
le réservoir d'hydrogène
la pile à combustible
la motrice
la batterie
l'aiguillage
questions.explanation: The electric train takes power from "la caténaire" through "le pantographe". The hydrogen train carries "le réservoir d'hydrogène" and "la pile à combustible" on the roof of its first car, "la motrice".

questions.stem: Complete: "Le chômage qui ne baisse pas, même quand la croissance revient, est dit ___."
choices: conjoncturel
excédentaire
boursier
structurel
questions.explanation: Unemployment that remains in normal times comes from how the economy is built: it is "structurel". "Conjoncturel" unemployment should fall when the cycle turns. "Excédentaire" means in surplus; "boursier" refers to the stock exchange.

questions.stem: What is "la déflation"?
choices: A general and lasting fall in prices
A general rise in prices
A fall in a company's share price
A cut in the central bank's key rate
questions.explanation: "La déflation" is the opposite of "l'inflation" (B2): prices fall across the economy for a long time, which discourages spending. A fall in one share is "un recul" or "un repli"; a rate cut is "une baisse des taux directeurs".

questions.stem: In the euro area, who sets "les taux directeurs"?
choices: The credit rating agencies
The European Central Bank (la BCE)
Each national government
The stock exchange
questions.explanation: The BCE runs the euro area's "politique monétaire", mainly through its key rates, which set what banks pay to borrow from it and earn on their deposits with it. In July 2022 it raised them for the first time since 2011, to curb inflation.

questions.stem: A rate goes from 4 % to 6 %. Which description is exact?
choices: Il progresse de 2 %, soit une hausse de deux points.
Il progresse de 50 points.
Il progresse de deux points, soit une hausse de 50 %.
Il progresse de 6 %, soit une hausse de deux points.
questions.explanation: From 4 % to 6 % is a rise of two percentage points ("deux points"), which is a rise of 50 % relative to 4 %. Confusing points and per cent is a classic error.

questions.stem: Complete: "Les banques ont prêté huit millions d'euros à l'entreprise : elles sont ses ___."
choices: débitrices
actionnaires
agences de notation
créancières
questions.explanation: Those who are owed money are "les créanciers" (here feminine, agreeing with "les banques": "créancières"). The firm, which owes, is "le débiteur". Shareholders own part of the capital; rating agencies grade debt.

questions.stem: Two companies combine to form a single new company. What is this called?
choices: une fusion
une acquisition
une levée de fonds
une introduction en Bourse
questions.explanation: "Une fusion" makes two companies one; "une acquisition" is one company buying another (the press often joins them as "une fusion-acquisition"). A fundraising round raises capital; a flotation lists the shares.

questions.stem: What does "le compte de résultat" show?
choices: What the company owns and owes on one day
Income and costs over the financial year, and the resulting profit or loss
The share price over the year
The list of shareholders and their dividends
questions.explanation: "Le compte de résultat" covers the whole "exercice": income ("les produits"), costs ("les charges") and the result. What a firm owns and owes on one day is "le bilan" (balance sheet).

questions.stem: Complete: "Une entreprise rentable peut pourtant manquer de ___ si ses clients paient en retard."
choices: capitalisation boursière
plus-value
trésorerie
solvabilité structurelle
questions.explanation: "La trésorerie" is the cash a firm actually has: profits on paper don't pay bills if customers pay late. Market capitalisation concerns listed shares; "une plus-value" is a capital gain.

questions.stem: A French company can no longer pay its debts that are due, but recovery seems possible. Which procedure does the court open?
choices: la liquidation judiciaire
l'introduction en Bourse
la levée de fonds
le redressement judiciaire
questions.explanation: In "cessation des paiements", the court opens a "redressement judiciaire" (an observation period, then a plan, a sale or liquidation) if recovery is possible, and a "liquidation judiciaire" if it is clearly impossible.

questions.stem: Within how many days of the cessation des paiements must the manager declare it, as of November 2026?
choices: 45 days
8 days
6 months
18 months
questions.explanation: The manager must declare the cessation des paiements within 45 days. Eighteen months is the longest possible observation period of a redressement judiciaire, renewals included.

questions.stem: According to paragraph 2 of the reading, what two things turned Cycles Lambert's fortunes?
choices: A strike at the factory and a fire in the warehouse
Large stocks sold off cheaply across the trade, and dearer credit after the BCE's rate rises
A fall in the price of e-bikes and a new tax on bicycles
The failure of its stock-market flotation and a merger
questions.explanation: Paragraph 2: "distributeurs et fabricants se sont retrouvés avec des stocks considérables, qu'ils ont écoulés à prix cassés", and "la hausse des taux directeurs … a renchéri le crédit". With its debt doubled, the combination was untenable.

questions.stem: According to paragraph 5 of the reading, what has happened to the investment fund's hopes?
choices: It has sold its shares at a profit
It has taken control of the company
The capital gain it expected at the flotation has turned into a likely loss
It has refused the Dutch group's merger
questions.explanation: Paragraph 5: "la plus-value qu'il espérait réaliser lors de l'introduction en Bourse s'est muée en moins-value probable". The fund still has to be convinced; it has not refused.

questions.stem: In paragraph 6 of the reading, why does the writer call the company's debt "structurel"?
choices: Because it was used to build a structure, the new factory
Because it will disappear when sales recover
Because it is owed to the state
Because it came from an investment bet made at the top of the cycle, not from a passing slump
questions.explanation: Paragraph 6 contrasts the "conjoncturel" fall in sales (an overstocking cycle now ending) with the "structurel" debt, which "découlait d'un pari pris au sommet du cycle": it won't go away with a recovery.

questions.stem: A company has been placed in receivership. In a news report, which wording is the most precise?
choices: L'entreprise a été placée en redressement judiciaire.
L'entreprise a fait faillite.
L'entreprise a été liquidée.
L'entreprise est entrée en déflation.
questions.explanation: "A fait faillite" is the everyday expression and doesn't say which procedure applies; "a été liquidée" names a different procedure (liquidation); "déflation" is about prices in the economy. The precise wording names the procedure.

questions.stem: Complete with the verb for a sudden, steep fall: "Le titre a ___ de 30 % en une seule séance."
choices: progressé
plongé
stagné
excédé
questions.explanation: A 30 % fall in one session is a plunge: "plonger". "Progresser" is to rise steadily; "stagner" (B2 honors) is to stay flat; "excéder" means to exceed and doesn't describe a movement of prices.

questions.stem: Listen to the economic news. How certain is the forecast?

audio.text: Journaliste : Selon les dernières projections, la croissance devrait atteindre un pour cent l'an prochain, sous réserve que la consommation des ménages se maintienne. Les économistes restent toutefois prudents.

choices: Certain: the figure has already been reached
Impossible: the economists reject it
Not certain: it depends on household spending holding up
Irrelevant: the newsreader calls it a rumour
questions.explanation: "Devrait atteindre" (is expected to), "sous réserve que la consommation des ménages se maintienne" (provided spending holds up) and "restent prudents" all mark a hedged forecast.

questions.stem: Listen to Hugo and Inès. What does Inès imply about the trade surplus?

audio.text: Hugo : Avec un tel excédent commercial, le pays se porte bien. Inès : Un excédent, oui. Mais parce que les importations s'effondrent : la demande intérieure est en panne.

choices: That it proves exports are booming
That it will turn into a deficit next year
That it was miscalculated by the government
That it reflects weak demand at home, not a healthy economy
questions.explanation: Inès concedes the fact ("Un excédent, oui") and gives another cause: imports have collapsed because "la demande intérieure est en panne". The surplus is a symptom, not good news.

questions.stem: Listen to the business chronicler. What is he suggesting?

audio.text: Chroniqueur : Le groupe explique ses pertes par des difficultés conjoncturelles. Conjoncturelles depuis cinq ans, tout de même.

choices: That the group's problems are in fact structural, whatever it claims
That the group's problems will pass quickly
That the group has never had any problems
That the group should go public
questions.explanation: The group calls its difficulties "conjoncturelles", which should pass; "conjoncturelles depuis cinq ans, tout de même" is ironic: problems that last five years are structural.

questions.stem: Reformulation: replace the everyday description with the legal term. "L'entreprise a fermé et ses biens ont été vendus pour payer ses dettes." → "L'entreprise a été placée en ___."
questions.explanation: When recovery is impossible, the court orders "la liquidation judiciaire": the assets are sold and the firm closes. "Faire faillite" is the everyday phrase.

questions.stem: Reformulation: say it in points. "Le taux de chômage est passé de 7 % à 8 %." → "Il a augmenté d'un ___."
questions.explanation: From 7 % to 8 % is one percentage point ("un point"), which is a rise of about 14 % relative to 7 %.

questions.stem: Complete with the opposite of "déficit": "Le budget de la région n'est pas en déficit mais en ___."
questions.explanation: "L'excédent" (surplus) is the opposite of "le déficit" (C1). The adjective is "excédentaire".

questions.stem: Put the stages of a French company's difficulties in order.
choices: la cessation des paiements
la déclaration au tribunal, sous 45 jours
l'ouverture du redressement judiciaire
la période d'observation
l'adoption d'un plan de redressement
questions.explanation: The firm can no longer pay its due debts; the manager declares it within 45 days; the court opens a redressement judiciaire; during the observation period creditors wait and the firm works on; at its end, the court may adopt a recovery plan (or order a sale or liquidation).

questions.stem: Match each term with what it means.
choices: what a company owns and owes on one day
income and costs over the financial year
the cash actually available
the share of the profit paid to shareholders
the financial year
the rate at which the central bank lends
questions.explanation: Here "le bilan" is the balance sheet (a new sense: you know it as "review") and "l'exercice" the financial year (you know it as "exercise"). The central bank's lending rate is "le taux directeur".

questions.stem: Which of these belong to monetary policy? Select all that apply.
choices: le taux directeur
la lutte contre l'inflation
le dividende
la levée de fonds
le compte de résultat
questions.explanation: Monetary policy, run by the central bank, uses the key rate ("le taux directeur") to keep prices stable (fighting inflation, or deflation). Dividends, fundraising rounds and income statements belong to company finance.

questions.stem: Name the numbered lines of this income statement.

image.alt: A simplified income statement of an invented company for 2024, in millions of euros, with the names of five lines removed and numbered; the amounts are shown.

choices: le chiffre d'affaires
les charges d'exploitation
le résultat d'exploitation
les charges financières
le résultat net
la trésorerie
le dividende
questions.explanation: Turnover (38.6) minus operating costs (41.9) gives the operating result (−3.3); financial costs (−1.1) and exceptional items and tax (+0.2) lead to the net result, a loss of 4.2 million.

questions.stem: What is "une aporie"?
choices: A starting point accepted without proof
A problem with no way out in the terms set
A statement that says the same thing twice
An opinion everyone repeats
questions.explanation: "Une aporie" is an impasse in reasoning. A starting point accepted without proof is "un axiome" (or "un postulat"); saying the same thing twice is "une tautologie"; an opinion everyone repeats is "un lieu commun".

questions.stem: "Le progrès, c'est aller de l'avant." What is wrong with this definition?
choices: It is an antinomy: it contradicts itself
It is an aporia: it has no solution
It is a tautology: it says the same thing twice
It is a paradigm: it changes a whole field
questions.explanation: "Progrès" already means moving forward, so the definition repeats the word in other terms and says nothing: "une tautologie". An antinomy opposes two claims that each seem justified.

questions.stem: Which -ism holds that all knowledge comes from experience?
choices: le rationalisme
l'idéalisme
le nihilisme
l'empirisme
questions.explanation: "L'empirisme" derives knowledge from experience; "le rationalisme" holds that reason can know some truths without it; "l'idéalisme" puts ideas or mind first; "le nihilisme" denies that any value holds.

questions.stem: Complete: "Pour certains croyants, la morale a une source ___ : elle vient d'au-delà du monde."
choices: transcendante
immanente
imminente
intrinsèque
questions.explanation: "Transcendant" means beyond the world or experience (spelt -ant). "Immanent" is its opposite (within); "imminent" means about to happen; "intrinsèque" means in itself.

questions.stem: Which sentence states a general truth about the human species?
choices: Homme est un être fini.
L'homme est un être fini.
Cet homme est un être fini.
Des hommes sont des êtres finis.
questions.explanation: French uses the generic definite article for a whole class: "L'homme est un être fini" (many writers now prefer "l'être humain"). The article can't be dropped; "cet homme" is one particular man; "des hommes" means some men.

questions.stem: An essayist writes: "L'essai prend le contre-pied de la doxa." What is the essay going against?
choices: Religious doctrine
The official statistics
Received opinion, what everyone accepts without examining it
The rules of grammar
questions.explanation: "La doxa" is received opinion. The word is slightly pejorative: an essayist names the doxa in order to question it.

questions.stem: In paragraph 2 of the reading, perfectibility in Condorcet is "posé comme un axiome". What does the writer mean?
choices: That it has been proved by experiment
That it contradicts itself
That everyone repeats it without thinking
That it is taken as a starting point and not proved
questions.explanation: An axiom is accepted without proof; the essay adds "On ne le démontre pas ; on le suppose." That is why the writer calls the idea of Progress a postulate, not an observation.

questions.stem: Complete: "Ce sont des risques ___ à toute innovation : on ne peut pas innover sans les courir."
choices: inhérents
étrangers
antérieurs
supérieurs
questions.explanation: "Inhérent à" means part of the nature of: the risks come with any innovation, as the second clause says. "Étrangers à" (unrelated to), "antérieurs à" (earlier than) and "supérieurs à" (greater than) are grammatical but contradict or miss that meaning.

questions.stem: According to the radio programme, what did Rousseau argue in his Discours sur les sciences et les arts (1750)?
choices: That human perfectibility has no limit
That the progress of the sciences and arts had not made people better
That science advances by changes of paradigm
That the future is written in advance
questions.explanation: Rousseau's first Discours, written for a prize question of the Académie de Dijon, answered no: the arts and sciences had not improved morals. Unlimited perfectibility is Condorcet's idea; paradigm shifts are Kuhn's (1962).

questions.stem: When and how was Condorcet's Esquisse d'un tableau historique des progrès de l'esprit humain written?
choices: In 1750, for a prize of the Académie de Dijon
In 1907, as a reply to Bergson
In 1793–1794, while he was in hiding during the Terror; it was published after his death, in 1795
In 1962, as a history of scientific revolutions
questions.explanation: Condorcet wrote the Esquisse in hiding in 1793–1794; it appeared in 1795, after his death. 1750 is Rousseau's first Discours, 1907 Bergson's L'Évolution créatrice, 1962 Kuhn's book.

questions.stem: In paragraph 1 of the reading, which two claims does the writer distinguish?
choices: That science progresses, and that art declines
That Rousseau was right, and that Condorcet was wrong
That progress is measurable, and that it is always good
That particular advances exist, and that history as a whole moves towards the better
questions.explanation: Paragraph 1: "l'existence de progrès particuliers … et l'idée du Progrès, au singulier et avec une majuscule, selon laquelle l'histoire humaine irait, dans son ensemble, vers le mieux."

questions.stem: What is the writer's own position in paragraph 4 of the reading?
choices: Progress is neither a law of history nor an illusion, but a task that depends on us
Progress is a law of history, so it will happen whatever we do
Progress is an illusion, so nothing can be done
The question has no answer, so the debate should stop
questions.explanation: Paragraph 4 goes beyond the antinomy dialectically: "Le progrès n'est ni une loi de l'histoire … ni une illusion … : il est une tâche. Rien ne garantit qu'il ait lieu, et c'est précisément pourquoi il dépend de nous."

questions.stem: In paragraph 5 of the reading, what does "l'altérité des autres peuples et des générations futures" forbid?
choices: Comparing different societies at all
Judging what is better by our own present interests alone
Speaking about the future
Believing in particular advances
questions.explanation: Because other peoples and future generations have a point of view that is "jamais exactement le nôtre", we can't judge "du mieux à l'aune de nos seuls intérêts présents".

questions.stem: In an essay on the philosophy of mind, a writer criticises "le matérialisme". What does the word most likely mean here?
choices: Caring too much about possessions
Having high ideals
The view that matter comes first and mind depends on it
Believing that nothing has value
questions.explanation: In a philosophy text the technical sense wins: "le matérialisme" puts matter first. Caring about possessions is the everyday sense; ideals belong to "l'idéalisme" in its everyday sense; believing nothing has value is "le nihilisme".

questions.stem: Which sentence is jargon rather than precise abstract writing?
choices: L'idée de progrès repose sur un postulat qu'on ne peut pas démontrer.
Il convient de distinguer le progrès technique du progrès moral.
Par finitude, on entend la condition d'un être limité dans le temps.
La problématisation de l'axiologie progressiste invite à une déconstruction de son paradigme ontologique.
questions.explanation: The sentence on "la problématisation de l'axiologie progressiste" piles up abstract nouns with no subject that acts and no clear claim. The others use one technical term each, in a clear sentence: a postulate, a distinction, a definition.

questions.stem: Listen to the extract from the programme. What is Mehdi Laroche's point?

audio.text: Claire Vasseur : Le progrès, une illusion ? Mehdi Laroche : Dire cela, c'est confondre deux choses : les progrès, que l'on mesure, et le Progrès, que l'on postule.

choices: Measurable advances and Progress as a principle are two different things
Progress is an illusion, as everyone now agrees
Nothing in human life can be measured
Progress is proved by the history of science
questions.explanation: He says the claim "confuses two things": "les progrès, que l'on mesure" (particular advances) and "le Progrès, que l'on postule" (Progress assumed as a principle). He doesn't endorse the commonplace.

questions.stem: Listen to Anne Feuillet and Mehdi Laroche. What does Laroche's remark about Condorcet convey?

audio.text: Anne Feuillet : Condorcet croyait à une perfectibilité sans limite. Mehdi Laroche : Écrire cela caché, traqué par la Terreur… Il faut reconnaître qu'il avait de la suite dans les idées.

choices: Contempt for Condorcet's naivety
A wry admiration for Condorcet's persistence in desperate circumstances
Doubt that Condorcet wrote the book
Indifference to the whole question
questions.explanation: "Avoir de la suite dans les idées" means sticking to one's ideas. Said of a man writing about unlimited progress while hunted by the Terror, it is wry, but admiring, not contemptuous.

questions.stem: Listen to the listener who calls the programme. What does he imply about the guest?

audio.text: Auditeur : Votre invité parle d'« immanence téléologique aporétique ». Moi, j'ai surtout compris qu'il ne savait pas.

choices: That he speaks too simply for a philosopher
That he has said something deep and true
That his jargon hides the fact that he has nothing clear to say
That he quoted Rousseau incorrectly
questions.explanation: The listener repeats the guest's pile of abstract nouns, then mocks it: "Moi, j'ai surtout compris qu'il ne savait pas." Jargon, for him, covers an absence of thought.

questions.stem: Reformulation: translate with the generic article. "Man is a social being." → "___ est un être social."
questions.explanation: French needs the article for a whole class: "L'homme est un être social." Many writers now prefer "L'être humain", also accepted.

questions.stem: Reformulation: replace the noun with a verb. "La définition du concept précède son usage." → "On ___ le concept avant de l'utiliser."
questions.explanation: Turning the noun back into a verb gives the sentence a subject that acts: "On définit le concept avant de l'utiliser." This is the first step in rewriting jargon.

questions.stem: Complete the defining formula: "___ altérité, on entend le fait que l'autre n'est pas moi."
questions.explanation: "Par X, on entend …" (by X we mean …) is one of the defining formulas, with "X désigne …", "X renvoie à …" and "On appelle X …".

questions.stem: Put the steps of a dialectical argument in order.
choices: a thesis is stated
an opposing thesis is set against it
the tension between them is examined
a new position goes beyond the opposition
questions.explanation: "La dialectique" moves through opposition: a thesis meets its contrary, and the tension leads to a new position (the "dépassement" of C1's plan dialectique). The essay's paragraph 4 does this with ascent and fall.

questions.stem: Match each -ism with its core idea.
choices: knowledge comes from experience
reason can know without experience
everything has causes that make it necessary
we make ourselves by our choices
no value or meaning holds
some values hold for every human being
questions.explanation: The distractor describes "l'universalisme", opposed to "le relativisme". The -isms come in pairs: empiricism and rationalism, determinism and free will.

questions.stem: Which of these words name an idea in order to question it, and are slightly pejorative in an essay? Select all that apply.
choices: la doxa
le lieu commun
le concept
l'axiome
la dialectique
questions.explanation: "La doxa" (received opinion) and "le lieu commun" (a commonplace) name what everyone thinks without examining it, which the writer is about to question. "Concept", "axiome" and "dialectique" are neutral terms of reasoning.

questions.stem: Name the numbered -isms on this concept map.

image.alt: A concept map of the -isms with six names removed and numbered; each oval keeps a short English gloss.

choices: l'empirisme
le rationalisme
le matérialisme
l'idéalisme
le déterminisme
l'universalisme
le nihilisme
le scepticisme
questions.explanation: Knowing: empiricism (experience) against rationalism (reason). The real: materialism (matter first) against idealism (mind first). Freedom: determinism against free will. Values: universalism against relativism.

questions.stem: When was the French space agency, the CNES, created?
choices: In April 1968
In December 1979
In December 1961
questions.explanation: The CNES was created on 19 December 1961. April 1968 is the first launch from Kourou, 1975 the founding of ESA, December 1979 the first flight of Ariane 1.

questions.stem: Why is Kourou a good place to launch rockets?
choices: It is about five degrees north of the equator, with open sea to the east
It is in mainland France, close to the factories
It is near the North Pole, where orbits are shorter
It is far from any sea, so debris falls on land
questions.explanation: Near the equator, a rocket launched eastward gets the most help from the Earth's rotation; open sea to the east means stages and debris fall away from people.

questions.stem: What does "la coiffe" do during a launch?
choices: It lights the engines at the end of the countdown
It protects the payload through the atmosphere, then is jettisoned
It carries the astronauts back to Earth
It holds the rocket on the launch pad
questions.explanation: "La coiffe" (the fairing) covers "la charge utile" while the rocket crosses the dense atmosphere, then splits open and falls away ("le largage de la coiffe"). In everyday French, "une coiffe" is a traditional headdress.

questions.stem: Complete the commentary: "Le largage de la coiffe interviendra lorsque la charge utile ___ plus besoin de protection."
choices: n'a
n'ait
n'aura
n'avait
questions.explanation: After "lorsque", French uses the future when the main verb is in the future ("interviendra … lorsque la charge utile n'aura plus besoin"), where English uses the present. "N'a" copies English; "n'ait" is a subjunctive, which "lorsque" doesn't take.

questions.stem: Why can a fixed dish on the ground point at a satellite in geostationary orbit?
choices: Because the satellite is only a few kilometres up
Because the satellite is above the North Pole
Because the dish follows the satellite with a motor
Because the satellite goes round in the time the Earth takes to turn, so it seems still
questions.explanation: A geostationary orbit is about 36,000 km above the equator; a satellite there completes one orbit as the Earth turns once, so from the ground it doesn't move.

questions.stem: Which statement about the words for space travellers is accurate?
choices: Astronaute is the more common word and FranceTerme's headword; spationaute is a correct French coinage
Spationaute is the only correct French word; astronaute is an anglicism
Cosmonaute is used for French astronauts
Spationaute is slang and should be avoided in writing
questions.explanation: The Académie's dictionary records "spationaute", a French coinage used mainly for French and European crews, and notes that "astronaute" is more common; FranceTerme gives "astronaute" as its headword, with "spationaute" as a synonym. "Cosmonaute" is used for Soviet and Russian crews.

questions.stem: What was new about Thomas Pesquet's Alpha mission in 2021?
choices: It was the first launch from Kourou
He became the first French commander of the International Space Station
It was the last flight of Ariane 5
It was his first stay in space
questions.explanation: During Alpha (April to November 2021, on a Crew Dragon) he became the first French commander of the station. His first stay was Proxima (2016–2017, launched on a Soyuz). Ariane 5 last flew in 2023.

questions.stem: A press release says: "L'amarrage du vaisseau à la station est intervenu à 10 h 08." What happened?
choices: The spacecraft left the station at 10.08
The spacecraft re-entered the atmosphere at 10.08
The spacecraft docked with the station at 10.08
The spacecraft was launched at 10.08
questions.explanation: "L'amarrage" is docking (and, for a boat, mooring); "intervenir" is the formal "avoir lieu". Leaving is "le désamarrage" or "le départ"; re-entry is "la rentrée atmosphérique".

questions.stem: What does the French space operations law of 3 June 2008 (the LOS) require?
choices: That every launch take place from mainland France
That French satellites be built only by the state
That space debris be counted once a year by the Académie des sciences
Authorisation for launches and satellite operations by French operators, checked by the CNES against technical rules
questions.explanation: Under the LOS, launches, control in orbit and return to Earth carried out from France or by a French operator need authorisation; the CNES checks requests against technical rules, which include limiting debris.

questions.stem: Unpack the noun into a verb. "L'amarrage du vaisseau est intervenu à 10 h 08." → "Le vaisseau s'est ___ à 10 h 08."
questions.explanation: "L'amarrage" comes from "s'amarrer"; the participle agrees with "le vaisseau" (masculine singular): "Le vaisseau s'est amarré". Press releases nominalise; unpack them for a general reader.

questions.stem: Put the stages of a launch in order, as in the lesson's commentary.
choices: le compte à rebours
la mise à feu
le décollage
la séparation des propulseurs d'appoint
le largage de la coiffe
la mise en orbite de la charge utile
questions.explanation: The countdown runs to zero, the engines are ignited, the thrust lifts the rocket, the side boosters separate (about two minutes in), the fairing is jettisoned above about a hundred kilometres, and the last stage places the payload in orbit.

questions.stem: Match each French term with its English equivalent.
choices: launch pad
thrust
atmospheric re-entry
ignition
space debris
fuel cell
questions.explanation: "La poussée" also means a push or a surge; "la mise à feu" is also the firing of a charge. "Fuel cell" is "la pile à combustible" (lesson 10).

questions.stem: Which of these are true of the geostationary orbit? Select all that apply.
choices: It lies above the equator
It is about 36,000 km up
A satellite there seems still from the ground
It passes over both poles
It is the orbit of the International Space Station
questions.explanation: A geostationary orbit is circular, above the equator, about 36,000 km up, with a period equal to the Earth's rotation. A polar orbit passes over the poles; the space station flies much lower, at a few hundred kilometres.

questions.stem: Name the numbered parts of this rocket on its pad.

image.alt: A rocket beside its service tower on a launch pad, with five numbered markers: at the nose, inside a cut-away window in the nose, on a band below the nose, on one of the side boosters and on the ground of the pad.

choices: la coiffe
la charge utile
l'étage supérieur
un propulseur d'appoint
le pas de tir
la caténaire
la station spatiale
questions.explanation: From the top: "la coiffe" (fairing) protects "la charge utile" (here a satellite); below it, "l'étage supérieur"; on the sides, "les propulseurs d'appoint"; under everything, "le pas de tir".

questions.stem: Before 1804, what did "le droit écrit" mean in France?
choices: The law of the south, based on Roman law
Any law written on paper, as opposed to custom
The law of the north, based on local customs
The laws passed by the Revolutionary assemblies
questions.explanation: "Le droit écrit" was the Roman-law tradition of the south; the north followed "le droit coutumier", customs that had themselves been written down. The name refers to the Roman tradition, not to writing.

questions.stem: Why did Bonaparte's commission of 1800 include two lawyers from the north and two from the south?
choices: So that each region could keep its own code
So that the Code would be a compromise between customary law and written law
So that the Code could be written in two languages
So that the commission could vote by region
questions.explanation: Tronchet and Bigot de Préameneu came from the customary-law north, Portalis and Maleville from the written-law south: the Code was meant to blend the two traditions into one law.

questions.stem: What does Portalis argue in his Discours préliminaire, as the lesson describes it?
choices: That laws should foresee every possible case in detail
That judges should never interpret the law
That laws should state general principles, and judges apply them to real cases
That customs should be abolished without replacement
questions.explanation: Portalis argues, roughly, that a lawmaker can't foresee everything, so laws should lay down general principles and leave their application to judges and jurists.

questions.stem: On what date was the Code civil promulgated?
choices: 14 July 1789
18 November 2016
4 June 1970
21 March 1804
questions.explanation: A law of 21 March 1804 (30 ventôse an XII) gathered thirty-six laws into one "Code civil des Français" of 2,281 articles. 4 June 1970 is the law on parental authority; 18 November 2016 the law on divorce without a judge.

questions.stem: What did Stendhal say about the Code civil, in a draft of a letter to Balzac in 1840?
choices: That he read a few pages every morning while writing La Chartreuse de Parme, to set his tone
That its style was too dry for any novelist to read
That he had helped to draft it
That it should be rewritten in verse
questions.explanation: Stendhal said he read a few pages of the Code each morning to set the tone of La Chartreuse de Parme: he wanted its plainness. The anecdote is often repeated as praise of the Code's style.

questions.stem: What can the holder of a usufruct (l'usufruitier) NOT do with a house?
choices: Live in it
Sell it
Rent it out
Keep the rent
questions.explanation: "L'usufruit" is the right to use and enjoy a thing that belongs to someone else, on condition of keeping it intact. The usufructuary can live in the house or let it and keep the rent, but only the bare owner can sell it.

questions.stem: Article 1240 of the Code civil (formerly 1382) states, in one sentence, the principle of civil liability. What is it?
choices: Every contract must be in writing to be valid
No one may be judged twice for the same act
Whoever, by their fault, causes damage to another must repair it
The law applies only to the future
questions.explanation: The article lays down the basis of civil liability in one general sentence, without listing kinds of fault or damage; two centuries of case law have filled it in. It was renumbered 1240 by the 2016 reform of contract law.

questions.stem: Which law replaced "la puissance paternelle" with "l'autorité parentale"?
choices: The law of 21 March 1804
The law of 13 July 1965
The ordinance of 4 July 2005
The law of 4 June 1970
questions.explanation: The law of 4 June 1970 replaced paternal authority with parental authority exercised by both parents. 1965 reformed marriage settlements; the 2005 ordinance removed the distinction between legitimate and natural parentage.

questions.stem: A couple married in France without a contract. What is their "régime matrimonial" by default, since the 1965 reform?
choices: La communauté réduite aux acquêts: what each earns during the marriage is shared
La séparation de biens: nothing is ever shared
La puissance paternelle: the husband manages everything
L'usufruit: one spouse uses the other's property
questions.explanation: Since the 1965 reform (and still as of November 2026), couples who sign no contract are under "la communauté réduite aux acquêts": earnings during the marriage are shared, and what each owned before, or inherits, stays their own.

questions.stem: Put these events in the history of the Code civil in order.
choices: Promulgation of the Code civil
The Naquet law brings back divorce
Parental authority replaces paternal authority
Divorce by mutual consent is introduced by a judge-led reform
Divorce by mutual consent without a judge becomes possible
questions.explanation: 1804 (promulgation), 1884 (Naquet law), 1970 (parental authority), 1975 (divorce reform), 2016 (divorce without a judge, in force from 2017).

questions.stem: Match each term with its meaning.
choices: gathering scattered rules into one written code
the legal link between a child and its parents
the right to use and enjoy another's property
law based on local customs
the lawmaker
a lawyer who pleads in court
questions.explanation: The distractor describes "l'avocat". "Le juriste" is broader: anyone trained in law.

questions.stem: Describe an article in your own French: "L'article 1240 du Code civil ___ le principe de la responsabilité civile." Give one verb in the present.
questions.explanation: Verbs of description for a legal text: "poser le principe de", "énoncer", "consacrer", "établir". The present serves both to describe and, in the article itself, to prescribe.

questions.stem: Give today's legal term for what the Code of 1804 called "la puissance paternelle" (with its article).
questions.explanation: "L'autorité parentale" (1970) names a duty exercised by both parents in the child's interest, not a father's power.

questions.stem: In which of these places did the Code of 1804 remain in force after French rule ended? Select all that apply.
choices: Belgium
Luxembourg
England
Québec
Louisiana
questions.explanation: The Code stayed in force in Belgium and Luxembourg (Belgium has been replacing it book by book with a new Civil Code). It inspired the codes of Louisiana and Québec (the Civil Code of Lower Canada, 1866) without being in force there; England kept its common law.

questions.stem: Why did the OIF's count of French speakers rise from 321 million (2022) to 396 million in its 2026 report?
choices: Because Mali, Burkina Faso and Niger made French their only official language
Because French replaced English as an official language in several countries
Mostly because of a new method that counts children aged 6 to 9 schooled in French
Because Algeria joined the OIF and counted all its speakers
questions.explanation: The 2026 report counts, for the first time, children aged 6 to 9 who are schooled in French; much of the rise comes from that change of method. Mali, Burkina Faso and Niger did the opposite: they made French a working language. Algeria is not a member of the OIF.

questions.stem: Which statement about the status of French is accurate as of November 2026?
choices: In Mali, the national languages are official and French is a working language.
In Senegal, Wolof has replaced French as the official language.
In Cameroon, French is the only official language.
In Niger, French is still the only official language.
questions.explanation: Mali's constitution of July 2023 made the national languages official and French the working language. Senegal's official language is French (Wolof is a national language and lingua franca); Cameroon has French and English; Niger's Charte de la refondation (2025) made French a working language.

questions.stem: A Malian trader and a Senegalese customer, whose first languages differ, do business in French. For the two of them, French is…
choices: a langue vernaculaire
an urban vernacular
their national language
a langue véhiculaire
questions.explanation: A langue véhiculaire (lingua franca) is used between people whose first languages differ. A langue vernaculaire is the language of a community among its own members; French is not a national language of either country in that sense, and an urban vernacular is a youth variety such as nouchi.

questions.stem: How was "l'essencerie" (petrol station, Senegal) made?
choices: It was borrowed from Wolof and spelt the French way.
A French suffix, -erie, was added to a French noun, essence.
An old French word took on a new meaning.
Two French nouns were joined into a compound.
questions.explanation: Essence + -erie gives l'essencerie, the place that sells the product, as la boulangerie and la papeterie are in France. Le grin is a borrowing, gâter (to break down) a shift of meaning, and le taxi-brousse a compound.

questions.stem: In Abidjan, a friend tells you: « Ma voiture est gâtée. » What does she mean?
choices: Her car has been ruined by the rain.
Her car has broken down.
Her car has been spoilt with new accessories.
Her car has been stolen.
questions.explanation: In much of West Africa gâter means to break down: une voiture gâtée won't start. In France gâter means to spoil (food, a child) or to ruin, which is what the other choices play on.

questions.stem: Which description of "le deuxième bureau" matches the lesson?
choices: A neutral administrative word for a branch office
A polite word for a second wife in a legal marriage
A slang word for a second job in the evening
An informal, judgemental word for a man's mistress
questions.explanation: Le deuxième bureau (literally the second office) is a man's mistress. It is informal and it judges: recognise it, don't use it. In France, le Deuxième Bureau was also the name of an old military intelligence service, but that is history, not an office of a company.

questions.stem: In paragraph 2 of the reading (the tontine), how does the savings club work?
choices: Each month twelve women pay the same sum and one of them takes the whole pot.
A bank lends twelve families money at a low rate of interest.
Twelve women pay into a fund that is shared out only at the end of the year.
The market traders share their profits every week.
questions.explanation: Mamadou explains that each month twelve women pay the same amount and each month one of them takes la cagnotte (the pot): a bank "sans guichet ni intérêts", with no counter and no interest.

questions.stem: In paragraph 3 of the reading, why does nobody complain that the bush taxi leaves at ten instead of eight?
choices: Because the driver was waiting for a marabout
Because the road to Thiès was closed until ten
Because the departure is the moment when the car is full
Because the passengers themselves arrived late
questions.explanation: The journalist concludes: "le départ, ici, c'est le moment où l'on est au complet": a taxi-brousse leaves when it is full, not at a set time.

questions.stem: In paragraph 5 of the reading, the journalist writes « Le mot fait rire, mais il juge ». What does she imply about "deuxième bureau"?
choices: It is a legal term that judges use in court.
It is a joke that nobody in Abidjan takes seriously.
Its humour hides a moral judgement on the people it describes.
It is too rude to be said aloud in a maquis.
questions.explanation: The sentence contrasts the laughter the word causes with the judgement it carries: calling a woman someone's deuxième bureau mocks and condemns. That is why the lesson tells you to recognise the word, not to use it.

questions.stem: In the reading, why is it « mon hôtesse m'a cadeautée », with -ée?
choices: Because the direct object m' is the journalist, a woman, and comes before avoir
Because the subject, mon hôtesse, is feminine
Because cadeauter always agrees with its subject
Because verbs from Africa always end in -ée
questions.explanation: With avoir the participle agrees with a direct object placed before it, as in elle m'a remerciée. Here m' stands for the journalist, who is a woman. The subject (mon hôtesse) plays no part in the agreement with avoir.

questions.stem: Leaving a maquis in Abidjan, a young man says: « On s'est enjaillés ! » He means…
choices: We got really angry!
We got completely lost!
We ate too much!
We had a great time!
questions.explanation: In nouchi, s'enjailler (from English enjoy) is to have fun. You only need to recognise it: nouchi is an urban vernacular, not something learners are expected to speak.

questions.stem: « Le mbom-là ne pense qu'à tchop. » (That guy only thinks about eating.) This sentence is an example of…
choices: nouchi
camfranglais
joual
reference French
questions.explanation: Le mbom (guy) and tchop (to eat) are camfranglais, the mixed urban variety of Cameroon's cities. Nouchi is Ivorian, joual is from Montreal (lesson 15), and reference French would say Ce type ne pense qu'à manger.

questions.stem: You are writing a report for readers in France about fuel prices in Dakar. Which sentence suits it best?
choices: À l'essencerie, le litre a grave augmenté, mon frère.
Le litre a augmenté dans les stations-service de Dakar (les essenceries, comme on dit au Sénégal).
Le litre, il a gâté à Dakar, présentement.
Les essenceries, elles ont ambiancé les prix.
questions.explanation: For French readers the safe choice is the France word with the Senegalese one glossed, as a journalist would do. The other sentences are informal (grave, mon frère), misuse gâter (to break down) or make no sense (ambiancer = to liven up a party).

questions.stem: Listen to the radio chronicle. What is the chronicler's attitude to words like essencerie?

audio.text: Chroniqueuse : Certains puristes s'étranglent quand ils entendent « essencerie » ou « cadeauter ». Pourtant, ces mots sont fabriqués exactement comme « boulangerie » ou « papeterie ». Ce que ces messieurs appellent des fautes, les linguistes l'appellent de la créativité.

choices: She thinks they should be kept out of schools and newspapers.
She lists them neutrally without giving any opinion.
She explains that they were borrowed from English.
She defends them as ordinary French word formation and gently mocks the purists.
questions.explanation: She points out that essencerie is built exactly like boulangerie or papeterie, and turns the purists' word fautes against them: what they call mistakes, linguists call creativity. That is a defence, with a touch of irony.

questions.stem: Listen to Awa and Moussa. What is Moussa's position?

audio.text: Awa : Le français n'est plus langue officielle au Mali. C'est la fin du français là-bas. Moussa : Pas si vite. Il reste la langue de travail, et l'administration l'utilise toujours. Ce qui a changé, c'est le symbole.

choices: French keeps a practical role in Mali even though its status has changed.
French has already disappeared from Malian offices and schools.
Mali has made French its only official language again.
He agrees with Awa that French has no future in Mali.
questions.explanation: Moussa answers "pas si vite": French remains the working language and the administration still uses it; what has changed is the symbol. He qualifies Awa's claim rather than accepting it.

questions.stem: Listen to the customer and the waitress in a maquis. What does the customer really mean?

audio.text: Client : Super, le service ! Une heure pour un poisson braisé, c'est un record. Serveuse : Merci, monsieur, on fait de notre mieux !

choices: He is sincerely praising how fast the food came.
He is asking for a second grilled fish.
He is complaining, ironically, that the service is slow.
He is complaining that his fish is cold.
questions.explanation: "Une heure pour un poisson braisé, c'est un record" praises in form and complains in substance: an hour is not a speed record. The waitress's cheerful thanks pretends to take the compliment at face value.

questions.stem: Which of these words were made with a French suffix or by turning a French noun into a verb? Select all that apply.
choices: le grin
l'essencerie
le boubou
la dibiterie
le gbaka
cadeauter
questions.explanation: L'essencerie (essence + -erie) and la dibiterie (the suffix -erie on a base usually traced to débiter) use a French suffix, and cadeauter turns the noun cadeau into a verb. Le grin and le boubou are borrowings from West African languages, and le gbaka is not built on a French word.

questions.stem: Match each word to its meaning.
choices: an open-air restaurant (Côte d'Ivoire)
a shared taxi on a fixed route
a rotating savings club
a grilled-meat stall (Senegal)
friends who meet every day over tea
a petrol station
questions.explanation: Le maquis is the Ivorian open-air restaurant; le woro-woro the Abidjan shared taxi; la tontine the savings club; la dibiterie the Senegalese grill; le grin the tea circle of Mali and Burkina Faso. A petrol station would be l'essencerie, which is not in the list.

questions.stem: Name the numbered parts of this street scene in Abidjan.

image.alt: A street scene in Abidjan with five numbered markers: on a minibus with a sliding door, on a small shared taxi, on an open-air restaurant under a corrugated roof, on a man in a long, wide blue robe, and on a woman in a skirt of wrapped printed cloth.

choices: le gbaka
le woro-woro
le maquis
le boubou
le pagne
l'essencerie
la tontine
questions.explanation: 1 is the minibus (le gbaka), 2 the shared taxi (le woro-woro), 3 the open-air restaurant (le maquis), 4 the man's long robe (le boubou), 5 the woman's wrapped cloth (le pagne). There is no petrol station in the picture, and a tontine is a savings club, not a thing you can see.

questions.stem: Reformulation. Rewrite for a reader in France: « Le directeur n'est pas là présentement. » Replace "présentement" with a word or phrase usual in France. Type only the replacement.
questions.explanation: Présentement is ordinary in Africa and Québec but is often felt as old-fashioned in France, where people say en ce moment, pour le moment, pour l'instant or actuellement.

questions.stem: Reformulation. Rewrite for a reader in France, without the Ivorian word: « Ce soir, on va au maquis. » → « Ce soir, on va au ___. » Type the missing word or words.
questions.explanation: In Côte d'Ivoire le maquis is an open-air restaurant; in France the word would suggest scrubland or the wartime Resistance. On va au restaurant (informally au resto) keeps the meaning.

questions.stem: Complete with the France expression. Where an Ivorian says « Ma voiture est gâtée », a speaker in France says « Ma voiture est en ___. »
questions.explanation: Gâter in the sense of to break down corresponds to être en panne in France: ma voiture est en panne.

questions.stem: Which language became official in Morocco in 2011 and in Algeria in 2016?
choices: French
Darija
Amazigh (Tamazight)
Spanish
questions.explanation: Morocco's constitution of 2011 made Amazigh an official language; in Algeria, where it had been a national language since 2002, the constitutional revision of 2016 made it official. French has no official status in either country, and darija is the spoken Arabic, not a separate official language.

questions.stem: What is darija?
choices: The spoken Arabic of daily life in the Maghreb
The standard Arabic of the constitution and the news
A Berber language of the Atlas mountains
The French of the pieds-noirs of Algeria
questions.explanation: Darija is everyday spoken Arabic, different in each country and from the standard. Standard Arabic is the official written language; Amazigh is the Berber language; the pieds-noirs' French is le pataouète.

questions.stem: A French newspaper prints « le hittiste » in italics and explains it in a footnote. In that article, the word is…
choices: a substrate
an interference
a calque
a xénisme
questions.explanation: A xénisme is a borrowing still felt as foreign, which is why it is in italics and explained. A substrate is an earlier language, interference a feature carried from one language into another, and a calque a word-for-word translation.

questions.stem: An English speaker says « Je suis chaud » to mean that she feels hot. Linguists call this…
choices: code-switching
interference
a xénisme
a substrate
questions.explanation: She has carried an English construction (I am hot) into French, where the right form is j'ai chaud: that is interference. Code-switching would be switching into English itself.

questions.stem: Linguists find traces of Gaulish in French words such as le chêne and la boue. For French, Gaulish is…
choices: a borrowing
a substrate
a xénisme
code-switching
questions.explanation: A substrate is an earlier language that was replaced but left traces in the new one, as Gaulish did in French and Amazigh in the Arabic of the Maghreb.

questions.stem: Yasmine starts in French and ends in darija when she is moved. How would a linguist describe this?
choices: As proof that she speaks neither language well
As interference that she should learn to correct
As a xénisme printed in italics
As code-switching, a normal skill of bilingual speakers
questions.explanation: Switching languages for an emotion, a joke or to show who you are is alternance codique, a skill of bilinguals. The lesson's Common mistakes warn against calling it a lack of French.

questions.stem: Which sentence suits a formal letter to a town hall?
choices: Ma famille au complet assistera à la cérémonie.
Toute la smala débarque à la cérémonie.
On vient avec toute la tribu, c'est kif-kif.
Ça va être le souk à la cérémonie.
questions.explanation: La smala, kif-kif and c'est le souk are informal loans from Arabic, and débarquer and la tribu add to the informal tone. Ma famille au complet assistera à is neutral to formal.

questions.stem: What does « Le train ou le car, c'est kif-kif » mean?
choices: Train or coach, it's chaos.
Train or coach, it's a stroke of luck.
Train or coach, it makes no difference.
Train or coach, it's crazy.
questions.explanation: Kif-kif (informal, from Arabic) means the same, same difference. Chaos would be le souk, luck la baraka, crazy maboul.

questions.stem: In « Range ta chambre, c'est le souk ! », what does le souk mean?
choices: A market
A quarrel
A mess, chaos
A big family
questions.explanation: In its literal, neutral sense le souk is a market in the Arab world; in informal French, c'est le souk means it's chaos, which is the sense here. A big family would be la smala.

questions.stem: Who were the pieds-noirs?
choices: The Europeans of French Algeria, most of whom left for France in 1962
Algerians who served as auxiliaries in the French army
The Amazigh people of Kabylia
French soldiers sent to Morocco in 1912
questions.explanation: Les pieds-noirs were the Europeans of Algeria; most of them, about a million people, left in 1962. The Algerian auxiliaries in the French army were the harkis.

questions.stem: What does l'arabisation refer to in the Maghreb?
choices: The spread of Arabic loanwords in French slang
Making Amazigh an official language
Advertising in Arabic in the streets of Marseille
Policies that replaced French with Arabic in schools and administration after independence
questions.explanation: L'arabisation names the language policies of the independent states, most thorough in Algeria from the 1960s and 1970s: Arabic became the language of schooling and administration in place of French.

questions.stem: In paragraph 2 of the reading, what does Karim say about several of his cousins in Oran in the 1990s?
choices: They had emigrated to Marseille with the rest of the family.
They were unemployed graduates who spent their days leaning against a wall.
They had become teachers of Arabic in Oran.
They spoke pataouète with their Spanish neighbours.
questions.explanation: Karim calls them hittistes: "diplômés, sans travail, ils passaient la journée adossés au mur du quartier", which is exactly the picture the word comes from (hit = wall).

questions.stem: In paragraph 5 of the reading, what does Fatiha mean by saying that dual culture is « avoir deux maisons »?
choices: Owning one house in Oran and one in Marseille
Belonging fully to two places, with their joys and their losses
Being half Algerian and half French
Wanting to go back to Oran one day
questions.explanation: She rejects the idea of being half of each (pas à moitié d'ici et à moitié de là-bas): it is having two homes, sometimes both full, sometimes both empty. The houses are a metaphor, not property.

questions.stem: Which statement about French in the Maghreb, as of November 2026, matches the lesson?
choices: It is an official language in Algeria, Morocco and Tunisia.
It has disappeared from Moroccan and Tunisian universities.
Algeria is a full member of the OIF and promotes French.
It has no official status but is widely used in higher education, business and the press, to a degree that varies by country.
questions.explanation: French is not official in any of the three countries, yet it remains widely used, especially in Morocco and Tunisia's universities and business; Algeria has promoted Arabic and English and is not an OIF member.

questions.stem: Listen to the radio item. According to it, what do some teachers fear?

audio.text: Au Maroc, les panneaux publicitaires parlent de plus en plus darija. Une marque de téléphonie a même écrit son dernier slogan en darija, en lettres latines. Les publicitaires y voient un moyen de parler aux jeunes ; certains enseignants, eux, craignent que l'arabe standard en sorte affaibli.

choices: That standard Arabic will be weakened
That French will disappear from advertising
That young people will stop buying phones
That Amazigh will replace darija on billboards
questions.explanation: The item contrasts the advertisers, who see darija as a way to reach young people, with some teachers, who fear that standard Arabic will come out weakened (en sorte affaibli).

questions.stem: Listen to Karim and Yasmine. What does Yasmine's answer show?

audio.text: Karim : Tu dis « wesh » à ton prof, toi ? Yasmine : Mais non ! Avec mes potes, oui. Avec mon prof, je dis bonjour, comme tout le monde.

choices: She never uses Arabic words in French.
She speaks only darija with her friends.
She adapts her language to the person she is talking to.
She thinks her teacher understands darija.
questions.explanation: Yasmine uses the informal greeting wesh with her friends and bonjour with her teacher: she chooses her words by situation and listener, which is register control, not a lack of it.

questions.stem: Listen to Fatiha. What is she doing?

audio.text: Fatiha : Mon fils, c'est un vrai caïd : il a réussi à faire cuire des pâtes tout seul !

choices: Telling a friend that her son leads a gang
Telling a friend that her son works in a restaurant
Teasing her son by calling him a big shot for a tiny achievement
Praising her son's training as a chef
questions.explanation: Un vrai caïd (a real big shot) for cooking pasta alone is ironic exaggeration: she is teasing him affectionately. Caïd can mean a gang boss, but nothing here suggests that.

questions.stem: Which of these words are informal in the French of France? Select all that apply.
choices: le bled
la médina
maboul
la diaspora
le clebs
l'arabophone
questions.explanation: Le bled, maboul and le clebs are informal loans from Arabic: in formal writing say le village (or le pays d'origine), fou, le chien. La médina, la diaspora and l'arabophone are neutral words.

questions.stem: Match each informal loan to a neutral equivalent.
choices: pareil
la chance
le chien
fou
un peu
le marché
questions.explanation: Kif-kif = pareil; la baraka = la chance; le clebs = le chien; maboul = fou; un chouïa = un peu. Le marché would be the neutral word for le souk in its literal sense, which is not in the list.

questions.stem: Name the language described in each numbered box.

image.alt: A diagram with four numbered boxes around the word Maghreb. Box 1: official texts, school, the mosque, TV news. Box 2: home in Kabylia, the Rif, the Atlas; official in Morocco 2011 and Algeria 2016. Box 3: home, street, songs, advertising. Box 4: universities, business, part of the press. A dashed double arrow marked alternance codique joins boxes 3 and 4.

choices: l'arabe standard
l'amazigh
la darija
le français
le pataouète
le wolof
questions.explanation: Standard Arabic is the official written language (1); Amazigh is spoken in Kabylia, the Rif and the Atlas and became official in 2011 and 2016 (2); darija is the everyday spoken Arabic (3); French is used in universities, business and the press (4). Le pataouète was the French of the pieds-noirs, and Wolof is a language of Senegal.

questions.stem: Reformulation. Rewrite in neutral French, replacing the informal loan: « Il a la baraka. » → « Il a de la ___. »
questions.explanation: La baraka (informal, from Arabic: blessing) corresponds to neutral la chance: il a de la chance.

questions.stem: Reformulation. Rewrite for a formal recipe book, replacing the informal loan: « Ajoutez un chouïa de sel. » → « Ajoutez un ___ de sel. »
questions.explanation: Un chouïa (informal) = un peu; un soupçon de sel (a hint of salt) is also correct and slightly literary.

questions.stem: Put the stages of a borrowing in the order the lesson describes.
choices: A word of another language is used by French speakers
It appears as a xénisme, in italics and explained
It becomes an ordinary borrowing, without italics
Its foreign origin is forgotten
questions.explanation: A borrowing starts as a foreign word, is first treated as a xénisme (la chorba in italics), then becomes ordinary (un chouïa), and may end fully integrated, its origin forgotten (l'algèbre, le sucre).

questions.stem: In Québec, what does « ma blonde » mean?
choices: my girlfriend
my blonde sister
my hairdresser
my best friend
questions.explanation: In informal Québec French, ma blonde is my girlfriend, whatever her hair colour; la petite amie or la copine in France. In France une blonde is a blonde woman (or a lager).

questions.stem: A Montrealer says: « J'ai capoté quand j'ai vu le prix. » What happened?
choices: She overturned her car at the price board.
She fell asleep before seeing the price.
She got a refund on the price.
She freaked out at the price.
questions.explanation: In informal Québec French, capoter is to freak out (with panic or joy). In France capoter means to overturn or to fall through, which does not fit here.

questions.stem: Many Québec speakers pronounce « tu » with a little hiss, like "tsu". What is this feature called?
choices: diphthongisation
affrication
vowel length
a sacre
questions.explanation: Affrication is the hiss added to t and d before i and u (tu → tsu, dire → dzire). Diphthongs and vowel length are other Québec features; a sacre is a swear word.

questions.stem: In « Tu viens-tu ? », what does the second -tu do?
choices: It repeats the subject for emphasis.
It marks a yes/no question.
It means "too", as in me too.
It turns the sentence into an order.
questions.explanation: In spoken Québec French the particle -tu marks a yes/no question, whatever the person (C'est-tu loin ?). It is not a second subject pronoun.

questions.stem: Which of these words is standard Québec French that appears in newspapers, not an informal word?
choices: la piasse
magané
achaler
le traversier
questions.explanation: Le traversier (the ferry) is the ordinary Québec word, used in the press. La piasse (a buck), magané (worn out) and achaler (to bother) are informal.

questions.stem: In France, « Ça va faire jaser » means that people will…
choices: gossip about it
chat about it online
laugh at it
complain to the police
questions.explanation: In France jaser means to gossip; in Québec it means to chat, without malice. The lesson lists it among the words whose meaning changes across the Atlantic.

questions.stem: Which word did the OQLF propose in 1997 for online chat?
choices: le tchat
le divulgâcheur
le clavardage
l'infolettre
questions.explanation: Le clavardage (clavier + bavardage) was proposed by the OQLF in 1997. Le tchat is the common word in France; le divulgâcheur is a spoiler and l'infolettre a newsletter.

questions.stem: What did the Charte de la langue française (loi 101) of 1977 do?
choices: It made Québec officially bilingual in French and English.
It created the Quiet Revolution of the 1960s.
It made French the language of the state, of work and business and, for most children, of school.
It made English the language of work in Montreal.
questions.explanation: Loi 101 (sanctioned on 26 August 1977) made French the language of the state, of work and business and, for most children, of school; it was reformed in 2022. New Brunswick, not Québec, is officially bilingual.

questions.stem: Which statement about joual is accurate?
choices: It is the working-class French of Montreal, brought to the stage by Michel Tremblay's Les Belles-sœurs in 1968.
It is the French of Moncton, mixed with English words.
It is the French of the Cajuns of Louisiana.
It is the French of Québec's laws and official texts.
questions.explanation: Joual (named after the way cheval sounds) is working-class Montreal French; Les Belles-sœurs, first performed in 1968, made it a literary language. Moncton's mixed French is chiac; Louisiana's is Cajun French.

questions.stem: What was the Grand Dérangement?
choices: Québec's Quiet Revolution of the 1960s
The 2022 reform of the Charte de la langue française
The founding of CODOFIL in Louisiana in 1968
The deportation of the Acadians by the British, which began in 1755
questions.explanation: Le Grand Dérangement is the Acadians' name for their deportation, which began in 1755 and lasted for years; some of the deported reached Louisiana, where their descendants are the Cajuns.

questions.stem: What does the lesson say about the sacres?
choices: They are polite religious greetings used in shops.
They are strong swear words built on church words; learners should recognise them, never use them.
They are OQLF terms that replace English words.
They are neutral Acadian words for church objects.
questions.explanation: Sacres such as tabarnak (from tabernacle) are among the strongest words of informal Québec French, a trace of the Church's central place before the 1960s. The lesson explains them so you recognise them, and no question asks you to produce one.

questions.stem: In paragraph 2 of the reading, why was Thomas upset when a colleague told him to stop « niaiser »?
choices: He thought she wanted him to stop chatting with clients.
He thought she was calling him stupid, but she meant he was fooling around.
He thought she was talking about his salary.
He thought she was speaking English to him.
questions.explanation: In France niais means silly, so niaiser sounded like an insult; in Québec niaiser is to fool around or to tease. The hosts reassure him: nobody is cross with him.

questions.stem: In paragraph 3 of the reading, what do the hosts say about prices in Montreal?
choices: Everything is cheaper than in Paris.
Phone plans cost less than in France.
Poutine has become too expensive for students.
Poutine is still affordable, but rent has become expensive.
questions.explanation: La poutine reste abordable ; le loyer, lui, est devenu dispendieux, and a phone plan costs more than in France. Dispendieux is the Québec word for expensive.

questions.stem: A Québec colleague writes in a formal email: « Ce logiciel est dispendieux. » How does the word sound to a reader in France?
choices: Understood, but formal or literary
Incorrect: the word does not exist in France
Informal slang
It means cheap
questions.explanation: Dispendieux is standard in France too, but rarer there and usually described as formal, where cher is usual; in Québec it is the ordinary neutral word. It is not slang, and it means expensive.

questions.stem: Listen to Mélodie and Sami. Why doesn't Sami turn his phone off at once?

audio.text: Mélodie : Sami, tu peux-tu fermer ton cellulaire ? On commence. Sami : Deux minutes, là. C'est ma blonde.

choices: His boss is calling him.
His phone is broken.
His girlfriend is calling him.
He is waiting for a ferry timetable.
questions.explanation: Sami answers "c'est ma blonde": his girlfriend is calling. Fermer ton cellulaire is Québec French for turning off your phone, and là softens his request for two minutes.

questions.stem: Listen to Sami. What is the effect of his remark about clavardage?

audio.text: Sami : Le clavardage ? Franchement, personne ne dit ça. Sauf ma mère. Et l'Office. Et la moitié de mes collègues.

choices: He proves that nobody uses the word.
He criticises his mother for using English.
He undercuts his own claim with a joke: the word is in fact widely used.
