He is reading the OQLF's official definition.
questions.explanation: He begins "personne ne dit ça" and then lists his mother, the Office and half his colleagues: the list contradicts the claim, which is the joke. The word is clearly in use.

questions.stem: Listen to the chronicle. What is the chronicler's attitude?

audio.text: Chroniqueuse : On a longtemps dit que le chiac allait tuer le français à Moncton. Cinquante ans plus tard, les jeunes Acadiens parlent toujours chiac, et toujours français. Les prophètes de malheur devront attendre.

choices: She is ironic about the people who predicted that chiac would kill French.
She agrees that chiac has killed French in Moncton.
She says young Acadians now speak only English.
She gives figures without taking any position.
questions.explanation: Fifty years later, young Acadians still speak chiac and still speak French; "les prophètes de malheur devront attendre" (the prophets of doom will have to wait) mocks the gloomy forecast.

questions.stem: Which of these Québec words are informal? Select all that apply.
choices: le traversier
pantoute
le cégep
magané
achaler
le cellulaire
questions.explanation: Pantoute (not one bit), magané (worn out) and achaler (to bother) are informal. Le traversier (ferry), le cégep (college) and le cellulaire (mobile phone) are the ordinary, neutral Québec words.

questions.stem: Match each Québec word or phrase to its usual equivalent in France.
choices: faire du stop
le portable
en avoir assez
bavarder
le dollar
la petite amie
questions.explanation: Faire du pouce = faire du stop; le cellulaire = le portable; être tanné = en avoir assez; jaser = bavarder; la piasse = le dollar. La petite amie would match la blonde, which is not in the list.

questions.stem: Name the numbered places on this schematic map.

image.alt: A schematic map, not to scale, with a river running from the south-west to a gulf in the north-east. Marker 1 is a dot on the river upstream, marker 2 a dot on the river further downstream, marker 3 a dot south of the gulf, and marker 4 a dot in a separate box at the bottom above the Gulf of Mexico.

choices: Montréal
Québec (the city)
Moncton
Lafayette (Louisiana)
Ottawa
Vancouver
questions.explanation: Montréal is upstream on the St Lawrence (1), Québec City downstream (2), Moncton in New Brunswick, south of the gulf (3), and Lafayette, the main town of Cajun Louisiana, in the separate box (4). Ottawa and Vancouver are not marked.

questions.stem: Reformulation. Rewrite in standard France French: « J'ai pas aimé ça pantoute. » → « Je n'ai pas aimé ça ___. »
questions.explanation: Pas pantoute (Québec, informal) = pas du tout. Careful French also restores the ne: Je n'ai pas aimé ça du tout.

questions.stem: Reformulation. Rewrite in France French: « On a fait du pouce jusqu'à Tadoussac. » → « On a fait du ___ jusqu'à Tadoussac. »
questions.explanation: Faire du pouce (Québec) = faire du stop or, more formally, faire de l'auto-stop. With du the answer is stop (or auto-stop, also written autostop).

questions.stem: Put these events in time order, oldest first.
choices: The deportation of the Acadians begins
CODOFIL is created in Louisiana
New Brunswick's first Official Languages Act
The Charte de la langue française (loi 101)
Québec's law reforming the Charte
questions.explanation: 1755: the Grand Dérangement begins; 1968: CODOFIL; 18 April 1969: New Brunswick's Official Languages Act; 26 August 1977: loi 101; 1 June 2022: the reform (Bill 96).

questions.stem: A Belgian student says: « Je suis en blocus jusqu'au 20 juin. » What is she doing?
choices: Blocking her school as a protest
Going to student parties every night
Taking a holiday abroad
Studying intensively before her exams
questions.explanation: In Belgium le blocus is the period of intensive study before exams. In France the word means a blockade, and a school blocus is a protest, which is exactly the misunderstanding in the lesson's dialogue.

questions.stem: Which word completes a Belgian administrative letter: « Veuillez répondre ___ les trente jours. »?
choices: dedans
endéans
depuis
parmi
questions.explanation: Endéans (Belgium, administrative) means within a period: endéans les trente jours. A French administration would write dans un délai de trente jours. Dedans, depuis and parmi don't give that meaning.

questions.stem: At a supermarket in Lausanne, the cashier asks: « Vous voulez un cornet ? » What is she offering?
choices: An ice-cream cone
A bag for your shopping
A receipt
A loyalty card
questions.explanation: In Switzerland un cornet is a paper or plastic carrier bag. Elsewhere it is a cone (un cornet de glace), which a supermarket cashier is unlikely to offer.

questions.stem: What is la maturité in Switzerland?
choices: The upper secondary school itself
The yearly university tuition fee
A vote of the people on a law
The school-leaving exam that opens the way to university
questions.explanation: La maturité (informally la matu) is the Swiss school-leaving exam, like the French baccalauréat. The school is le gymnase (Vaud) or le collège (Geneva); a popular vote is la votation.

questions.stem: What can 100,000 Swiss citizens do with an initiative populaire?
choices: Put a change to the federal constitution to the vote, if they collect the signatures within eighteen months
Dismiss the federal government before the end of its term
Elect the mayor of their commune directly
Abolish a canton and merge it with another
questions.explanation: A federal popular initiative needs 100,000 signatures collected within eighteen months; the people then vote on the proposed change to the constitution.

questions.stem: Which phrase is correct?
choices: les impôts cantonals
les impôts cantonales
les impôts cantonaux
les impôts cantonaus
questions.explanation: Cantonal follows the -al → -aux pattern in the masculine plural: cantonaux (feminine plural cantonales: les écoles cantonales).

questions.stem: What does it mean to say that French is a pluricentric language?
choices: It is spoken on several continents.
It has one standard, Paris, and many dialects.
It has several standard centres, each with its own norms and institutions.
It has no standard at all.
questions.explanation: Pluricentric means several standard centres (Paris, Brussels, Geneva, Montréal, Dakar), like English or German. Being spoken on several continents is a fact about geography, not about norms.

questions.stem: A Belgian woman in Paris apologises for saying « septante », convinced that her French isn't real French. Linguists call this…
choices: linguistic insecurity
glottophobia
code-switching
an endogenous norm
questions.explanation: Her own doubt about her French is linguistic insecurity. Glottophobia is other people's prejudice against an accent or way of speaking.

questions.stem: A recruiter rejects a candidate because of her strong regional accent. This is…
choices: linguistic insecurity
a regionalism
a pluricentric norm
glottophobia
questions.explanation: Discriminating against someone because of their accent is glottophobia, Philippe Blanchet's term. Linguistic insecurity is the speaker's own doubt.

questions.stem: Which statement about the feminisation of job titles matches the lesson?
choices: France feminised job titles first, and the other countries followed its lead.
Québec (from 1979) and Belgium (a decree of 1993) feminised job titles before the Académie française accepted the principle in 2019.
Switzerland refused to feminise job titles until 2019.
The Dictionnaire des francophones imposed feminine titles in 2021.
questions.explanation: Québec began in 1979, the Fédération Wallonie-Bruxelles adopted a decree on 21 June 1993, Swiss administrations followed gradually, and the Académie française accepted the principle only in 2019. The DDF records usage; it imposes nothing.

questions.stem: In linguistics, what is une variété?
choices: A dialect considered incorrect
Any form of a language shared by a group, with no judgement attached
A regional word to avoid in writing
A list of synonyms for one word
questions.explanation: A variety (Belgian French, Québec French, the French of Dakar) is a neutral term: it says neither dialect nor mistake. A regional word is a regionalism.

questions.stem: In paragraph 1 of the reading, what did it take the columnist twenty years to understand?
choices: That endéans is a mistake to avoid
That her teacher had been right
That Paris French is the only standard
That her grandmother's Belgian French was perfectly correct
questions.explanation: She writes that her grandmother spoke "un français parfaitement correct, simplement belge": the school had taught her to distrust it.

questions.stem: In paragraph 3 of the reading, what role does the columnist give to reference French?
choices: To let documents be read from Brussels to Dakar, without erasing the varieties
To replace every regional word in speech
To impose the Paris accent on the media
To ban words such as cornet from shops
questions.explanation: A shared standard is needed so that a letter, an article or a treaty can be read everywhere, but "une norme commune n'exige pas l'effacement des variétés".

questions.stem: In paragraph 6 of the reading, people with an accent are found « sympathique plutôt que compétent ». What does the columnist imply?
choices: That people with an accent are more competent
That accents are always mocked openly
That a friendly-sounding judgement can hide a professional prejudice
That she prefers friendly colleagues
questions.explanation: Calling someone nice instead of competent sounds kind but denies them seriousness: that is the insidious (sournois) glottophobia she describes.

questions.stem: Listen to Claire and Luc. What does Luc question?

audio.text: Claire : Pour un manuel lu partout, je préfère le français de référence. Luc : D'accord, mais pourquoi faudrait-il qu'il soit parisien ?

choices: Whether a textbook needs a common standard at all
Whether Claire really works in Paris
Whether the common standard has to be Parisian
Whether his pupils should learn French
questions.explanation: Luc concedes the need for a common standard (d'accord) and questions only its centre: pourquoi faudrait-il qu'il soit parisien ?

questions.stem: Listen to Manon. Why do her French friends misunderstand her?

audio.text: Manon : Quand je dis que je suis en blocus, mes amis français croient que je manifeste devant mon université !

choices: In France le blocus suggests a protest, while in Belgium it is the study period before exams.
They have never heard of university exams.
She speaks too fast for them.
They think she is at a student party.
questions.explanation: Le blocus is a Belgian word for the weeks of study before exams; in France the word means a blockade, and students who block a school are said to faire un blocus.

questions.stem: Listen to the chronicler. What is she doing?

audio.text: Chroniqueuse : Bien sûr, il n'existe qu'un seul bon français : celui de Paris. D'ailleurs, à Toulouse, à Marseille et à Lille, tout le monde parle exactement comme à Paris. N'est-ce pas ?

choices: Seriously defending Paris French as the only correct French
Asking people in Toulouse to change their accent
Reporting the results of a survey on accents
Mocking the idea of a single Parisian standard by pointing to variation inside France itself
questions.explanation: Her "bien sûr" and the final "n'est-ce pas ?" after an obviously false claim (everyone in Toulouse, Marseille and Lille speaks like Paris) are irony: France has regional variation too.

questions.stem: Which of these are Belgian words taught in this lesson? Select all that apply.
choices: la poutze
le minerval
la guindaille
le gymnase
le cheni
l'échevin
questions.explanation: Le minerval (tuition fee), la guindaille (student party) and l'échevin (alderman) are Belgian. La poutze, le gymnase (in the school sense) and le cheni are Swiss words from the lesson.

questions.stem: Match each word to its meaning.
choices: a folder
a commuter
clutter, a mess
a big clean
a tuition fee
a door handle
questions.explanation: La farde (Belgium) is a folder; le navetteur (Belgium) a commuter; le cheni (Switzerland) clutter; la poutze (Switzerland) a big clean; le minerval (Belgium) a tuition fee. A door handle would be la clenche.

questions.stem: Name each numbered object with the Belgian or Swiss word taught in the lesson.

image.alt: Four picture cards, numbered: 1, a ring binder with papers; 2, a door handle on a door; 3, a long white endive with a yellow tip; 4, a plastic carrier bag with handles.

choices: la farde
la clenche
le chicon
le cornet
la panosse
le minerval
questions.explanation: 1 la farde (Belgium: folder), 2 la clenche (Belgium and northern France: door handle), 3 le chicon (Belgium and northern France: endive), 4 le cornet (Switzerland: carrier bag). La panosse is a Swiss floorcloth and le minerval a fee, neither of them pictured.

questions.stem: Reformulation. Rewrite for a French administration: « Veuillez répondre endéans les trente jours. » → « Veuillez répondre dans un ___ de trente jours. »
questions.explanation: Dans un délai de trente jours is the France equivalent of the Belgian endéans les trente jours.

questions.stem: Reformulation. Rewrite for a reader in most of France: « Ce soir, on mange des chicons au gratin. » → « Ce soir, on mange des ___ au gratin. »
questions.explanation: Le chicon (Belgium and northern France) is l'endive in most of France: des endives au gratin.

questions.stem: Complete with one word: « Comme l'anglais ou l'allemand, le français est une langue ___ : il a plusieurs centres. »
questions.explanation: A language with several standard centres is une langue pluricentrique.

questions.stem: Where and when was Les Soleils des indépendances first published?
choices: In Paris, in 1968
In Montréal, in 1968
In Abidjan, in 1960
In Lyon, in 1970
questions.explanation: The novel won a prize from the Montréal journal Études françaises and appeared from the Presses de l'Université de Montréal in 1968; Le Seuil published it in Paris in 1970.

questions.stem: Which prizes did Allah n'est pas obligé win in 2000?
choices: The prix Goncourt and the prix Femina
The prix Renaudot and the Goncourt des lycéens
The Grand prix du roman de l'Académie française
The Nobel Prize in Literature
questions.explanation: Allah n'est pas obligé (2000) won the prix Renaudot and the Goncourt des lycéens that year.

questions.stem: In the title Les Soleils des indépendances, what does soleils mean?
choices: The suns painted on the new flags
The new leaders of the independent states
The hot seasons after independence
Days, an era: a Malinké sense of the word
questions.explanation: Kourouma uses soleil in a Malinké sense, a day and by extension an era: the days or the age of independence. That transposed meaning is the clearest example of malinkéisation.

questions.stem: How does Fama make a living in the capital?
choices: By attending funerals, where gifts are handed out to mourners
By working as an actuary for an insurance company
By ruling as chief of Togobala
By working for the single party
questions.explanation: Ruined by independence, Fama lives from the gifts handed out at funerals. Kourouma, not Fama, was an actuary; Lacina, not Fama, had become chief of Togobala.

questions.stem: What does the novel suggest about Fama and Salimata's childlessness?
choices: A rival's fetish is proved to be the cause.
Fama has several children with Mariam.
Salimata is blamed, but the reader may suspect that the infertility is Fama's.
The novel never mentions it.
questions.explanation: Salimata tries every remedy, prayer and charm, yet the novel lets the reader suspect Fama. The childless marriage mirrors the end of the Doumbouya dynasty.

questions.stem: What is malinkéisation?
choices: Translating Malinké epics into classical French
Writing novels entirely in Malinké
Carrying Malinké meanings, images, proverbs and an oral narrator into French
Replacing French with Malinké in schools
questions.explanation: Critics call Kourouma's style the malinkéisation of French: the words are French, but meanings, images, proverbs and the storyteller's voice come from Malinké.

questions.stem: Who narrates Allah n'est pas obligé?
choices: Birahima, a child soldier, who explains difficult words with dictionaries
Fama, the last prince of the Doumbouya
An anonymous griot from Togobala
Kourouma himself, as a reporter
questions.explanation: Birahima, a boy from Côte d'Ivoire who becomes a child soldier in Liberia and Sierra Leone, explains words by looking them up in four dictionaries, among them the Inventaire des particularités lexicales du français en Afrique noire.

questions.stem: How does Kourouma's French differ from that of the Negritude poets (B2 honors)?
choices: They wrote in Malinké; he wrote in French.
He wrote in classical alexandrines; they wrote free prose.
They wrote for French readers only; he wrote only for Malinké readers.
They wrote a classical French; he bent French from within.
questions.explanation: Senghor and Césaire wrote a classical, often solemn French; Kourouma filled French with Malinké ways of saying. Both chose French.

questions.stem: Listen to the critic. What is her attitude?

audio.text: Critique : Kourouma ne casse pas le français : il le remplit d'une autre façon de voir. Ceux qui y voient des fautes n'ont simplement pas écouté.

choices: She regrets the mistakes in Kourouma's French.
She defends Kourouma's style and dismisses those who see mistakes in it.
She prefers the Negritude poets to Kourouma.
She summarises the plot without judging it.
questions.explanation: "Kourouma ne casse pas le français : il le remplit d'une autre façon de voir" defends the style, and "ceux qui y voient des fautes n'ont simplement pas écouté" dismisses the critics.

questions.stem: Put these events of Fama's story in order.
choices: Fama lives by attending funerals in the capital
His cousin Lacina dies and Fama goes to Togobala for the funeral rites
Fama inherits Lacina's young widow, Mariam
Fama is arrested and sent to prison
Fama is freed and tries to cross a closed border
questions.explanation: Funerals in the capital; Lacina's death and the journey to Togobala; Mariam inherited by custom; back in the capital, arrest and prison; release, the journey north and the fatal attempt to cross the border.

questions.stem: Match each word to its meaning.
choices: chieftaincy
single party
colonial settler
charm
line of rulers
child soldier
questions.explanation: La chefferie = chieftaincy; le parti unique = the single party; le colon = the colonial settler; le fétiche = a charm; la dynastie = a line of rulers. A child soldier is un enfant-soldat.

questions.stem: Which of these are features of malinkéisation described in the lesson? Select all that apply.
choices: Proverbs and images used as argument
Strict classical alexandrines
French words used with a Malinké range of meaning
The complete absence of humour
A narrator who talks to the listener
questions.explanation: The lesson names transposed meanings (soleil = day, era), proverbs and images, a storyteller's voice addressing the listener and bold syntax with a crude humour. Kourouma wrote prose, not alexandrines, and his humour is part of the style.

questions.stem: Complete with one French noun: a text that belongs fully to neither of two cultures and draws its force from both shows ___.
questions.explanation: L'hybridité (hybridity) is the critics' word for this quality of Kourouma's writing.

questions.stem: Reformulation. Rewrite in neutral reference French, replacing the Malinké sense of soleils: « Trois soleils plus tard, le village se tut. » → « Trois ___ plus tard, le village se tut. »
questions.explanation: Soleil here means a day: trois jours plus tard. The reference-French version is correct, and loses the voice; that contrast is the lesson's Example 2.

questions.stem: What distinguishes a creole from a pidgin?
choices: A pidgin has native speakers; a creole does not.
A creole is the first language of a community, with a full grammar; a pidgin has no native speakers.
A creole is a dialect of French; a pidgin is a separate language.
A pidgin is always French-based; a creole never is.
questions.explanation: A pidgin is a simplified contact language nobody speaks as a first language; a creole has become a community's first language. Creoles are separate languages, not dialects of their lexifier.

questions.stem: Under Haiti's constitution of 1987, what is the status of Haitian Creole?
choices: The only official language
A national language without official status
A regional language of France
Official, together with French
questions.explanation: Article 5 of the 1987 constitution makes Creole and French the official languages of the Republic. The regional-language status belongs to the creoles of the French overseas departments.

questions.stem: In Haitian Creole, what does « liv yo » mean?
choices: the books
the book
a book
his book
questions.explanation: The determiner follows the noun: liv la = the book, liv yo = the books, while yon liv = a book keeps the indefinite in front.

questions.stem: In « M ap manje », what does ap mark?
choices: The past: I ate
The future: I'm going to eat
An action in progress: I am eating
A question: am I eating?
questions.explanation: Haitian Creole marks tense and aspect with small words before an unchanging verb: ap = in progress, te = anterior (past), pral = going to.

questions.stem: When was slavery abolished for good in the French colonies?
choices: In 1794, by the Convention
In 1802, under Bonaparte
In 1848, by the decree of 27 April
In 1804, with Haiti's independence
questions.explanation: The Revolution abolished slavery in 1794, Bonaparte restored it in 1802, and the decree of 27 April 1848 abolished it for good. Haiti freed itself through its revolution and became independent in 1804.

questions.stem: What is le marronnage?
choices: The escape of enslaved people from the plantation
The chestnut harvest in the Antilles
A creole song form
The 1848 abolition decree
questions.explanation: Le marronnage (marronage) was the escape of enslaved people, for a few days or for good in free communities in the hills and forests: one form of resistance.

questions.stem: Which pairing is right?
choices: Créolité: a process (Glissant); créolisation: an identity (Bernabé, Chamoiseau, Confiant)
Both words were coined by Aimé Césaire in the 1930s
Both words name the plantation economy
Créolité: an identity (Bernabé, Chamoiseau, Confiant, 1989); créolisation: a process (Glissant)
questions.explanation: Éloge de la créolité (1989) defined an identity; Glissant's créolisation names an open, unfinished process of cultures mixing.

questions.stem: A Martinican teacher uses French in class and Creole in the staffroom; her pupils answer in French and joke in Creole. This is a classic case of…
choices: a pidgin
diglossia
a lexifier
marronage
questions.explanation: Two varieties with different roles in one society, French for formal functions and Creole for informal ones, is diglossia.

questions.stem: Listen to the linguist. What point is she making?

audio.text: Linguiste : Dire que le créole est du français mal parlé, c'est comme dire que l'espagnol est du latin mal parlé.

choices: Spanish is a form of badly spoken Latin.
A creole is a language of its own, just as Spanish is a language of its own and not bad Latin.
Creole is badly spoken French.
Latin was originally a creole.
questions.explanation: Her comparison is a reductio: if creole were badly spoken French, Spanish would be badly spoken Latin. Both are new languages that grew out of older ones.

questions.stem: Match each place to the status of its creole (as of November 2026).
choices: official with French
one of three national languages
a regional language of France; only French is official
the most spoken language; English and French dominate official use
the only official language of the state
questions.explanation: Haiti: official with French (1987). Seychelles: Seselwa is a national language with English and French. Martinique: a French department, where Creole is a regional language. Mauritius: Kreol Morisien is the most spoken, but English and French dominate official use. No French-based creole is the sole official language of a state.

questions.stem: Put these events in time order, oldest first.
choices: The French Revolution first abolishes slavery
Bonaparte restores slavery
Haiti becomes independent
Slavery is abolished for good in the French colonies
questions.explanation: 1794: first abolition; 1802: restoration; 1804: Haiti's independence; 1848: final abolition.

questions.stem: Which statements about French-based creoles are true? Select all that apply.
choices: Haitian Creole puts the definite determiner after the noun.
French is their lexifier.
They are dialects of French.
Haitian Creole marks tense with small words before the verb.
Speakers of any two of them understand each other fully.
questions.explanation: French supplies most of their words; Haitian Creole has preverbal markers (te, ap, pral) and a determiner after the noun (liv la). They are separate languages, not dialects, and Haitian, Martinican, Réunion and Mauritian creoles are only partly mutually intelligible.

questions.stem: Complete: the language that gives a creole most of its words is its « langue ___ ».
questions.explanation: La langue lexificatrice (the lexifier) supplies the vocabulary: French for the creoles of this lesson.

questions.stem: Translate into French: Haitian « liv la » = « le ___ ».
questions.explanation: Liv la is le livre: liv comes from livre, and the determiner la follows the noun.

questions.stem: Which statement describes the DALF C2 written paper, as the lesson presents it, and not the C1 synthèse?
choices: You write a committed text in a set genre, using the documents and your own knowledge.
You condense every document faithfully, with no opinion and nothing from outside.
You write 200 to 240 words and may not use je.
You answer comprehension questions on each document, then write a short summary.
questions.explanation: The C2 paper asks for a structured, committed text of at least 700 words in the genre the subject sets (article, éditorial, report, speech), built from the dossier and your apports personnels. Faithful condensation with no opinion and 200–240 words describe the C1 synthèse.

questions.stem: Which document of the lesson's dossier must above all be named for what it is (its genre and interest) before it is used?
choices: The regional daily's report on the repair café
The appliance maker's blog post « Chez nous, une machine ne meurt jamais »
The consumer association's guide to the European directive
The economist's opinion piece « Réparer ne suffira pas »
questions.explanation: The blog belongs to the manufacturer, praises its own products without checkable figures and ends on a trade-in offer: its partialité is built in. It can be used, but as an example of marketing, introduced as such (Un fabricant se félicite, sur son propre blog, de …). The economist also has a position, but she signs an opinion piece that says so openly.

questions.stem: During the survol of a dossier, what do you read?
choices: The first and last paragraphs of every document
Every figure, to copy them into your plan
Only the paratext: titles, chapôs, authors, sources, dates, captions
The longest document, since it carries the most information
questions.explanation: The survol is the fast first pass over the paratext only, to know who speaks, where, when and roughly for what. Looking for figures is the job of the balayage, which comes after you have chosen a subject.

questions.stem: You have chosen your subject and now run your eyes over the five documents looking only for figures on the cost of repair. What is this pass called?
choices: le survol
la contextualisation
la hiérarchisation
le balayage
questions.explanation: Le balayage (scanning) is a search for what one subject needs. The survol reads only the paratext; la contextualisation situates a document (who, where, when, why); la hiérarchisation ranks ideas.

questions.stem: Look at the infographic (document 4). Which obstacle to repair is cited more often in 2026 than in 2020?

image.alt: A bar chart titled "Pourquoi ne faites-vous pas réparer vos appareils ?" comparing 2020 and 2026: trop cher 61 then 54; pas de réparateur près de chez moi 38 then 31; pièce introuvable 24 then 29; appareil trop ancien 30 then 22; ne sait pas à qui s'adresser 27 then 18.

choices: Pièce introuvable
Trop cher
Pas de réparateur près de chez moi
Appareil trop ancien
questions.explanation: Pièce introuvable rises from 24 % to 29 %; every other bar falls. Trop cher is still the most cited obstacle (54 %), but less than in 2020 (61 %).

questions.stem: In paragraph 2 of document 1, what replaced the indice de réparabilité for televisions and washing machines in 2025?
choices: The bonus réparation
The indice de durabilité
A European repair platform
An extra year of legal guarantee
questions.explanation: In 2025 the indice de durabilité replaced the repairability index for televisions, then washing machines; it also rates how sturdy the appliance is. The bonus réparation (since December 2022) is a discount on repairs; the platform and the extra year come from the 2024 EU directive (document 5).

questions.stem: According to document 5, what does a consumer gain by choosing to have a product under guarantee repaired rather than replaced?
choices: A free replacement after the repair
A refund of the repair bonus
An extra year of guarantee
Spare parts at cost price for ten years
questions.explanation: Document 5: « Le consommateur qui choisit de faire réparer un produit sous garantie plutôt que de le faire remplacer bénéficie d'une année de garantie supplémentaire. » This follows the EU directive of 13 June 2024.

questions.stem: What is Claire Vasseur's main argument in document 2?
choices: Repair cafés should replace professional repairers.
Planned obsolescence explains most breakdowns.
The repairability index has solved the problem of waste.
Repair is welcome but not enough: design imposed by law, prices and our own habits matter more.
questions.explanation: She grants the return of repair (On aurait tort de bouder …), then argues that labour is expensive, that the real battle is eco-design imposed by law, and that our own wish for novelty counts as much as planned obsolescence (L'obsolescence programmée a bon dos).

questions.stem: Subject B asks a city councillor to persuade the council to create a municipal repair service. Which problématique fits its genre and addressee best?
choices: Pourquoi une commune devrait-elle prendre en charge ce que le marché ne fait pas ?
L'obsolescence programmée existe-t-elle vraiment ?
Quel téléphone reconditionné choisir en 2026 ?
Les consommateurs européens sont-ils plus vertueux que les autres ?
questions.explanation: Councillors think about what the town should do and what it will cost, so the question must lead to a public decision. The others may be interesting, but they speak to consumers or to theory, not to a council voting on a service.

questions.stem: In the sentence « Un fabricant se félicite, sur son propre blog, de la durabilité de ses machines », what does « sur son propre blog » do?
choices: It shows that the claim has been checked by an independent source.
It signals the source's interest, so the reader weighs the claim accordingly.
It makes the sentence more formal without changing its meaning.
It suggests that the manufacturer is lying.
questions.explanation: Naming the outlet (his own blog) is source criticism in one phrase: the reader knows the praise is self-interested. It doesn't accuse him of lying (the lesson: a partial source is not a lie), and it says nothing about verification.

questions.stem: Which way of introducing a source casts doubt on what follows?
choices: selon l'association
comme le souligne l'économiste
à en croire le fabricant
d'après l'enquête
questions.explanation: À en croire (if we are to believe) distances the writer from the claim. Selon and d'après are neutral attributions; comme le souligne endorses the point (the writer agrees that it is worth stressing).

questions.stem: Which of these is the best apport personnel for subject A (an article on whether consumers really have the choice to repair)?
choices: A list of five famous brands that sell refurbished phones
The infographic's figures, copied in the same order
A general sentence: « Tout le monde sait que réparer, c'est mieux. »
A developed example from your own country: how a repair or guarantee rule works there, and what it changed
questions.explanation: Personal input is what you bring beyond the dossier, and one developed example beats a list of names. Copying the infographic is the dossier, not input, and a general truth adds nothing.

questions.stem: What does the lesson advise writing out in full in your 30-minute plan?
choices: The first and last sentences of the text
Every paragraph, so that you only copy it out afterwards
A summary of each document
The word count of each part
questions.explanation: Plan in words, not sentences, except the opening and closing sentences: a written opening gets you started, a written ending stops you drifting. Writing every paragraph twice would take far longer than the time available.

questions.stem: « Elle a acheté un téléphone reconditionné. » What did she buy?
choices: A new phone whose parts can all be replaced
A used phone checked and restored by a professional before being sold again
A phone she had repaired herself at a repair café
A phone sold without a charger to save resources
questions.explanation: Reconditionné means refurbished: a second-hand device that has been tested, repaired if necessary and resold, usually with a guarantee (Elle a acheté un ordinateur reconditionné, garanti un an).

questions.stem: Listen to the radio chronicle. What is the chronicler's attitude to the repairability index?

audio.text: Chroniqueur: Formidable, cet indice de réparabilité. Mon grille-pain a obtenu sept sur dix. Dommage que la seule pièce qui casse, la résistance, coûte plus cher que le grille-pain lui-même. Mais rassurez-vous : il est très réparable.

choices: Enthusiastic: the index has made his toaster easy to repair.
Neutral: he simply reports the toaster's score.
Ironic: a good score means little if the part that breaks costs more than the appliance.
Angry at repair cafés for not fixing his toaster
questions.explanation: Formidable and rassurez-vous : il est très réparable are ironic: the score looks good, but the one part that breaks costs more than a new toaster, so no one will repair it. This echoes the dossier's point about the price of spare parts.

questions.stem: Listen to two colleagues. What does Marc imply?

audio.text: Léa: Le reconditionné, c'est l'avenir. Plus besoin de produire, on fait durer. — Marc: L'avenir de qui ? Des plateformes qui prennent leur commission sur chaque vente, ou de la planète ?

choices: He agrees that refurbished goods are the future of the planet.
He has never bought a refurbished product.
He thinks production of new goods has already stopped.
He suspects that the refurbished market serves the platforms' profits more than the environment.
questions.explanation: His rhetorical question (L'avenir de qui ?) opposes the platforms that take a commission to the planet: he doubts that the boom is mainly ecological. He doesn't say production has stopped; Léa's plus besoin de produire is the claim he challenges.

questions.stem: Listen to the researcher. What exactly does she claim about planned obsolescence?

audio.text: Chercheuse: Je ne dirais pas que l'obsolescence programmée n'existe pas. Je dis qu'elle explique moins de pannes qu'on ne le croit, et que nos envies de nouveauté expliquent bien davantage de remplacements.

choices: It exists, but it explains fewer breakdowns than people think, and our wish for novelty explains more replacements.
It does not exist; it is a myth.
It explains most breakdowns, and our desires play no part.
It has been abolished by European law.
questions.explanation: Je ne dirais pas que … n'existe pas is a careful double negation: it exists. She then limits its role (moins … qu'on ne le croit) and gives more weight to our desires. At C2 the scope of each qualifier matters.

questions.stem: Complete with the noun taught in the lesson: « D'abord, je ne lis que les titres, les sources, les dates et les légendes : c'est le ___ du dossier. »
questions.explanation: Le survol is the quick first pass over the paratext (from survoler, to skim).

questions.stem: Reformulation. Rewrite the marked part in a careful written register, with the verb écarter in the passé composé: « [J'ai laissé tomber] le document 3, qui ne servait pas mon sujet. » Type only the words that replace the marked part.
questions.explanation: J'ai écarté le document 3, qui ne servait pas mon sujet. Laisser tomber is informal; écarter is the precise verb for setting a document or a hypothesis aside.

questions.stem: Reformulation. Turn the sentence into a noun phrase for a plan heading: « On classe les arguments par ordre d'importance. » → « La ___ des arguments »
questions.explanation: La hiérarchisation des arguments: ranking them by importance (from hiérarchiser). Note the aspirated h: la hiérarchisation, not l'hiérarchisation.

questions.stem: Put the steps of the lesson's method for the written paper in order.
choices: Read the two subjects
Survol of the paratext
Choose one subject
Balayage and repérage
Set a problématique and a line
Write in the genre
Reread and count
questions.explanation: Subjects first (so that you read the dossier with them in mind), then the survol, the choice, the targeted reading, the problématique and line, the writing and the final reread and count, as in the lesson's flowchart.

questions.stem: Which of these belong to the paratext you read during a survol? Select all that apply.
choices: The titles and chapôs
The authors, outlets and dates
The légende of an infographic
The middle paragraphs of each document
Every figure in the body of the texts
questions.explanation: The paratext is everything around the text proper: titles, chapôs, sources, dates, captions. The body paragraphs and their figures come later, in the balayage.

questions.stem: Match each word to what it means when you work on a dossier.
choices: a quick first look at the paratext
a search through the texts for what one subject needs
marking and identifying passages with a pencil
saying who wrote a document, where, when and why
ranking ideas by importance
questions.explanation: The three passes are survol, balayage and repérage; contextualisation situates a document. Ranking ideas is la hiérarchisation.

questions.stem: Name the numbered parts of the infographic, as you would note them during a survol.

image.alt: The infographic of document 4 with four numbered markers: beside the large heading at the top, beside the italic line under it, beside the two shaded squares with years, and beside the italic line at the bottom naming the association.

choices: le titre
le sous-titre
la légende
la source
le chapô
l'intertitre
questions.explanation: The heading is the title; the italic line under it (what the figures measure) is the subtitle; the squares that explain the two shades are the légende (key); the bottom line gives the source and the size of the survey. Chapô and intertitre belong to press articles.

questions.stem: Who speaks in an éditorial?
choices: The newspaper itself, as nous, often through its editor
An outside expert invited by the paper
A reporter describing what he saw on the spot
Readers answering a previous article
questions.explanation: The éditorial is the paper's own position (its ligne éditoriale), often unsigned or signed by the editor, in the nous of the paper. An outside expert writes a tribune; a reporter writes a reportage; readers use the courrier des lecteurs or the droit de réponse.

questions.stem: What is the chapô of a press article?
choices: The short line above the headline giving the topic
The bold paragraph under the headline that sums up the article
A boxed text with key figures beside the article
The last sentence, which closes the article
questions.explanation: The chapô (press spelling of le chapeau) sums up the article in two or three bold sentences. The line above the headline is the surtitre, the box is the encadré, and the last sentence is the chute.

questions.stem: Which attaque opens with a marronnier?
choices: Quatre-vingt-dix mille : c'est le nombre de voitures qui entrent chaque matin dans Valmont.
À 6 heures, Nadia Ferhat attend un bus qui ne passera qu'à 6 h 30.
Comme chaque été, les routes des vacances sont saturées et les automobilistes s'impatientent.
« Un coup de poignard » : c'est ainsi que les commerçants qualifient le projet.
questions.explanation: A marronnier is a story that comes back every year at the same time; an attaque that could run every summer in every paper loses the reader. The others open on a figure, a scene or a striking quotation, which are the lesson's good attaques.

questions.stem: In document 2 of the dossier, what does Nadia Ferhat ask for?
choices: The abandonment of the congestion charge
Free parking for health workers in the centre
A lower charge for people who live far away
A way of getting to work other than by car, before the charge
questions.explanation: Document 2: « Elle ne demande pas l'abandon du péage : Qu'on me donne d'abord un moyen d'y aller autrement. » Her problem is that no bus runs before her 6 a.m. shift.

questions.stem: Which of these is NOT one of the conditions Paul Kessler sets in document 3?
choices: Exempting every resident of the conurbation
Providing transport before introducing the charge
Earmarking the revenue, visibly, for mobility
Measuring traffic, air quality and trade before and after, and publishing the figures
questions.explanation: Kessler asks for transport first, earmarked revenue, acceptance built over time and published measurements. Exemptions appear in document 1 (reduced rate for residents, exemptions for disabled people and emergency vehicles), not as his condition.

questions.stem: In paragraph 3 of the model éditorial: « Il faudrait donc, pour sauver les boutiques, conserver les embouteillages qui en éloignent les clients. » What is the device?
choices: A rhetorical question addressed to the mayor
Irony that draws an absurd consequence from the opponents' argument
A direct quotation from the shopkeepers' association
A concession that adopts the shopkeepers' view
questions.explanation: Il faudrait donc pretends to follow the shopkeepers' logic to its end, which turns out absurd (keeping the traffic jams that drive customers away). The irony targets the argument, not the people, as the lesson requires; the real concession comes next (L'inquiétude est légitime).

questions.stem: Why does the model éditorial write « À en croire l'association des commerçants, le péage serait un coup de poignard » rather than « Selon l'association … »?
choices: Because selon cannot be followed by an organisation
Because à en croire is more neutral than selon
Because à en croire, with the conditional, distances the paper from the claim it is about to refute
Because the association asked to be quoted that way
questions.explanation: À en croire (if we are to believe) and the conditional of hearsay (serait) mark the claim as the association's, not the paper's, preparing the refutation. Selon is a neutral attribution and works with any source.

questions.stem: Which headline is in the nominal style?
choices: La voiture paiera son entrée
Faut-il faire payer la ville ?
Les commerçants redoutent le péage
Péage urbain : le grand saut de Valmont
questions.explanation: A nominal headline has no conjugated verb: Péage urbain : le grand saut de Valmont. The others have a verb (paiera, faut-il, redoutent).

questions.stem: Which sentence belongs in an article d'information rather than in an éditorial?
choices: Le conseil métropolitain votera en juin un projet de péage urbain de quatre euros par jour.
Nous croyons ce péage juste, mais prématuré.
Qui osera dire à cette aide-soignante qu'elle n'a qu'à changer ses habitudes ?
Que les élus choisissent d'oser, mais d'oser dans l'ordre.
questions.explanation: An information article reports facts with their source and no stance. The other three carry the paper's position: a nous that judges, a rhetorical question and a wish in the subjunctive.

questions.stem: « La rédaction a bouclé le numéro à minuit. » What happened at midnight?
choices: The newsroom locked its doors for the night.
The issue was closed and sent to print.
The editors cancelled the issue.
The journalists finished a long investigation.
questions.explanation: Boucler un numéro is to put an issue to bed: close it for printing. The moment is le bouclage. Boucler also means to buckle or to lock, but in a newsroom the press sense is meant.

questions.stem: In French traffic rules, what is a zone de rencontre?
choices: A car park at the edge of town linked to a tram line
A street closed to cars at school times
An area where pedestrians have priority and vehicles are limited to 20 km/h
A zone where only low-emission vehicles may enter
questions.explanation: The zone de rencontre (in the Code de la route since 2008) is shared by everyone, with priority to pedestrians and vehicles at 20 km/h. A street closed at school times is a rue scolaire; the low-emission zone is the ZFE (B2).

questions.stem: According to the lesson, which statement about congestion charges is true?
choices: Paris introduced a congestion charge in 2010.
French law has never allowed a city to try a congestion charge.
Stockholm abandoned its charge after a trial in 2006.
London introduced one in 2003, and no French city has one so far.
questions.explanation: London's charge dates from 2003; Stockholm made its charge permanent in 2007 after a 2006 trial; a 2010 French law allowed large conurbations to experiment, and none did before it was repealed at the end of 2021.

questions.stem: Which word for a newspaper is dismissive?
choices: la feuille de chou
le quotidien
l'hebdomadaire
le journal
questions.explanation: La feuille de chou (a local rag) is informal and dismissive. Le quotidien (a daily), l'hebdomadaire (a weekly) and le journal are neutral. Le canard is informal too, but often affectionate rather than dismissive.

questions.stem: What does the model éditorial ask the councillors to do?
choices: Reject the congestion charge outright
Vote for the principle of the charge but not its timetable, and set three conditions
Hold a referendum before any vote
Introduce the charge immediately and add trams later
questions.explanation: Paragraph 5: « Nous demandons donc aux élus de voter le principe, mais pas le calendrier », followed by three conditions (transport first, earmarked revenue, a social rate). A wider consultation is suggested later (pourquoi pas), not made a precondition.

questions.stem: Listen to the billet d'humeur. What is the writer's attitude?

audio.text: Chroniqueuse: Bonne nouvelle pour les automobilistes pressés : à partir de lundi, il sera interdit de se garer en double file devant l'école. Il faudra donc se garer en triple file, un peu plus loin. Le progrès est en marche.

choices: She welcomes the new rule as a real progress.
She explains the new rule neutrally for drivers.
She mocks drivers' habits, implying the rule will simply be dodged.
She criticises the school for asking for the rule.
questions.explanation: Bonne nouvelle, se garer en triple file and Le progrès est en marche are ironic: the writer pretends to celebrate while implying that drivers will just park badly elsewhere. That personal, ironic tone is typical of the billet d'humeur.

questions.stem: Listen to the editor and the journalist. What is the editor's criticism?

audio.text: Rédactrice: Ton titre, « Le vélo-cargo, poids lourd de la livraison », j'adore. — Journaliste: Merci ! — Rédactrice: Seulement, ton article dit qu'ils livrent trois pour cent des colis. Le lecteur va se sentir floué.

choices: The pun is too hard to understand.
The article is too long for the page.
The headline should be nominal.
The headline promises more than the article shows, so readers will feel misled.
questions.explanation: She likes the pun, but poids lourd (heavyweight) suggests cargo bikes carry a large share of deliveries, while the article says three per cent. Floué means cheated: a headline must keep its promise.

questions.stem: Listen to the head of the news desk. What will happen if the article is late?

audio.text: Chef d'édition: Le bouclage est à vingt-deux heures. Si ton papier n'est pas là à vingt et une heures trente, il passe en filet, en page huit.

choices: It will be cut to a few lines on page eight.
It will be published the next day in full.
It will move to the front page.
It will be given to a freelance journalist.
questions.explanation: Passer en filet: to be reduced to a short item of a few lines. Le papier is press jargon for an article, and le bouclage is the moment the issue closes.

questions.stem: Type the press word for the bold paragraph under a headline that sums up the article (with its article).
questions.explanation: Le chapô, the press spelling of le chapeau; both spellings are found, and journalists usually write chapô.

questions.stem: Reformulation. Rewrite so that the éditorial distances itself from the mayor's claim, with the phrase taught for this: « Selon le maire, tout est réglé. » → « ___ le maire, tout serait réglé. »
questions.explanation: À en croire le maire, tout serait réglé: à en croire and the conditional of hearsay mark the claim as the mayor's and invite doubt. Selon is neutral.

questions.stem: Reformulation. Turn this verbal headline into a nominal one: « La ville supprime le stationnement payant le dimanche » → « ___ du stationnement payant le dimanche »
questions.explanation: Suppression du stationnement payant le dimanche (or Fin du …, Abandon du …): the verb supprimer becomes a noun and the headline loses its conjugated verb, as French headlines often do.

questions.stem: Match each press genre to who speaks and how.
choices: the paper itself, as nous, with a clear stance
one writer, short, personal and often ironic
a journalist who went there, with scenes and voices
the paper, anonymously, a few lines of facts
outside authors, often a collective, demanding a change
questions.explanation: The distractor describes the tribune (honors lesson 20h1), which the newspaper publishes without endorsing.

questions.stem: Which of these belong to the titraille of an article? Select all that apply.
choices: le surtitre
le chapô
l'intertitre
l'encadré
la chute
questions.explanation: The titraille is the set of titles: surtitre, titre, sous-titre, chapô, intertitres. The encadré is a box beside the article, and the chute is the article's last sentence.

questions.stem: Name the numbered parts of this newspaper page.

image.alt: A mock newspaper page with five numbered markers: on the small word above the headline, on the large headline, on the bold paragraph under it, on a short bold line inside the left column, and on the shaded box of figures on the right.

choices: le surtitre
le titre
le chapô
l'intertitre
l'encadré
le bandeau
le filet
questions.explanation: Surtitre (MOBILITÉ) above the titre; the chapô under it; an intertitre (Une ville saturée) breaking the column; the encadré (Repères) with the key figures. A bandeau runs across the top of a page, and a filet is a short item of a few lines.

questions.stem: Who is the commanditaire of a report?
choices: The person or body that ordered the report and must decide
The author of the report
Each person interviewed for the report
The journalist who will write about the report
questions.explanation: The commanditaire (a mayor, a board, a president) orders the report through a lettre de mission; the report is addressed to it. The author is the rapporteur or chargé(e) de mission; the people interviewed are parties prenantes.

questions.stem: What does a lettre de mission usually fix?
choices: The recommendations the report must make
The task, its scope (périmètre) and the deadline
The budget the town will spend
The names of the people to interview
questions.explanation: The terms of reference set the task, the périmètre (what the study covers) and when the report is due. The recommendations are the report's own work.

questions.stem: Which sentence belongs in the constat of a report?
choices: Il conviendrait d'équiper les salles de stores extérieurs.
Cette situation est indigne d'une commune moderne.
Neuf salles sur trente-deux ont dépassé 33 °C en fin d'après-midi.
Nous recommandons d'adopter ce plan au prochain conseil.
questions.explanation: The constat states facts and figures without judgement. Il conviendrait de … and Nous recommandons … are préconisations or the conclusion; Cette situation est indigne … is a judgement worthy of an éditorial.

questions.stem: What does each préconisation of a C2 report give, as the lesson teaches?
choices: A rhetorical question that engages the reader
A quotation from one of the documents
The names of the people who suggested it
What to do, its cost, its feasibility and its deadline
questions.explanation: A préconisation is numbered and ranked, and says what to do, at what cost (chiffrage), how feasibly (faisabilité) and by when (échéance).

questions.stem: Which sentence suits a report?
choices: Les relevés font apparaître des températures supérieures à 33 °C dans neuf salles.
Franchement, à 33 degrés, qui pourrait apprendre quoi que ce soit ?
Laisser des enfants étudier à 33 degrés est indigne d'une ville moderne.
Imaginez Léa, huit ans, rouge et épuisée devant son cahier.
questions.explanation: The report is impersonal, measured and precise. A rhetorical question, an indignant judgement and an imagined scene belong to the éditorial or the speech.

questions.stem: In careful written French, which mood follows « il ressort de l'enquête que » when it introduces a finding?
choices: The subjunctive
The indicative
The infinitive
The conditional, always
questions.explanation: Il ressort de … que states a finding, so the indicative follows: Il ressort de l'enquête que la moitié des classes dépassent 30 °C. A conditional is possible when the finding itself is hypothetical, which is why always is wrong.

questions.stem: « Eu égard aux contraintes budgétaires, nous proposons un plan en trois temps. » What does eu égard à mean here?
choices: Despite
Instead of
In view of
As a result of an error in
questions.explanation: Eu égard à (formal) means in view of, considering: the budget is the reason for a three-step plan. Eu is invariable in this phrase.

questions.stem: The report says: « Un parangonnage avec trois communes a guidé nos choix. » What did the authors do?
choices: They held a vote in three towns.
They interviewed three mayors in a semi-structured way.
They copied the reports of three towns.
They compared the town's situation and solutions with those of three other towns.
questions.explanation: Le parangonnage is the recommended French term for benchmarking: comparing with others to learn from them.

questions.stem: According to document 1, which classrooms suffered most from the heat?
choices: South-facing rooms under uninsulated roofs from the 1970s
Rooms on the ground floor next to the playground
The newest rooms, built with large windows
Rooms in the Pasteur school
questions.explanation: Nine rooms went above 33 °C; seven of them face south under uninsulated 1970s roofs, and Jules-Ferry was the worst school. Pasteur is mentioned for the only shaded spot in a yard.

questions.stem: Which lesson from other towns does document 3 stress?
choices: Green playgrounds cool classrooms as well as air conditioning would.
A greener playground relieves the heat outside but does not cool badly insulated classrooms.
Users should be consulted only after the work is done.
Trees need no upkeep once planted.
questions.explanation: « La cour soulage dehors ; c'est le bâti qui protège dedans. » Document 3 also advises involving pupils and teachers from the start and planning summer upkeep.

questions.stem: Why are the model report's recommendations ordered from blinds (4.1) to playgrounds (4.2) to roofs (4.3)?
choices: Because roofs matter least
Because the documents mention them in that order
Cheap and quick measures first, structural ones last, each with its own deadline
Because the commissioning body asked for that order
questions.explanation: The ranking follows cost and speed: blinds and a protocol by summer 2027, playgrounds over 2027–2029, roof renovation (the flagship, most expensive) over 2028–2032. Ranking is where a report shows its commitment.

questions.stem: In the model report, which measure is named the mesure phare (flagship measure)?
choices: The external blinds
The heatwave protocol
The greening of the four playgrounds
The energy renovation of the roofs, starting with Jules-Ferry
questions.explanation: « La rénovation thermique des toitures, à commencer par celle de Jules-Ferry, constitue la mesure phare du plan. » It is the most structural and the most expensive.

questions.stem: Which device has no place in a report?
choices: A rhetorical question
The conditional of recommendation
Numbered headings
Impersonal constructions
questions.explanation: Rhetorical questions, irony and emotional appeals belong to the éditorial or the speech. The conditional (il conviendrait de), numbered headings and impersonal forms (il a été procédé à) are the report's tools.

questions.stem: Which indicators does the model report propose to measure its plan's effect?
choices: The number of complaints from parents and the cost per pupil
The number of days above 30 °C in each room and the share of shaded surface in the playgrounds
The pupils' exam results and the number of trees bought
The heating bill and the number of meetings held
questions.explanation: The conclusion names two indicators: days above 30 °C per room, measured each summer, and the share of shaded surface. Both measure the problem itself, not the effort spent.

questions.stem: Listen to a councillor and the report's author. What does the author imply?

audio.text: Élue: Votre rapport recommande d'abord des stores. Pourquoi pas des arbres ? — Rapporteuse: Les arbres viendront. Mais un arbre planté cet hiver donnera de l'ombre dans dix ans, et les enfants auront chaud en juin prochain.

choices: Trees are useless in school playgrounds.
Blinds are cheaper than trees in every case.
Measures that act quickly must come first, while slower ones are prepared.
The councillor has not read the report.
questions.explanation: Les arbres viendront grants their place; the contrast between dix ans and juin prochain justifies the ranking: quick measures first. She doesn't call trees useless.

questions.stem: Listen to the radio report. What does the opposition criticise?

audio.text: Journaliste: Le rapport, très attendu, préconise de végétaliser les cours et de rénover les toitures. Mais sans chiffrage ni calendrier, ces préconisations risquent de rester des vœux pieux, a regretté l'opposition.

choices: The report recommends too many trees.
The report was published too late.
The report ignores the playgrounds.
The recommendations have no costing and no timetable, so they may never be carried out.
questions.explanation: Sans chiffrage ni calendrier … des vœux pieux (wishful thinking): recommendations without cost and deadline are not actionable, which is exactly what the lesson warns against.

questions.stem: Listen to the head teacher. What is her attitude?

audio.text: Directrice: Des stores ? Nous les avons demandés il y a trois ans. J'imagine que notre dossier fait la sieste quelque part, bien au frais, lui.

choices: Ironic about the administration's slowness
Grateful that blinds are finally planned
Indifferent to the heat in her school
Confused about who should install the blinds
questions.explanation: The file taking a nap bien au frais (nicely in the cool), while the classes overheat, is ironic: three years without an answer. Compare document 2, where she says she asked for blinds three years ago.

questions.stem: Type the recommended French term for benchmarking, with its article.
questions.explanation: Le parangonnage, from parangon (a model). Many reports still say le benchmark, but the French term is the one to use in formal writing.

questions.stem: Reformulation. Rewrite in the register of a report, with the conditional of convenir: « On pense qu'il faudrait planter des arbres. » → « Il ___ de planter des arbres. »
questions.explanation: Il conviendrait de planter des arbres: impersonal, conditional, measured; the writer disappears behind the recommendation.

questions.stem: Reformulation. Replace « À cause de son coût » with a formal phrase meaning in view of: « ___ son coût, la mesure ne peut être que progressive. »
questions.explanation: Eu égard à son coût (the lesson's formula), or compte tenu de / au regard de / vu / au vu de / étant donné / en raison de son coût, all correct. À cause de is neutral and slightly negative; the report prefers a phrase that presents the cost as a fact to take into account.

questions.stem: Put the sections of a report in order.
choices: Introduction
Constat
Analyse
Préconisations
Conclusion
Annexes
questions.explanation: Object and method first, then the facts, their causes, the ranked recommendations, the conclusion that proposes a decision, and the annexes, listed at the end.

questions.stem: Which of these belong in the introduction of a report? Select all that apply.
choices: The scope of the study (le périmètre)
The method (visits, interviews, benchmarking)
The ranked recommendations with their costs
A reminder of the terms of reference (la lettre de mission)
The detailed temperature readings
questions.explanation: The introduction gives the object, the lettre de mission, the périmètre and the method in one paragraph. The readings go in the constat, the recommendations in their own section.

questions.stem: Name the numbered sections of this report outline.

image.alt: A report outline as a column of seven blocks. The first is labelled En-tête and the sixth 5. Conclusion; five numbered markers sit beside the others, whose contents read: objet, lettre de mission, périmètre, méthode; ce que l'on observe : chiffres, faits; causes, enjeux, publics vulnérables; mesures classées : coût, faisabilité, échéance; tableaux, entretiens, sources.

choices: Introduction
Constat
Analyse
Préconisations
Annexes
Sommaire
Résumé
questions.explanation: Object and method → introduction; facts and figures → constat; causes and vulnerabilities → analyse; ranked, costed measures → préconisations; tables and interviews → annexes.

questions.stem: Match each word to its meaning in a report.
choices: the costing of a measure
the date by which it must be done
whether it can realistically be done
what the study covers and leaves out
everyone with a stake in the decision
questions.explanation: The distractor defines les parties prenantes (stakeholders).

questions.stem: What is the captatio benevolentiae?
choices: Winning the audience's goodwill at the start of a speech
The summing-up at the end of a speech
The answer to the main objection
The list of people to thank
questions.explanation: Latin for capturing goodwill: in the exorde, a modest word, a shared memory or a thanks makes the audience well disposed. The summing-up is the récapitulation, in the péroraison; the answer to objections is the réfutation.

questions.stem: Which sentence works mainly through ethos?
choices: Trente-deux kilomètres, trente-huit minutes jusqu'à Valbrune.
Je suis né dans cette vallée, et j'en suis parti à vingt ans, comme tant d'autres.
Pensez à Léa, qui rêve d'être médecin.
Le chantier a coûté 410 millions d'euros.
questions.explanation: Ethos is the speaker's credibility: being from the valley and having left it gives him the right to speak of it. Figures are logos; Léa's dream appeals to feelings (pathos).

questions.stem: Which sentence works mainly through logos?
choices: Vous, Marcel, qui avez éteint la dernière lampe …
Si ces rails pouvaient parler, ils nous diraient qu'ils ont attendu.
Trente-deux kilomètres, quatorze allers-retours par jour, Valbrune à trente-huit minutes.
Je vous avoue que j'ai écrit et réécrit ce discours.
questions.explanation: Logos appeals to reason with facts and figures. The others are an apostrophe and a prosopopée (pathos) and a modest confession (ethos).

questions.stem: Which sentence is a prosopopée?
choices: Cette ligne, ce sont des lycéens ; cette ligne, ce sont des malades.
Et vous, Marcel, permettez-moi de vous parler directement.
Un espoir, une promesse, une ligne.
Si ces rails pouvaient parler, ils nous diraient que l'attente est finie.
questions.explanation: A prosopopée makes the absent, the dead or a thing speak: here the rails. Cette ligne … ce sont is an anaphora; Et vous, Marcel is an apostrophe; un espoir, une promesse, une ligne is a gradation.

questions.stem: Which sentence contains an apostrophe (the figure)?
choices: Vous, les ouvriers du chantier, vous avez posé ces rails.
Le train nous désenclave ; il ne nous dispense pas d'agir.
Hier l'attente, aujourd'hui la fête, demain le travail.
Combien nous ont coûté cinquante-huit ans d'isolement ?
questions.explanation: The apostrophe turns to address someone directly (Vous, les ouvriers …). The others are an antithesis, a ternary récapitulation and a rhetorical question.

questions.stem: « Ce pont, nous l'avons attendu. Ce pont, nous l'avons financé. Ce pont, nous allons le faire vivre. » Which figure carries this passage?
choices: The prosopopée
The anaphora (figure)
The apostrophe
The hypallage
questions.explanation: The same words open each sentence (Ce pont, nous …): an anaphora, the figure of repetition, which gives the ear a beat and builds towards the last step.

questions.stem: Which opening respects the usual order of precedence at a French inauguration?
choices: Mesdames et Messieurs, Madame la Préfète, Mesdames et Messieurs les élus, Monsieur le Président du conseil régional,
Salut à tous, et merci d'être venus,
Madame la Préfète, Monsieur le Président du conseil régional, Mesdames et Messieurs les élus, Mesdames et Messieurs,
Mesdames et Messieurs les élus, Mesdames et Messieurs, Madame la Préfète,
questions.explanation: The address goes from the highest rank down: the préfète (the State's representative), the president of the regional council, the elected officials, then everyone. Salut à tous is familiar and out of register.

questions.stem: Who would normally open a speech with « Mes chers compatriotes » ?
choices: A mayor at a village fête
A bride's father at a wedding
A teacher at a prize-giving
A head of state addressing the nation
questions.explanation: Mes chers compatriotes is the formula of a head of state speaking to the whole country. A mayor would say Mes chers concitoyens.

questions.stem: In paragraph 5 of the model speech, how does the mayor deal with the objection about cost?
choices: He grants it, then asks what fifty-eight years of isolation have cost.
He denies that the line was expensive.
He says the European Union paid for everything.
He refuses to discuss money on a day of celebration.
questions.explanation: « On a dit que ce train coûtait cher, et c'est vrai … Mais je pose une question simple : combien nous ont coûté cinquante-huit ans d'isolement ? » A concession followed by rhetorical questions that turn the objection around.

questions.stem: « Le train nous désenclave ; il ne nous dispense pas d'agir. » What does this sentence do in the speech?
choices: It rejects the critics of document 3 entirely.
It grants the critics a point and turns it into a commitment of the speaker.
It thanks the State for financing the line.
It announces the end of the speech.
questions.explanation: Document 3 said a line is not a development plan. The mayor agrees (nos critiques ont raison sur ce point) and makes it a duty for the elected officials: concession becomes commitment.

questions.stem: At the Académie française, what is the new member's first speech, which praises the member whose seat he or she takes?
choices: l'éloge funèbre
le panégyrique
le discours de réception
le toast
questions.explanation: Le discours de réception. An éloge funèbre is given at a funeral; a panégyrique is lavish praise (often ironic today); a toast is short and given glass in hand.

questions.stem: Which sentence would be out of register in an inauguration speech?
choices: C'est avec une émotion particulière que je prends la parole.
Permettez-moi de saluer les ouvriers du chantier.
Votre présence nous honore.
Bon, ben, on est super contents, hein, c'est cool.
questions.explanation: Bon, ben, super, hein and c'est cool are familiar spoken French. The other three are the formal formulas of opening, greeting and honour the lesson teaches.

questions.stem: Which objection is NOT raised in document 3 of the dossier?
choices: The trains will be too slow to compete with the road.
The line cost a great deal for fourteen return trips a day.
The route cut several farms in two.
The train could make it easier for people to leave the valley.
questions.explanation: Document 3 raises the cost, an unverified traffic forecast, the farms cut in two, the viaduct's impact on the gorges and the risk of departure or of a dormitory valley. Speed is never criticised: 38 minutes to Valbrune is presented as a gain.

questions.stem: What does the péroraison of a speech do?
choices: It greets the audience in order of precedence.
It sums up, moves the audience and ends with a call.
It tells the story of how the project began.
It answers the objections one by one.
questions.explanation: The péroraison gathers (récapitulation), lifts (envolée) and calls to act, remember or celebrate. Greeting is the exorde, the story the narration, the objections the réfutation.

questions.stem: Listen to the extract of a speech. What effect does its construction aim at?

audio.text: Oratrice: Cette école, nous l'avons défendue. Cette école, nous l'avons reconstruite. Cette école, nous allons maintenant la remplir.

choices: It lists the school's defects with irony.
It addresses the school as if it were a person.
It repeats the same opening to hammer the idea and rise towards the next task.
It hides the speaker behind an impersonal tone.
questions.explanation: The anaphora (Cette école, nous …) gives a beat the ear can follow and leads from past efforts to the future task. The speaker talks about the school, not to it, so it is not an apostrophe.

questions.stem: Listen to two guests after a speech. What is Sonia's attitude?

audio.text: Paul: Beau discours, tu ne trouves pas ? — Sonia: Magnifique. Vingt minutes, et pas un mot pour les agriculteurs expropriés.

choices: She sincerely admires the speech.
She found the speech too short.
She thinks the farmers spoke too much.
She praises it ironically and criticises what it left out.
questions.explanation: Magnifique followed by et pas un mot pour … is ironic: the speech forgot the farmers whose land was taken. A réfutation that ignores an objection costs the speaker his ethos.

questions.stem: Listen to the opening of a speech. Which appeal does the speaker use first?

audio.text: Oratrice: Je ne suis ni ingénieure ni cheminote. Je suis la fille d'un garde-barrière de cette ligne, et c'est à ce titre que je vous parle.

choices: Ethos: she builds her right to speak from her family's link to the line.
Logos: she gives figures about the line.
Prosopopée: she makes her father speak.
Réfutation: she answers an objection.
questions.explanation: C'est à ce titre que je vous parle: she presents her credentials, modest and personal. That is ethos, often combined with the captatio benevolentiae in the exorde.

questions.stem: Complete the ritual phrase: « La ministre va ___ le ruban à midi. »
questions.explanation: Couper le ruban: to cut the ribbon, the gesture that opens a new building or line.

questions.stem: Reformulation. Rewrite in the formal register of a speech: « Merci beaucoup aux ouvriers. » → « Je veux dire ma ___ aux ouvriers. »
questions.explanation: Je veux dire ma gratitude (or ma reconnaissance) aux ouvriers: a noun of thanks after a verb of saying is the formal frame. Both nouns are correct here.

questions.stem: Reformulation. Turn the statement into an apostrophe to the workers by adding one word at the start: « Les ouvriers ont posé ces rails. » → « ___, les ouvriers, vous avez posé ces rails. »
questions.explanation: Vous, les ouvriers, vous avez posé ces rails: the speaker turns from the audience to address the workers directly, which is the apostrophe.

questions.stem: Match each figure to an example from the lesson.
choices: Cette ligne, ce sont … Cette ligne, c'est …
Et vous, Marcel, permettez-moi de vous parler directement.
Si ces rails pouvaient parler, ils nous diraient …
un espoir, une promesse, une ligne
Votre présence nous honore.
questions.explanation: Votre présence nous honore is a formula of honour, not a figure.

questions.stem: Which are good advice for writing a speech for the ear? Select all that apply.
choices: Write short sentences.
Signpost where you are going (J'en viens à …).
Repeat the key word.
Put details in parentheses.
Replace names with celui-ci and celle-ci to avoid repetition.
questions.explanation: A listener can't go back: short sentences, signposts and repetition help. Parentheses and pronouns like celui-ci, fine on the page, lose the listener; repeat the name instead.

questions.stem: Name the numbered parts of a classical speech.

image.alt: Five boxes in a row on a timeline, each with a numbered marker and a description: saluer, gagner l'auditoire (with captatio benevolentiae written under it); ce qui s'est passé; les arguments pour; les objections, réfutées; résumer, émouvoir, appeler (with récapitulation et envolée under it).

choices: exorde
narration
confirmation
réfutation
péroraison
digression
questions.explanation: Exorde (greet and win the audience), narration (the facts), confirmation (arguments for), réfutation (objections answered), péroraison (sum up, move, call).

questions.stem: What distinguishes a tribune from an éditorial?
choices: A tribune is written by outside authors, often a collective; an éditorial is the paper's own voice.
A tribune is always shorter than an éditorial.
A tribune never takes a position.
An éditorial is always signed by many people.
questions.explanation: The newspaper opens its pages to a tribune without endorsing it (Les tribunes publiées n'engagent que leurs auteurs); the éditorial speaks for the paper. Both take positions.

questions.stem: To whom is a lettre ouverte addressed?
choices: Only to the newspaper's editor
To one named person, while being read by everyone
To a court, as a formal complaint
To the signatories of a petition
questions.explanation: A lettre ouverte (C1 honors) challenges one person publicly (Monsieur le Ministre, …); a tribune speaks to the public about someone or something.

questions.stem: What was the Manifeste des 343, as the lesson describes it?
choices: A petition of 343 mayors against a law on benches
The first online petition in France
A declaration by women, published in 1971, that they had had an abortion when it was a crime
A speech by 343 deputies in the Assemblée nationale
questions.explanation: Published in Le Nouvel Observateur on 5 April 1971, it was signed by 343 women and is seen as a step towards the 1975 law. Like the Manifeste des 121 (1960), it is named by its number of signatories.

questions.stem: Why does the model tribune open with « Gériatres, kinésithérapeutes, architectes, nous voyons chaque jour … » ?
choices: To list the signatories in alphabetical order
To avoid saying what the signatories demand
To make the text sound informal
To give the signatories' credentials at once, which builds the text's ethos
questions.explanation: The apposition before nous tells the reader why these voices matter: they see the problem every day. Credentials in the first lines are the classic ethos device of a tribune.

questions.stem: « La présence d'une ancienne ministre apporte une caution morale au texte. » What does she bring?
choices: Moral backing: her name lends the text credit.
A financial guarantee for the campaign
A legal check of the text before publication
A deposit paid to the newspaper
questions.explanation: La caution morale is moral backing or endorsement. La caution alone is a deposit or a guarantor, which is why the adjective matters.

questions.stem: Which sentence is a precise demand rather than a wish?
choices: Nous espérons que les villes penseront davantage aux piétons.
Nous demandons aux maires de recenser avant la fin de l'année les bancs supprimés depuis dix ans.
Il faudrait sans doute réfléchir à la place des bancs.
Chacun sait que les bancs sont utiles.
questions.explanation: A demand names who (les maires), what (recenser les bancs supprimés), the scope (depuis dix ans) and when (avant la fin de l'année), so it can be checked later. The others commit no one.

questions.stem: What is a lanceur d'alerte?
choices: A journalist who writes breaking news
An official who sounds the siren in an emergency
A person who reveals wrongdoing from inside an organisation
The organiser of an online petition
questions.explanation: A whistleblower. In France the status was defined by the loi Sapin II (2016), and protection was strengthened in 2022.

questions.stem: According to the lesson, what does a European citizens' initiative need?
choices: 100,000 signatures in one member state
The support of a national parliament
A tribune in three national newspapers
One million signatures from at least seven member states
questions.explanation: A European citizens' initiative needs one million signatures from at least seven member states. The French parliamentary platforms have their own thresholds, which the lesson asks you to check.

questions.stem: In paragraph 2 of the model tribune: « en terrasse, on s'assoit ; sur la place, on circule. » What does this antithesis suggest?
choices: That in today's city one may sit down only if one pays for something
That cafés should be closed on the square
That people prefer to walk rather than sit
That the square has too many benches
questions.explanation: The sentence before says the city no longer lets people stop « sauf pour consommer »: the café terrace (where you pay) against the public square (where you must keep moving).

questions.stem: Complete with s'insurger in the present: « Nous nous ___ contre cette ville debout. »
questions.explanation: Nous nous insurgeons: a -ger verb keeps the e before -ons (insurgeons). S'insurger contre: to protest strongly against.

questions.stem: Match each genre to its addressee and aim.
choices: one named person, challenged in public
the public, through a newspaper, to demand a change
an authority, with as many signatures as possible
everyone, to declare principles or found a movement
the paper's readers, in the paper's own voice
questions.explanation: The distractor describes the éditorial (lesson 18).

questions.stem: Name the numbered parts of this tribune.
