image.alt: The layout of a tribune with four numbered markers: on the large headline Rendez-nous les bancs !, on the bold paragraph under it presenting the collective, on a bold line near the end asking the mayors for commitments, and on the shaded block of names at the bottom.

choices: le titre
le chapô
l'appel à l'action
les signataires
l'encadré
le surtitre
questions.explanation: Title, chapô presenting the collective, the call to action (Nous demandons aux maires de France …) and the list of signatories with their titles.

questions.stem: What makes a call to action checkable a year later? Select all that apply.
choices: It names who must act.
It says exactly what must be done.
It sets a deadline.
It ends with a slogan.
It uses strong adjectives.
questions.explanation: Addressee, action and deadline (and, if possible, a measurable target) make a demand verifiable. Slogans and adjectives may move readers but commit no one.

questions.stem: Reformulation. Turn the wish into a demand with demander in the present: « Nous espérons que les maires agiront. » → « Nous ___ aux maires d'agir avant la fin de l'année. »
questions.explanation: Nous demandons aux maires d'agir avant la fin de l'année: a verb of demand, an addressee and a deadline replace a hope.

questions.stem: How does a commentaire composé differ from an explication de texte?
choices: It is organised in two or three axes, each a claim, rather than following the text line by line.
It summarises the passage instead of analysing it.
It may only discuss figures of speech.
It is always oral.
questions.explanation: The explication follows the text in order (C1 honors); the commentaire composé regroups the observations under axes. Both analyse; neither summarises.

questions.stem: Which tonality best describes the lesson's passage « La vallée »?
choices: épique
élégiaque
comique
tragique
questions.explanation: The loss is certain, but the text laments it gently, without cry or revolt: élégiaque. Nothing is enlarged or celebrated (épique), nothing makes us laugh, and the tone avoids the fatality and violence of the tragic.

questions.stem: In literary analysis, what does « une scène pathétique » mean?
choices: A pitiful, badly written scene
A scene that makes us laugh at a character
A scene full of pathos, which moves the reader to pity
A scene of combat and heroism
questions.explanation: In literature pathétique means full of pathos, moving. The everyday sense (pitiful) is the false friend to avoid in a commentary.

questions.stem: Which phrase of the passage is a hypallage?
choices: comme un doigt levé pour demander la parole
le clocher trapu qui comptait les heures pour personne
Une tuile ne contient pas un été.
le chemin pensif
questions.explanation: The path isn't pensive; Jeanne is: the adjective is transferred to the path. The steeple counting the hours is a personification, the doigt levé a simile, and the tile sentence an antithesis between an object and time.

questions.stem: What is the main focalisation of the passage?
choices: Internal: we perceive the village through Jeanne
Zero: an all-knowing narrator comments on everyone
External: we see only what an outside observer could see
There is no narrator at all
questions.explanation: Rien … ne semblait avoir bougé, elle crut … entendre, comme s'il savait are Jeanne's perceptions: internal focalisation. A third-person narrator still tells the story.

questions.stem: In sentence 9, « Que faut-il emporter d'un lieu qui va disparaître ? », who is most plausibly asking the question?
choices: The narrator, addressing the reader directly
Jeanne, in free direct thought
Jeanne's mother, from the garden
The inhabitants who left in spring
questions.explanation: There is no narrator's mark (no elle se demanda); the present and the question render Jeanne's own thought inside the narration, with no verb of thinking: free direct thought (a free indirect version would shift the tense: Que fallait-il emporter …). Internal focalisation makes Jeanne the natural asker; the shift is what the study of énonciation reveals.

questions.stem: Which is an axe (a claim) rather than a topic?
choices: L'eau
Les personnages
Un village présenté comme déjà englouti
Le style
questions.explanation: An axe says what the text does: the village is shown as already drowned. L'eau, les personnages and le style are topics; a plan built on them describes instead of demonstrating.

questions.stem: An introduction reads: « Ce court passage suit Jeanne dans son dernier retour au village de son enfance. Comment ce récit d'adieu fait-il d'un village condamné le lieu d'une mémoire ? Nous verrons d'abord …, puis … » Which of the four moves is missing?
choices: La présentation
La problématique
L'annonce du plan
L'amorce
questions.explanation: It presents the passage, asks the question and announces the plan, but it has no amorce, the way in (in the lesson's model: Dans le récit de la perte, la littérature hésite souvent entre le cri et le silence).

questions.stem: In sentence 14, « bien qu'aucune lampe n'y fût allumée », what is « fût » ?
choices: The imperfect subjunctive of être, after bien que
The passé simple of être
A spelling mistake for fut
The noun le fût (a barrel)
questions.explanation: Bien que takes the subjunctive; in a literary narrative in the past, the imperfect subjunctive fût is found (recognition only at C2; current French would say soit). The passé simple is fut, without the circumflex.

questions.stem: Relevé. In sentence 16, which noun belonging to the lexical field of water names animals? Type it as it appears in the text.
questions.explanation: Les poissons nageraient dans la salle de classe: the water field reaches its strongest image, a classroom under water.

questions.stem: Put the four moves of a commentary's introduction in order.
choices: L'amorce
La présentation du passage
La problématique
L'annonce du plan
questions.explanation: A way in, the passage situated and summed up, the question, then the plan announced in one sentence.

questions.stem: Match each tonality to the effect it aims at.
choices: expresses a personal feeling
laments a loss, gently
moves the reader to pity
enlarges and celebrates struggle
makes the reader laugh
questions.explanation: The distractor describes the comique.

questions.stem: Which words of the passage belong to the lexical field of water? Select all that apply.
choices: le lavoir
le ruisseau
le barrage
la tuile
le clocher
questions.explanation: The wash-house, the stream and the dam (with l'eau, les poissons, les eaux) form the field of water that will drown the village. The tile and the steeple belong to the village's buildings.

questions.stem: Type the name of the figure that attaches an adjective to a neighbouring word, as in « une cigarette nerveuse » (with l').
questions.explanation: L'hypallage (feminine): the smoker, not the cigarette, is nervous.

questions.stem: In the DALF C2 sample paper, what does the candidate do first in front of the jury?
choices: present the content of the recording: a compte rendu
give an argued point of view on the problem the recording raises
debate the recording's subject with the jury
read out the notes taken during the two hearings
questions.explanation: The three parts come in this order: the compte rendu of the recording, then the point of view (lesson 22), then the debate (lesson 23). Notes support the compte rendu; they are not read out.

questions.stem: "Elle récuse le chiffre avancé par la maire." What does the resident do?
choices: She proves with new data that the figure is false.
She refuses to accept the figure as a fair measure.
She repeats the figure to stress it.
She asks the mayor where the figure comes from.
questions.explanation: Récuser is to refuse to accept (a figure, an argument, a witness). Proving something false is réfuter (B1 honors); stressing is souligner; asking for a source is questionner, demander.

questions.stem: A speaker says: "Ce n'est qu'une poignée de plaintes, quelques nuits par an." Which verb reports this attitude most precisely?
choices: Elle fustige les plaintes.
Elle ironise sur les plaintes.
Elle minimise les plaintes.
Elle se rallie aux plaintes.
questions.explanation: Ne … que, une poignée and quelques are cues of minimising: she plays the complaints down. Fustiger would be a loud condemnation, ironiser saying the opposite of what she means, and se rallier à coming round to them.

questions.stem: A resident who opposes the mayor's plan says, with a short laugh: "Formidable : on va donc interdire de rire après minuit." How should a compte rendu report this?
choices: La riveraine salue le projet de la maire.
La riveraine se rallie au projet de la maire.
La riveraine minimise le projet de la maire.
La riveraine ironise sur le projet de la maire.
questions.explanation: Praise that means blame, from a speaker who opposes the plan, with a laugh: this is irony (antiphrase). Reporting it as praise (salue) or agreement (se rallie) would invert her meaning; she is not playing the plan down either.

questions.stem: Which sentence does NOT belong in a compte rendu oral?
choices: La maire, à juste titre, souligne le poids de l'économie de la nuit.
Le gérant prend ses distances avec la fermeture des terrasses.
L'acousticien apporte un contrepoint technique.
En fin de débat, on observe une inflexion des positions.
questions.explanation: À juste titre (rightly) is the reporter's own opinion, which belongs in part 2. The other sentences attribute a position or describe the debate without judging it.

questions.stem: According to the lesson, what should you mainly note during the FIRST hearing of a long recording?
choices: every figure and example, word for word
the structure and the positions: who speaks, in what order, for or against what
only the moderator's questions
your own opinion on each speaker
questions.explanation: First hearing: structure and positions, leaving space. Examples, figures and attitudes are filled in during the second hearing; your opinion waits for part 2.

questions.stem: In careful written French, complete: "La riveraine s'indigne qu'on ___ d'une poignée de plaintes."
choices: parlera
parlait
parle
a parlé
questions.explanation: S'indigner que, like other verbs of feeling, takes the subjunctive: qu'on parle (a past subjunctive, qu'on ait parlé, would also be possible, but it is not offered). Parlera, parlait and a parlé are indicative.

questions.stem: "Restituez la teneur de chaque intervention." What are you asked to render?
choices: the exact words of each speaker
the tone of voice of each speaker
the length of each contribution
the gist of what each speaker said
questions.explanation: La teneur is the content, the gist. The compte rendu reports the gist and the thread of the argument, not the exact words; attitude is reported through your verbs.

questions.stem: Which opening is the best start for a compte rendu oral of the round table?
choices: Le document est une table ronde de Radio Estuaire sur la vie nocturne à Castelbrune ; quatre intervenants y prennent part.
Je trouve que la maire a raison, et je vais vous expliquer pourquoi.
D'abord la maire a parlé, puis la riveraine a répondu, puis le gérant a parlé.
Le bruit est un vrai problème dans toutes les villes.
questions.explanation: A compte rendu opens by presenting the document: its nature, source, topic and speakers. The others give an opinion, announce a turn-by-turn list, or start with a generality that says nothing about the document.

questions.stem: "L'acousticien intervient en contrepoint." What does en contrepoint mean here?
choices: as the moderator of the debate
as a contrasting voice, adding a different angle
in agreement with everyone
at the very end of the programme
questions.explanation: En contrepoint = as a counterpoint: a different angle set against the other voices (here, technical facts against opinions). It says nothing about the moderator's role, agreement or timing.

questions.stem: Listen to the extract. How does the mayor treat the residents' complaints?

audio.text: Claire Vasseur : Bonsoir à tous. Ce soir, une question qui agite Castelbrune : peut-on concilier la fête et le sommeil ? Madame la maire, vous présentez cette semaine une charte de la vie nocturne. Pourquoi maintenant ? Martine Ollier : Parce que la nuit, c'est aussi la ville. L'économie de la nuit fait vivre des centaines de salariés, elle attire les étudiants, les touristes. Je ne veux pas d'une ville qui s'éteint à vingt-deux heures. Claire Vasseur : Les riverains, eux, parlent d'un enfer. Martine Ollier : Le mot est fort. Nous recevons une centaine de plaintes par an, pour cent vingt mille habitants. Ce n'est pas rien, mais enfin, cela concerne une poignée de rues. Je préfère parler d'une cohabitation à améliorer que d'une guerre entre voisins.

choices: She denies that there are any complaints.
She says the complaints are growing fast.
She admits they exist but plays them down.
She promises to close the bars earlier.
questions.explanation: "Ce n'est pas rien, mais enfin, cela concerne une poignée de rues": she concedes, then minimises (une poignée, mais enfin). She gives a figure, so she doesn't deny the complaints; nothing is said about growth or closing bars.

questions.stem: Listen to the extract. What is Hélène Rocher's attitude to the night mediators?

audio.text: Claire Vasseur : Hélène Rocher, vous présidez l'association Dormir en ville. Les médiateurs de nuit, c'est une bonne nouvelle pour vous ? Hélène Rocher : Formidable. Des médiateurs ! Ils viendront sans doute nous expliquer, à deux heures du matin, pourquoi nous ne dormons pas. Pendant ce temps, on appelle la police pour tapage nocturne, et personne ne se déplace. Claire Vasseur : La maire parle d'une centaine de plaintes par an seulement. Hélène Rocher : Une centaine de plaintes, oui, parce que les gens ont cessé d'en déposer ! À quoi bon, puisqu'il ne se passe rien ? Ce chiffre ne mesure pas le bruit : il mesure notre découragement. Moi, je tiens un carnet depuis deux ans, avec les heures et les nuits. Personne ne me l'a jamais demandé.

choices: She welcomes them warmly as a real solution.
She is indifferent: the subject doesn't concern her.
She asks for more information before judging.
She is ironic: she doubts they will change anything.
questions.explanation: "Formidable. Des médiateurs ! Ils viendront sans doute nous expliquer … pourquoi nous ne dormons pas": praise that means the opposite. The tone and the next sentence (the police never come) show that she doubts the measure.

questions.stem: Listen to the extract again. What does Hélène Rocher do with the mayor's figure?

audio.text: Claire Vasseur : Hélène Rocher, vous présidez l'association Dormir en ville. Les médiateurs de nuit, c'est une bonne nouvelle pour vous ? Hélène Rocher : Formidable. Des médiateurs ! Ils viendront sans doute nous expliquer, à deux heures du matin, pourquoi nous ne dormons pas. Pendant ce temps, on appelle la police pour tapage nocturne, et personne ne se déplace. Claire Vasseur : La maire parle d'une centaine de plaintes par an seulement. Hélène Rocher : Une centaine de plaintes, oui, parce que les gens ont cessé d'en déposer ! À quoi bon, puisqu'il ne se passe rien ? Ce chiffre ne mesure pas le bruit : il mesure notre découragement. Moi, je tiens un carnet depuis deux ans, avec les heures et les nuits. Personne ne me l'a jamais demandé.

choices: She rejects it as a measure of noise: it shows how discouraged people are.
She corrects it with a higher official figure.
She accepts it and thanks the mayor for it.
She says it should be checked by the police.
questions.explanation: "Ce chiffre ne mesure pas le bruit : il mesure notre découragement": she récuse the figure as a measure of noise. She gives no other figure, doesn't accept it, and doesn't ask the police to check it.

questions.stem: Listen to the extract. Which sentence best reports Karim Benali's position?

audio.text: Claire Vasseur : Karim Benali, vous gérez Le Quai 9. On vous accuse d'empêcher le quartier de dormir. Karim Benali : Le bruit ne vient pas des clubs. Le Quai 9 est insonorisé, comme la plupart des établissements. Le bruit, c'est la rue : les clients qui sortent fumer, qui attendent un taxi, qui discutent sur le trottoir. Claire Vasseur : Alors la fermeture des terrasses à minuit, vous y êtes favorable ? Karim Benali : Les médiateurs, oui, cent fois oui. Mais fermer les terrasses, c'est autre chose : vous allez disperser les noctambules dans les petites rues, là où dorment les enfants. Cela dit, je ne vais pas vous mentir : j'ai besoin que mes clients restent tard. Et j'ai besoin que les voisins me supportent.

choices: Il approuve toutes les mesures de la maire sans réserve.
Il soutient les médiateurs, prend ses distances avec la fermeture des terrasses et reconnaît des intérêts contradictoires.
Il fustige les médiateurs et la fermeture des terrasses.
Il nie que la rue soit bruyante la nuit.
questions.explanation: He says yes to the mediators ("cent fois oui"), no to closing the terraces, and admits he needs both late customers and tolerant neighbours: an ambivalent position. He doesn't approve everything, doesn't attack the mediators, and says the street is where the noise is.

questions.stem: Listen to the extract. What does Paul Gendron imply about the sound level meters?

audio.text: Claire Vasseur : Paul Gendron, vous êtes acousticien. Les sonomètres sur la place, cela va régler le problème ? Paul Gendron : Ils vont le mesurer, ce qui n'est déjà pas mal. Mais attention aux moyennes. Une rue peut afficher un niveau moyen raisonnable et réveiller tout le monde trois fois par nuit. Ce qui réveille, ce sont les pics : un cri, une portière qui claque. Claire Vasseur : Et les décibels, comment faut-il les lire ? Paul Gendron : L'échelle est logarithmique. Trois décibels de plus, c'est deux fois plus d'énergie sonore. Quant aux immeubles anciens, leur isolation phonique est souvent très faible. On peut mesurer tant qu'on veut : une fenêtre à simple vitrage reste une fenêtre à simple vitrage.

choices: They will solve the problem within a year.
They are useless and should be removed.
They will measure the problem, but an average can hide what wakes people.
They should be installed inside the clubs.
questions.explanation: "Ils vont le mesurer, ce qui n'est déjà pas mal. Mais attention aux moyennes": useful for measuring, not a solution, and averages hide the peaks. He doesn't call them useless, promises nothing, and says nothing about clubs.

questions.stem: Listen to the extract. What shift in positions does it show?

audio.text: Martine Ollier : Je l'ai dit : cent plaintes par an. Hélène Rocher : Cent plaintes déposées, madame la maire. Pas cent nuits de bruit. Martine Ollier : J'en conviens, la nuance est importante. Disons cent plaintes déposées, et sans doute bien davantage de nuits difficiles. C'est pour cela que je propose une évaluation au bout d'un an. Hélène Rocher : Une évaluation, très bien. Et les médiateurs, jusqu'à quelle heure ? Martine Ollier : Jusqu'à minuit, dans un premier temps. Hélène Rocher : Alors ils partiront au moment où le bruit commence. S'ils travaillent jusqu'à trois heures du matin, je suis prête à soutenir le projet. Je le dis devant vos auditeurs : c'est la première fois que je soutiens une proposition de la mairie.

choices: The resident withdraws her complaint and the mayor drops the mediators.
The mayor and the resident both refuse any compromise.
The resident accepts that the mediators stop at midnight.
The mayor concedes what her figure measures, and the resident offers support on one condition.
questions.explanation: The mayor grants the nuance ("J'en conviens": a hundred complaints filed, not a hundred nights), and the resident says she will support the plan if the mediators work until 3 a.m. Midnight is exactly what she rejects.

questions.stem: Listen to the extract. What remains unresolved between the two speakers at the end?

audio.text: Karim Benali : Madame Rocher, nous ne sommes pas d'accord sur grand-chose, mais sur les médiateurs jusqu'à trois heures, je vous suis. Hélène Rocher : Tiens ! Voilà qui est nouveau. Karim Benali : Je suis sérieux. Mes clients écoutent plus volontiers un médiateur qu'un voisin en pyjama à sa fenêtre, et un médiateur ne crie pas. Hélène Rocher : Je ne vous le fais pas dire. Et qui les paiera, ces médiateurs ? Karim Benali : Là, il faudra en discuter. Les établissements peuvent participer, mais pas tout seuls. Hélène Rocher : Bon. On progresse, mais il reste la question de l'argent. Et ce n'est pas aux riverains de payer pour dormir. Karim Benali : Là-dessus, au moins, nous sommes d'accord.

choices: who will pay for the mediators
whether mediators should work until 3 a.m.
whether the clubs are soundproofed
whether the terraces should close at midnight
questions.explanation: They agree on mediators until 3 a.m. ("je vous suis"); the open question is money: "il reste la question de l'argent". Soundproofing and terraces are not discussed in this extract.

questions.stem: Rewrite the sentence with se rallier à, in the passé composé: "La riveraine a fini par accepter la proposition des médiateurs."
accept: La riveraine s'est ralliée à la proposition des médiateurs
La riveraine a fini par se rallier à la proposition des médiateurs
La riveraine s'est finalement ralliée à la proposition des médiateurs
Finalement, la riveraine s'est ralliée à la proposition des médiateurs
La riveraine s'est ralliée finalement à la proposition des médiateurs
La riveraine s'est enfin ralliée à la proposition des médiateurs
Finalement la riveraine s'est ralliée à la proposition des médiateurs
questions.explanation: Se rallier à takes être in compound tenses and the participle agrees with the subject: elle s'est ralliée. You may keep the idea of "in the end" (a fini par se rallier, s'est finalement ralliée).

questions.stem: Rewrite the sentence with prendre ses distances, in the present: "Le gérant ne soutient plus la fermeture des terrasses."
accept: Le gérant prend ses distances avec la fermeture des terrasses
Le gérant prend ses distances vis-à-vis de la fermeture des terrasses
Le gérant prend ses distances par rapport à la fermeture des terrasses
Le gérant prend désormais ses distances avec la fermeture des terrasses
questions.explanation: Prendre ses distances avec (or vis-à-vis de, par rapport à) quelque chose: the possessive ses agrees with the subject (il prend ses distances).

questions.stem: Type the imparfait of fustiger for nous (without the pronoun).
questions.explanation: The imparfait comes from the nous present, fustigeons, but the e is only needed before a and o: nous fustigions, vous fustigiez (and je fustigeais, ils fustigeaient).

questions.stem: Put these sentences of a compte rendu oral in order.
choices: Le document que j'ai écouté est une table ronde diffusée par Radio Estuaire.
Quatre intervenants y prennent part : la maire, un gérant de club, une riveraine et un acousticien.
Je rendrai compte de ce débat en trois temps : le constat, les solutions, puis le point d'accord.
Sur le constat, d'abord, deux lectures s'opposent.
Ce débat soulève une question plus large, sur laquelle je voudrais maintenant prendre position.
questions.explanation: Present the document, then its speakers (y refers to the table ronde), then the announced plan, then the first part (d'abord, le constat: the first of the three temps), and the transition to part 2 last.

questions.stem: Match each verb to what the speaker does.
choices: plays something down
says the opposite of what they mean, to mock
condemns loudly
refuses to accept a figure or an argument
comes round to a proposal
proves an argument false
questions.explanation: Minimiser: play down; ironiser: mock by antiphrasis; fustiger: castigate; récuser: refuse to accept; se rallier à: come round to. Proving an argument false is réfuter, not in the list.

questions.stem: Which elements belong in a DALF C2 compte rendu oral? Select all that apply.
choices: a presentation of the document and its speakers
an announced plan organised by ideas
your own opinion on who is right
the speakers' attitudes, named by precise verbs
a transition to the wider problem
questions.explanation: Present the document, announce a plan by ideas, report positions and attitudes, end with a transition. Your opinion belongs in part 2, the point of view.

questions.stem: Name the numbered parts of this chart of the DALF C2 oral (sample paper).

image.alt: A chart in two blocks. Left, listening and preparation, about 1 hour: two numbered boxes of about 15 minutes with a pause of about 3 minutes between them, and a box for notes, plan and key sentences, with a monolingual dictionary allowed. Right, in front of the jury, about 30 minutes: three rows, about 5 to 10 minutes, about 10 minutes, and the rest of the time.

choices: la première écoute
la deuxième écoute
le compte rendu
le point de vue argumenté
le débat avec le jury
la lecture du dossier
l'exposé de documents écrits
questions.explanation: The recording is heard twice with a pause between the hearings; in front of the jury, the compte rendu (about 5 to 10 minutes) comes first, then the point of view (about 10), then the debate. The DALF C2 oral starts from a recording, not from a written dossier or written documents.

questions.stem: After the round table on nightlife, which is the best problématique for the point de vue?
choices: Faut-il fermer les terrasses de la rue des Tanneurs à minuit ?
Une ville peut-elle rester vivante la nuit sans sacrifier le sommeil de ceux qui y vivent ?
Le bruit dans le monde moderne.
Combien de plaintes la mairie de Castelbrune reçoit-elle chaque année ?
questions.explanation: A problématique is a real question, wider than the recording, with more than one defensible answer. One street and one measure is too narrow, "le bruit dans le monde moderne" is a topic, not a question, and the number of complaints is a fact to look up.

questions.stem: According to the lesson's chart, which plan suits a question that can be answered yes or no, with strong arguments on both sides?
choices: the thematic plan
the problem–causes–solutions plan
the dialectical plan
a plan with one part per document
questions.explanation: Yes or no with strong arguments both ways: thesis, antithesis, then going beyond both. The thematic plan suits aspects of a phenomenon, the problem–causes–solutions plan a recognised problem, and a part per document is a summary, not a plan.

questions.stem: "Les clubs du quartier sont insonorisés, et pourtant toutes les plaintes portent sur la rue : le bruit vient donc moins des établissements que de leurs abords." What kind of reasoning is this?
choices: deduction
reductio ad absurdum
an ad hominem argument
induction
questions.explanation: It draws a general conclusion from observed cases (the clubs, the complaints): induction. Deduction would go from a general rule to a case; there is no absurd consequence and no attack on a person.

questions.stem: "Si tout bruit nocturne devait être interdit, il faudrait supprimer les bus de nuit et la Fête de la musique." What is the speaker doing?
choices: following the opposing view to an absurd consequence
drawing an analogy with another city
stating a premise of a syllogism
giving a cultural reference for its own sake
questions.explanation: This is a raisonnement par l'absurde: assume the view (ban every noise), follow it to a consequence nobody wants, and reject the view. The Fête de la musique serves the reasoning here, it isn't decoration.

questions.stem: "Les riverains sont des grincheux : inutile d'écouter leurs plaintes." Which move is this?
choices: an argument d'autorité
an argument ad hominem
an analogy
a corollary
questions.explanation: It attacks the people (grumps) instead of answering what they say: an ad hominem argument. An appeal to authority cites an expert; an analogy compares two cases; a corollary is a consequence of something already shown.

questions.stem: "L'exemple de Castelbrune est intéressant, mais il n'est pas probant." What does the speaker mean?
choices: The example is untrue.
The example is not convincing at all.
The example doesn't settle the question.
The example is too long.
questions.explanation: Probant = conclusive: it settles the point. Saying it is not probant means it doesn't prove the case on its own, while the speaker still calls it interesting; it doesn't say the example is false or long.

questions.stem: Complete the syllogism. "Tout ce qui menace durablement la santé publique relève de l'action publique. ___ Donc le bruit nocturne relève de l'action publique."
choices: Or les riverains se plaignent du bruit nocturne.
Or l'action publique coûte cher.
Or certains bruits sont agréables.
Or le bruit nocturne menace durablement la santé publique.
questions.explanation: The missing premise must link the subject of the conclusion (le bruit nocturne) to the condition of the first premise (menacer la santé publique). Complaints, cost or pleasant sounds don't make the conclusion follow.

questions.stem: "Si la nuit est un bien commun, elle a un coût : c'en est le corollaire." What is a corollaire here?
choices: a consequence that follows directly from what was just shown
an objection to what was just said
an example taken from another country
a premise that has not been proved
questions.explanation: Le corollaire is a direct consequence of what has just been established. It is not an objection, an example or an unproved premise.

questions.stem: According to the lesson, how many examples does a ten-minute point de vue need?
choices: one, developed at length
about four to six, at least one from outside the recording
as many as possible, to show general knowledge
none: the jury wants reasoning, not examples
questions.explanation: About one per argument, so four to six, varied and precise, with at least one beyond the recording. Too many examples, unexplained, weaken the talk; none at all leaves the arguments unsupported.

questions.stem: Complete: "Établissons ___ parallèle entre la rue la nuit et un immeuble en copropriété."
choices: une
des
un
de
questions.explanation: Un parallèle (masculine) is a comparison: faire, établir un parallèle entre. Une parallèle (feminine) is a parallel line in geometry, which makes no sense here; des and de don't fit a single comparison.

questions.stem: Which sentence contains a gradation (climax)?
choices: La nuit est un espace partagé.
Je défendrai l'idée que oui.
Commençons par la thèse du repos.
Une ville sans nuit s'appauvrirait, s'ennuierait, puis se viderait.
questions.explanation: A gradation lists three or more terms in rising force: grow poorer, grow bored, empty out. The other sentences make a claim, state a position and open a part.

questions.stem: "Personne ne conteste le bien-fondé de cette objection." What does nobody dispute?
choices: that the objection is well founded
that the objection was raised
that the objection is polite
that the objection is new
questions.explanation: Le bien-fondé is the soundness, the validity of a claim or request. The sentence grants that the objection has merit.

questions.stem: Listen to the extract from a point de vue. What kind of reasoning does the speaker use?

audio.text: Je voudrais établir un parallèle. Dans un immeuble, personne n'interdit de vivre : on fixe des horaires pour les travaux, on partage des parties communes, et un syndic arbitre les conflits. La rue, la nuit, n'est pas si différente. Elle aussi est un espace commun, où chacun a des droits et des devoirs. Toutes proportions gardées, ce qui fonctionne dans un immeuble pourrait inspirer la ville : non pas l'interdit, mais la règle partagée.

choices: a deduction from a general rule
an analogy
a raisonnement par l'absurde
an induction from several cases
questions.explanation: "Établir un parallèle", "n'est pas si différente", "toutes proportions gardées": the speaker compares the street with a block of flats, which is an analogy. No general rule is applied, no absurd consequence is drawn, and no series of cases is generalised.

questions.stem: Listen to the introduction. What plan does the speaker announce?

audio.text: Le débat que nous venons d'entendre dépasse Castelbrune. Il pose une question que connaissent toutes les grandes villes : une ville peut-elle rester vivante la nuit sans sacrifier le sommeil de ceux qui y vivent ? Je défendrai l'idée que oui, à condition de cesser de penser la nuit en termes d'interdits. Je montrerai d'abord que le droit au repos a pour lui des arguments très solides ; j'examinerai ensuite ce que coûterait une ville sans vie nocturne ; enfin, je proposerai une manière de dépasser cette opposition.

choices: a thematic plan: economy, culture, health
a problem–causes–solutions plan
a dialectical plan: the case for rest, the cost of silence, then going beyond both
one part per speaker of the round table
questions.explanation: Thesis (the right to rest), antithesis (what a city without nightlife would cost), then "dépasser cette opposition": a dialectical plan. The speaker states a position (oui, à condition de …) before the plan, as the lesson advises.

questions.stem: Listen to the extract. How does the speaker deal with the opposing view?

audio.text: On me dira que tout cela est bien théorique, et l'objection n'est pas sans fondement : une charte ne fait pas dormir. Mais regardons ce qui s'est passé pendant le débat. En quelques minutes, la riveraine et le gérant, qui s'opposaient sur presque tout, se sont rapprochés sur les médiateurs. Ce n'est pas une démonstration, j'en conviens. C'est un indice : quand on organise la discussion, les positions bougent.

choices: She ignores it and moves on to her conclusion.
She attacks the people who hold it.
She says it is absurd and refuses to discuss it.
She grants it some validity, then answers it with an example, without overstating the example.
questions.explanation: "L'objection n'est pas sans fondement" grants its bien-fondé; the round table is then used as an example, called "un indice", not "une démonstration": the claim goes exactly as far as its support.

questions.stem: Rewrite the sentence with the noun bien-fondé: "Personne ne conteste que cette objection soit fondée."
accept: Personne ne conteste le bien-fondé de cette objection
Nul ne conteste le bien-fondé de cette objection
questions.explanation: Le bien-fondé de + noun replaces the clause que … soit fondée. The noun is masculine and hyphenated: le bien-fondé.

questions.stem: Rewrite the sentence with établir un parallèle entre, keeping the nous imperative: "Comparons la rue et un immeuble."
accept: Établissons un parallèle entre la rue et un immeuble
questions.explanation: Établir un parallèle entre A et B = to draw a parallel between A and B; in the nous imperative, établissons. Un parallèle is masculine.

questions.stem: Type the French word, with its article, for a premise of an argument (singular).
questions.explanation: La prémisse: feminine, with an accent on the first e and a double s, unlike English premise.

questions.stem: Put these sentences from the model monologue in the order in which they come.
choices: Je défendrai l'idée que oui, à condition de penser la nuit comme un espace partagé.
Commençons par la thèse qui paraît la plus forte : celle du repos.
Faut-il alors en conclure qu'une ville doit se taire à vingt-deux heures ?
Nous voici donc devant deux exigences également légitimes.
Pour conclure, la question n'est pas de savoir qui doit l'emporter.
questions.explanation: Position in the introduction; commençons opens part 1 (the thesis); the question with alors turns part 1 into part 2 (the antithesis); nous voici donc devant deux exigences sums up both before part 3; pour conclure ends.

questions.stem: Match each kind of reasoning to its example.
choices: Le tapage nocturne est une infraction ; or ces cris en constituent un : donc …
Clubs insonorisés, plaintes sur la rue : le bruit vient des abords.
La rue la nuit, c'est comme un immeuble : il faut des règles communes.
Si tout bruit était interdit, il faudrait supprimer la Fête de la musique.
Les riverains sont des grincheux.
questions.explanation: Deduction applies a rule to a case; induction generalises from cases; analogy compares two cases; reductio ad absurdum follows a view to an absurd end. Calling residents grumps is an ad hominem attack, not a kind of reasoning in this list.

questions.stem: Which practices does the lesson recommend for examples in the point de vue? Select all that apply.
choices: say what each example shows
include at least one example from outside the recording
give a date you are not sure of, to sound precise
vary the kinds of example: a law, another city, a cultural reference, experience
list many examples without comment, to show range
questions.explanation: Examples are part of the argument: explained, varied, at least one beyond the recording. A doubtful date costs more than no date, and an unexplained list doesn't argue anything.

questions.stem: Name the kind of reasoning shown in each numbered panel.

image.alt: Three numbered panels. Panel 1: a box règle générale with an arrow down to a box cas particulier, and an example about night-time noise being an offence. Panel 2: three boxes cas 1, cas 2, cas 3 with arrows converging up to a box règle générale, and an example about soundproofed clubs and complaints about the street. Panel 3: two boxes, cas connu and cas étudié, joined by a two-way arrow marked comme, and an example comparing the street at night to a block of flats.

choices: la déduction
l'induction
l'analogie
le syllogisme
le raisonnement par l'absurde
questions.explanation: Rule to case is deduction; cases to rule is induction; two cases compared (comme) is analogy. A syllogism is a form of deduction with two premises written out, and no panel follows a view to an absurd end.

questions.stem: What is part 3 of the DALF C2 oral, as the sample paper describes it?
choices: an exchange with the jury, with no extra preparation
a second compte rendu of the recording
a written summary handed to the jury
a new recording followed by questions
questions.explanation: After the compte rendu and the point of view comes an interaction with the jury on what you have said, with no further preparation time. Nothing is written or played again.

questions.stem: An examiner says: "Je vais me faire l'avocat du diable." What is he about to do?
choices: admit that he agrees with you
defend a view he may not hold, to test your argument
accuse you of bad faith
ask you to start your talk again
questions.explanation: Se faire l'avocat du diable = to argue the other side on purpose, to see how your view stands up. It is a test, not an accusation or an agreement.

questions.stem: An examiner objects: "Les riverains ont choisi d'habiter en centre-ville." Which reply concedes and then rebounds?
choices: Vous avez tout à fait raison, je retire ce que j'ai dit.
Ce n'est pas la question.
J'en conviens, en partie ; mais je rebondis sur votre mot « choisi » : beaucoup n'ont rien choisi, le bar est arrivé après eux.
Je préfère ne pas répondre à cette question.
questions.explanation: J'en conviens grants what is fair; je rebondis sur votre mot turns the examiner's own word against the objection. Withdrawing everything gives up the argument; the other two replies dodge the question.

questions.stem: "C'est de bonne guerre." What does the candidate mean?
choices: That's an act of war.
That's a good question to end on.
That's not allowed in a debate.
That's a fair move on your part.
questions.explanation: De bonne guerre = fair play in a contest: the candidate accepts the attack as legitimate, which makes the answer that follows look calm. It doesn't mean the opposite (not allowed) and has nothing to do with real war or the end of the debate.

questions.stem: An examiner asks for a figure you don't know: "Savez-vous combien coûte un médiateur de nuit ?" What is the best answer?
choices: Je ne saurais vous donner un chiffre précis, et je préfère ne pas en inventer ; ce que je sais, c'est que ce coût se compare à celui des interventions de police.
Environ trois mille euros par mois, je crois.
Ce n'est pas mon sujet.
Personne ne le sait, de toute façon.
questions.explanation: Admit and offer: say you don't know, refuse to invent, then bring the question back to what you do know. A guessed figure can be wrong, "ce n'est pas mon sujet" is an evasion, and "personne ne le sait" is an unfounded claim.

questions.stem: An examiner says: "Vous noyez un peu le poisson." What is the examiner telling the candidate?
choices: You have answered too briefly.
You are wandering into details to avoid answering.
You are being too aggressive.
You have changed the subject to fishing.
questions.explanation: Noyer le poisson = to muddy the waters, drowning a question in details so as not to answer it. The right response is to recentre on what the argument depends on.

questions.stem: The jury points out that one of your claims was unproven. Which answer backtracks without losing face?
choices: Je retire tout ce que j'ai dit.
Je maintiens tout, c'est évident.
Je rectifie le tir : c'est une idée répandue, que je n'ai pas vérifiée. Le reste de mon raisonnement tient sans elle.
Vous êtes de mauvaise foi.
questions.explanation: Rectifier le tir corrects one claim and protects the rest. Withdrawing everything gives up the whole view; maintaining an unproven claim is rigid; accusing the examiner of bad faith is a personal attack.

questions.stem: Which sentence is critical of the person it describes, suggesting rigidity?
choices: Il défend son point de vue.
Il maintient sa position.
Il tient bon face aux objections.
Il campe sur ses positions.
questions.explanation: Camper sur ses positions (to dig one's heels in) usually suggests firmness without listening. Défendre son point de vue is neutral; maintenir sa position and tenir bon describe firmness without that criticism.

questions.stem: "Je fais amende honorable : ce chiffre venait de la riveraine, pas de la maire." What is the speaker doing?
choices: admitting a mistake and apologising for it
paying a fine
refusing to change a word
accusing the resident of lying
questions.explanation: Faire amende honorable = to admit a fault publicly and apologise. Une amende alone is a fine, but in this set phrase the meaning is figurative.

questions.stem: "Dire qu'il faut du dialogue, c'est enfoncer des portes ouvertes." What is the criticism?
choices: The remark is rude.
The remark states the obvious.
The remark is false.
The remark is too technical.
questions.explanation: Enfoncer des portes ouvertes = to break down doors that are already open: saying what nobody disputes. The criticism is that it adds nothing, not that it is false, rude or technical.

questions.stem: Complete with the present of désamorcer: "Nous ___ la question en la reformulant."
choices: désamorcons
désamorceons
désamorçons
désamorssons
questions.explanation: Before o, c takes a cedilla to keep the [s] sound: nous désamorçons (and je désamorçais). Adding e is the spelling for -ger verbs (fustigeons), not -cer verbs.

questions.stem: "Le vrai point d'achoppement, ce sont les horaires." What are the hours?
choices: the point on which everyone agrees
the first point of the debate
the point the jury forgot
the sticking point where agreement breaks down
questions.explanation: Un point d'achoppement is a sticking point, a stumbling block (achopper sur = to stumble over).

questions.stem: Listen to the exchange. What does the candidate do?

audio.text: Mme Lemaire : Vous proposez que les établissements paient une partie des médiateurs. Quelle part, exactement ? Le candidat : C'est une question très intéressante, qui renvoie à des débats plus larges sur la fiscalité locale, sur l'histoire des taxes municipales, et même sur la manière dont les villes européennes, d'une façon générale, organisent leurs services, ce qui est un sujet passionnant en soi.

choices: He drowns the question in generalities instead of answering it.
He answers precisely with a percentage.
He admits he doesn't know and offers what he does know.
He concedes the examiner's point and rebounds.
questions.explanation: The examiner asks "quelle part, exactement ?" and the candidate lists wider topics without giving any answer: he noie le poisson. He gives no figure, doesn't admit ignorance, and concedes nothing.

questions.stem: Listen to the exchange. Which move does the candidate make?

audio.text: M. Duval : Vous avez affirmé que les villes qui ferment tôt deviennent dangereuses. Sur quoi vous appuyez-vous ? La candidate : Je me suis sans doute avancée un peu vite. C'est une idée répandue, mais je n'ai pas de chiffres pour l'étayer. Je la retire. Cela dit, le cœur de mon argument ne change pas : une ville sans vie nocturne perd une part de son attrait.

choices: She refuses to withdraw anything.
She withdraws one unsupported claim and keeps the core of her argument.
She abandons her whole position.
She accuses the examiner of a procès d'intention.
questions.explanation: "Je la retire. Cela dit, le cœur de mon argument ne change pas": a limited retreat, the graceful backtrack the lesson teaches (rectifier le tir). She neither digs in nor gives up everything, and makes no accusation.

questions.stem: Listen to the exchange. What technique does the candidate use?

audio.text: Mme Lemaire : La gratuité totale, c'est simple et juste. Pourquoi compliquer les choses ? Le candidat : « Simple », je vous l'accorde. « Juste », j'en suis moins sûr. Je rebondis sur votre mot : est-il juste que la personne qui gagne bien sa vie voyage gratuitement aux frais de tous, quand le bus reste plein à craquer aux heures de pointe ?

choices: He changes the subject to avoid the question.
He agrees completely with the examiner.
He grants one of the examiner's words and turns the other into a question against the objection.
He asks the examiner to repeat the question.
questions.explanation: He concedes "simple" (je vous l'accorde) and rebounds on "juste" (je rebondis sur votre mot), turning it into a question about fairness. He stays on the subject and doesn't agree completely.

questions.stem: Rewrite in a formal register with revenir sur ses propos, in the passé composé: "Il a retiré ce qu'il avait dit."
accept: Il est revenu sur ses propos
questions.explanation: Revenir takes être: il est revenu. Ses propos (his words) agrees with the subject: elle est revenue sur ses propos, ils sont revenus sur leurs propos.

questions.stem: Rewrite with tenir tête à, in the passé composé: "Elle a résisté à l'examinateur avec fermeté et courtoisie."
accept: Elle a tenu tête à l'examinateur avec fermeté et courtoisie
Elle a tenu tête à l'examinateur avec courtoisie et fermeté
Elle a tenu tête avec fermeté et courtoisie à l'examinateur
questions.explanation: Tenir tête à quelqu'un, passé composé with avoir: elle a tenu tête à l'examinateur. Tenu is the participle of tenir; tête has no article in the phrase.

questions.stem: Complete with one word: "Sur la question du financement, je ne céderai pas de ___."
questions.explanation: Céder du terrain = to give ground; in the negative, ne pas céder de terrain.

questions.stem: Put this exchange, adapted from the model debate, in order.
choices: M. Duval : Je vais me faire l'avocat du diable. Les riverains ont choisi d'habiter en centre-ville.
Ana : C'est de bonne guerre. Mais je rebondis sur votre mot « choisi » : beaucoup n'ont rien choisi.
M. Duval : Admettons. Mais vos médiateurs jusqu'à trois heures, qui les paie ?
Ana : En partie le contribuable, et je l'assume ; mais les établissements devraient contribuer.
Mme Lemaire : Et ce coût, savez-vous à combien il s'élève pour un médiateur de nuit ?
questions.explanation: The devil's-advocate objection comes first; Ana rebounds on its word "choisi"; Admettons accepts her answer and moves to cost; she answers who pays; the follow-up (ce coût) asks for the exact figure behind that answer.

questions.stem: Match each phrase to the move it makes.
left: Si je comprends bien votre question, …
C'est une vraie question, et je vais y répondre franchement.
Je ne saurais vous donner un chiffre, mais ce que je sais, c'est que …
choices: clarify
concede and rebound
defuse
admit and offer
hold your ground
evade the question
questions.explanation: Each phrase is the lesson's model for one of the five moves. None of them evades: even the admission of ignorance offers something in return.

questions.stem: Which phrases are ways of backtracking? Select all that apply.
choices: rectifier le tir
faire machine arrière
revenir sur ses propos
camper sur ses positions
faire amende honorable
questions.explanation: Rectifier le tir (correct and go on), faire machine arrière (backpedal), revenir sur ses propos (take back one's words, formal) and faire amende honorable (admit a fault and apologise) all retreat to some degree. Camper sur ses positions is the opposite: refusing to move.

questions.stem: Name the move in each numbered box of this wheel.

image.alt: Five numbered boxes around a central circle labelled objection, each with an example phrase: 1, si je comprends bien votre question; 2, j'en conviens, mais; 3, je rebondis sur votre mot « … »; 4, c'est une vraie question, j'y réponds franchement; 5, je maintiens que.

choices: clarifier
concéder
rebondir
désamorcer
tenir bon
esquiver
noyer le poisson
questions.explanation: The phrase in each box gives the move: checking the question (clarifier), granting a point (concéder), picking up a word (rebondir), calming a hostile question by facing it (désamorcer), keeping your position (tenir bon). Esquiver and noyer le poisson are evasions, not moves to make.

questions.stem: According to the sample papers and the sources the lesson cites, what do you need to pass the DALF C2?
choices: 60/100 in all, whatever the marks in each paper
at least 25/50 in each paper
50/100 in all and at least 5/25 in each part
50/100 in all and at least 10/50 in each paper
questions.explanation: Total 50/100, and below 10/50 in either paper fails the diploma whatever the total. 5/25 per part is the DALF C1 rule (four parts of 25), not the C2's two papers of 50.

questions.stem: What does the DALF C2 written paper ask for, in the sample papers?
choices: one structured text of at least 700 words, from a dossier of about 2,000 words
a synthesis of 200 to 240 words and an essay of 250 words
two texts of 350 words each, one per subject
a summary of each document, then a conclusion
questions.explanation: One text of at least 700 words (article, éditorial, rapport, discours …) on one of two subjects, from a dossier of about 2,000 words, in 3 h 30. The synthesis and the essay belong to the DALF C1.

questions.stem: An older book says DALF C2 candidates choose between lettres et sciences humaines and sciences. What does the lesson say?
choices: The choice still exists for the written paper only.
The choice of domain was removed from the March 2020 sessions.
It was never true.
The choice now exists for the oral only.
questions.explanation: FEI's change kit of October 2019 removed the choice of domain from both DALF C2 papers from March 2020. Older books and sample papers still show it.

questions.stem: Which statement matches the lesson?
choices: C2 means speaking exactly like a native speaker.
Only native speakers can reach C2.
C2 is defined by what a user can do, not by passing for a native speaker.
C2 is the same as a near-native accent.
questions.explanation: The Companion Volume describes C2 without using the native speaker as its yardstick; plenty of natives would not meet every C2 descriptor, and quasi natif is a different idea.

questions.stem: In the CEFR sense, what is la médiation?
choices: settling a quarrel between two neighbours
teaching grammar to beginners
translating a text word for word
making a text or an exchange accessible to someone else, by summarising or explaining
questions.explanation: As a CEFR activity, mediation is passing meaning on: summarising sources, explaining what a speaker implies or what irony does. Mediation in a dispute is the other, everyday sense; word-for-word translation is not what the scales describe.

questions.stem: "Chaque descripteur décrit ce qu'un apprenant sait faire." What is a descripteur?
choices: a short statement of what a learner can do at a level
an examiner who marks the oral
a list of words to learn
a description of a picture in the exam
questions.explanation: Un descripteur is a can-do statement on a CEFR scale. A set of them used as a standard is un référentiel.

questions.stem: "La passation de l'épreuve orale dure environ trente minutes." What does la passation mean here?
choices: the handover of power
the sitting of the test
the marking of the test
the registration for the test
questions.explanation: La passation d'une épreuve is the sitting, the administration of a test. La passation de pouvoirs (a handover) is the other sense, which doesn't fit here.

questions.stem: In a French concours, what does it mean to be admissible?
choices: to have passed the whole exam
to have registered on time
to have passed the written papers and be eligible for the oral
to be allowed to use a dictionary
questions.explanation: In a concours, the written papers decide l'admissibilité, and l'admission (the final pass) is decided after the oral, in many concours on all the marks together. The DALF has no such stage: its two papers simply add up.

questions.stem: "Après dix ans en France, elle avait atteint un palier." What had she reached?
choices: the landing of her building
the top level of the CEFR
a new job
a plateau: a level where she stopped progressing
questions.explanation: Un palier is a landing on a staircase, and figuratively a plateau, a stage where progress levels off; the context (ten years, no more progress) chooses the second meaning.

questions.stem: According to the lesson, what shifts fossilised errors?
choices: feedback: someone who corrects you
more input: reading and listening more
a stay in France
learning rarer words
questions.explanation: Fossilised errors persist precisely because the speaker no longer notices them and nobody corrects them, so input alone doesn't change them; feedback does.

questions.stem: Which adjective comes from the stripes on a soldier's sleeve that mark years of service?
choices: aguerri
chevronné
idiomatique
admissible
questions.explanation: Chevronné comes from le chevron, a service stripe: seasoned by years. Aguerri comes from la guerre: hardened by battle.

questions.stem: "Au niveau C2, la justesse compte plus que la rareté des mots." What counts more than rare words?
choices: speaking fast
a perfect accent
the exact, right word in the right place
knowing many idioms
questions.explanation: La justesse is accuracy: the right word in the right place. The sentence contrasts it with rare vocabulary, not with speed, accent or idioms.

questions.stem: Listen. According to the speaker, why had her errors fossilised?

audio.text: Après dix ans à Lyon, je croyais que l'examen serait une formalité. Je parlais français tous les jours. Mais une enseignante m'a fait remarquer que mes erreurs s'étaient fossilisées. Je les faisais depuis des années, et personne ne me corrigeait plus, puisque tout le monde me comprenait. Je ne les entendais même plus moi-même.

choices: She had stopped speaking French.
Her teacher had taught her wrong forms.
She had moved to a region with a strong accent.
Nobody corrected her any more, because everyone understood her.
questions.explanation: "Personne ne me corrigeait plus, puisque tout le monde me comprenait": the errors no longer got in the way of understanding, so nobody pointed them out. She spoke French every day, and nothing is said about a teacher's mistakes or an accent.

questions.stem: Listen to the message from an (invented) exam centre. What should a candidate take from it?

audio.text: Bonjour, vous êtes bien au centre d'examen de l'Alliance française de Rivemont. Les inscriptions au DALF C2 pour la session de mai sont ouvertes jusqu'au quinze mars. Les dates des épreuves et les frais d'inscription figurent sur notre site. Attention : l'épreuve orale peut avoir lieu un autre jour que l'épreuve écrite. Votre convocation vous indiquera l'heure exacte de chaque épreuve.

choices: The oral may be on a different day, and the convocation gives the exact time of each paper.
The two papers always take place on the same morning.
The dates and fees are the same in every centre.
Registration is open all year.
questions.explanation: "L'épreuve orale peut avoir lieu un autre jour … Votre convocation vous indiquera l'heure exacte." The message gives a registration deadline (15 March) and refers to its own site for dates and fees: each centre sets its own.

questions.stem: Listen to a teacher's advice. What is her main point?

audio.text: Vous lisez beaucoup, et c'est très bien. Mais la lecture ne corrige pas une erreur que vous ne voyez plus. Écrivez chaque semaine et faites-vous relire. Et quand on vous corrige, notez la correction quelque part : une erreur qu'on ne note pas revient.

choices: Reading is a waste of time at C2.
Write regularly, get corrected, and keep a record of corrections.
Only grammar exercises can fix errors.
Avoid writing until your errors have disappeared.
questions.explanation: She praises reading but says it can't correct invisible errors: write, be reread, note the corrections. She doesn't call reading a waste of time or recommend avoiding writing.

questions.stem: Rewrite with se fossiliser, in the plus-que-parfait: "Ses erreurs étaient devenues permanentes."
questions.explanation: Pronominal verbs take être: s'étaient. The se is a direct object, so the participle agrees with erreurs (feminine plural): fossilisées.

questions.stem: Rewrite with perfectionner or se perfectionner, in the present: "Elle continue à améliorer son français."
accept: Elle continue à se perfectionner en français
Elle continue de se perfectionner en français
Elle continue à perfectionner son français
Elle continue de perfectionner son français
questions.explanation: Se perfectionner en français (to improve one's French) or perfectionner son français (to perfect it): both say the same thing. Continuer à and continuer de are both correct.

questions.stem: Type the French abbreviation for the CEFR, with its article.
questions.explanation: Le CECRL: Cadre européen commun de référence pour les langues (also written le CECR).

questions.stem: Put the modules of French C2 in their order in the course.
choices: Precision, register and the norm
Style and the literary tenses
Specialised French
French across the French-speaking world
The long written text
Speaking at C2 and the DALF C2
questions.explanation: Modules 1 to 6: precision and the norm first, then style, specialised French, the francophone world, the long written text, and speaking with the exam last.

questions.stem: Match each word to its meaning.
choices: the sitting of a test
a plateau in progress
a refresher, catching up
double marking
the pass mark
questions.explanation: La passation d'une épreuve; un palier (also a landing); une mise à niveau (also a software upgrade); la double correction (two markers). The pass mark is le seuil de réussite (C1).

questions.stem: Which statements about the DALF C2 match the lesson? Select all that apply.
choices: The diploma is valid for life.
The two papers are each marked out of 50.
The written paper lasts 2 h 30.
Each exam centre sets its own dates and fees.
The oral starts from a long recording heard twice, in the sample paper.
questions.explanation: Valid for life; two papers of 50; centres set dates and fees; a recording heard twice. The written paper lasts 3 h 30 (2 h 30 is the DALF C1 writing paper).

questions.stem: Name the numbered parts of this DALF C2 chart.

image.alt: Two boxes with numbered gaps. Left box, gap 1 at the top, then: épreuve individuelle, about 1 hour of preparation, gap 3, a recording of about 15 minutes heard twice, compte rendu, point de vue, débat, 50 points. Right box, gap 2 at the top, then: épreuve collective, gap 4, a dossier of about 2,000 words, two subjects with one to treat, a text of at least 700 words, article, éditorial, rapport, discours, 50 points. Below: total out of 100; pass with 50/100 and gap 5.

choices: compréhension et production orales
compréhension et production écrites
environ 30 minutes devant le jury
au moins 10 sur 50 à chaque épreuve
au moins 5 sur 25 à chaque partie
questions.explanation: The individual paper is the oral, the collective one the written paper; the oral lasts about 30 minutes in front of the jury after about an hour of preparation; the written paper 3 h 30; at least 10/50 in each paper. 2 h 30 and 5/25 are DALF C1 figures.

questions.stem: In the DALF C2 written paper, as the sample papers describe it, what do you write?
choices: two texts, one on each subject
a summary of every document
one structured text on one of two subjects, at least 700 words
a 250-word essay and a synthesis
questions.explanation: You treat one of the two subjects, in one structured text of at least 700 words in the genre it names. Summaries and the synthesis-plus-essay pair are not the C2 task.

questions.stem: Under the decree of 22 May 2023 (document 1), when can a regular domestic air route be banned?
choices: when any train covers the trip in under 4 hours
when the flight emits more CO2 than a car
when the airport has fewer than a hundred passengers a day
when a direct train covers the trip in under 2 h 30, several times a day, leaving more than 8 hours on site
questions.explanation: The decree requires a direct train (no change) under 2 h 30, several daily return trips at satisfactory times, and more than 8 hours on site. Four hours was the Convention citoyenne's proposal, not the rule.

questions.stem: Which routes did the 2023 decree cover, as document 1 reports?
choices: Paris-Orly to Bordeaux, Nantes and Lyon
every route from Paris to a city under 500 km
Paris to Marseille, Nice and Toulouse
Valbrume to Paris
questions.explanation: Three routes from Orly: Bordeaux, Nantes and Lyon, already largely abandoned since 2021. Valbrume's route is invented and, the dossier says, not covered (over 2 h 30 by train, with a change).

questions.stem: How should you use the figures of document 5 in your text?
choices: as real national statistics
by attributing them to the dossier's infographic, since they are invented for the exercise
not at all: invented figures are forbidden
by rounding them to look more official
questions.explanation: The figures are labelled fictitious: you may use them, as the dossier's (selon l'infographie du dossier), never as real data. Changing them or presenting them as national statistics misreports the source.

questions.stem: Which document comes from an interest group, to be cited as a voice rather than as neutral fact?
choices: document 1, the fact sheet on the law
document 7, the science magazine
document 4, the interview with a rail users' association
document 5, the infographic
questions.explanation: Rail Avenir defends rail users: fair, but partial by position. Document 1 is a fact sheet of record; documents 5 and 7 are presented as information (5 with invented figures).

questions.stem: "Le report modal ne se décrète pas." What does the speaker mean?
choices: Transport reports can't be published by decree.
Train timetables can't be changed.
Fares must be decided by law.
A shift from one mode of transport to another can't simply be ordered: the alternative must be good enough.
questions.explanation: Le report modal is modal shift; ne se décrète pas = can't be imposed by decree. The rest of the interview explains why: frequency, prices, capacity.

questions.stem: Which feature belongs to the rapport (subject 2) rather than to the éditorial (subject 1)?
choices: a heading with the addressee and an Objet line, and ranked, dated recommendations
a title that announces a line
the newspaper's nous
rhetorical questions and a conditional threat at the end
questions.explanation: The rapport answers a commissioning body: heading, numbered parts, impersonal but committed, ranked préconisations with an échéancier. Title, nous and rhetorical effects are the éditorial's tools.

questions.stem: The model éditorial ends: "son interdiction n'aura de climatique que le nom." What does this mean?
choices: The ban will have a long name.
The ban will be climate policy in name only.
The ban will only concern the climate.
The ban will be named after the climate.
questions.explanation: N'avoir de X que le nom = to be X in name only. The paper warns that a ban without a train would not really serve the climate.

questions.stem: What does document 7 say about carbon offsetting (la compensation carbone)?
choices: It erases a flight's emissions.
It is required by European law.
Many scientists judge it insufficient: a tree takes decades to absorb a flight's CO2.
It is cheaper than sustainable aviation fuel and widely available.
questions.explanation: The article reports that many scientists find offsetting insufficient (decades for a tree to absorb the CO2, projects that would have happened anyway). It credits it with drawing attention to the cost but says it lets people believe the cost can be erased. The EU obligation it mentions concerns sustainable fuels, not offsetting.

questions.stem: Type the French phrase, with its article, that translates the Swedish word flygskam in document 6.
questions.explanation: La honte de prendre l'avion (flight shame), a calque of Swedish flygskam.

questions.stem: Rewrite in the impersonal style of a rapport, starting with "Il est préconisé de": "Nous conseillons de renouveler la subvention pour deux ans."
accept: Il est préconisé de renouveler la subvention pour deux ans
Il est préconisé de renouveler la subvention pour une durée de deux ans
Il est préconisé de renouveler pour deux ans la subvention
questions.explanation: Il est préconisé de + infinitive removes the writer (nous) while keeping the recommendation: the committed but impersonal voice of the rapport.

questions.stem: Put the steps of the 3 h 30 in the order the lesson suggests.
choices: Read both subjects, survey the dossier and choose
Scan, spot and select what the subject needs
Set the problématique and plan, with your own examples
Write straight onto the answer sheet
Reread, correct and count the words
questions.explanation: Survey and choose (15 minutes), select (35), plan (30), write once from the plan (105), reread and count (25): lesson 17's split, advice rather than an exam rule.

questions.stem: Match each document to its genre.
choices: a fact sheet on the law
an economist's op-ed
an essayist's column
readers' letters
a court decision
questions.explanation: 1 is the fact sheet; 3 the economist's tribune; 6 the column on flight shame; 8 the readers' letters. No document is a court decision.

questions.stem: Which checks are on the lesson's self-check list? Select all that apply.
choices: each document cited by its source, in your own words
at least two examples of your own
one document per part, in the dossier's order
participle agreements, especially with avoir and a direct object placed before
the word count written where the paper asks
questions.explanation: Cite by source, add your own examples, check agreements, count and write the count. Planning one part per document is a summary, which the lesson warns against: plan by idea.

questions.stem: Listen to extract 1. Which two reasons does Céline Arnaud give for free transport?

audio.text: Julien Marchal : Bonsoir. Rivemont rendra son réseau de bus et de tramway gratuit pour ses habitants à la rentrée. Céline Arnaud, vous êtes vice-présidente de la métropole chargée des mobilités. Pourquoi ce choix ? Céline Arnaud : Pour une raison de justice d'abord : se déplacer, c'est accéder à l'emploi, aux soins, à la culture. Et pour une raison pratique : les recettes des titres de transport ne couvrent qu'une petite part du coût du réseau, alors que la billettique et la lutte contre la fraude nous coûtent cher. Les distributeurs, les cartes, les contrôles : tout cela disparaît avec la gratuité.

choices: pressure from employers and a fall in ridership
a national law and a European grant
the end of the car and the closure of car parks
fairness of access, and the cost of ticketing and fraud control compared with fare revenue
questions.explanation: Justice (access to jobs, care, culture) and a practical reason: fares cover only a small part of the cost, while ticketing and fraud control are expensive. Employers, laws, grants and car parks aren't mentioned.

questions.stem: Listen to extract 2. What does the economist mean by un effet d'aubaine here?

audio.text: Julien Marchal : Thomas Weber, vous êtes économiste des transports. La gratuité fonctionne ? Thomas Weber : Elle remplit les bus, c'est incontestable : à Dunkerque, par exemple, la fréquentation a nettement augmenté. Mais qui sont ces nouveaux voyageurs ? Une bonne partie marchait ou prenait le vélo. Et ceux qui payaient déjà leur abonnement ne paient plus, sans rien changer à leurs habitudes : c'est un effet d'aubaine. Quant aux automobilistes, ils sont beaucoup moins nombreux à laisser leur voiture qu'on ne l'espérait.

choices: Passengers who already paid now travel free without changing their habits.
Drivers leave their cars at home.
The buses become faster.
The network makes a profit.
questions.explanation: "Ceux qui payaient déjà … ne paient plus, sans rien changer à leurs habitudes : c'est un effet d'aubaine": a benefit to people who would have acted the same way anyway. He says few drivers switch.

questions.stem: Listen to extract 2 again. What is Thomas Weber's overall stance?

audio.text: Julien Marchal : Thomas Weber, vous êtes économiste des transports. La gratuité fonctionne ? Thomas Weber : Elle remplit les bus, c'est incontestable : à Dunkerque, par exemple, la fréquentation a nettement augmenté. Mais qui sont ces nouveaux voyageurs ? Une bonne partie marchait ou prenait le vélo. Et ceux qui payaient déjà leur abonnement ne paient plus, sans rien changer à leurs habitudes : c'est un effet d'aubaine. Quant aux automobilistes, ils sont beaucoup moins nombreux à laisser leur voiture qu'on ne l'espérait.

choices: He rejects every effect of free transport.
He grants that free transport raises ridership, but doubts it shifts many drivers.
He supports free transport without reservation.
He says Dunkirk's experiment failed and was stopped.
questions.explanation: "Elle remplit les bus, c'est incontestable" is a concession; the rest qualifies it (walkers and cyclists, a windfall, few drivers). He says nothing about Dunkirk stopping.

questions.stem: Listen to extract 3. Which best describes Fatou Diallo's attitude?

audio.text: Fatou Diallo : Sur le principe, notre association ne peut qu'applaudir. Mais allez prendre la ligne 4 à huit heures du matin : gratuite ou pas, on y voyage debout, collés les uns aux autres. La gratuité, très bien ; la gratuité debout, merci bien. Céline Arnaud : Nous allons renforcer les fréquences. Fatou Diallo : Alors commencez par là ! Un bus toutes les vingt minutes, même gratuit, ne fera jamais concurrence à la voiture. Ce qu'il nous faut, c'est le cadencement : un passage régulier, à heure fixe. Et pour les plus modestes, le tarif solidaire existe déjà.

choices: completely opposed to free transport
indifferent to the debate
in favour in principle, ironic about overcrowding, and asking for frequency first
worried mainly about fare dodging
questions.explanation: "Sur le principe … applaudir" (in favour), "la gratuité debout, merci bien" (irony about la saturation), "commencez par là" and le cadencement (frequency first). Fraud isn't her subject.

questions.stem: Listen to extract 4. Which sentence reports Marc Lebrun's position?

audio.text: Julien Marchal : Marc Lebrun, vous représentez les entreprises de la métropole. Elles financent déjà le réseau. Marc Lebrun : Oui, par le versement mobilité, qui pèse sur la masse salariale. Je ne vais pas cracher dans la soupe : des transports gratuits, c'est bon pour nos salariés, surtout les moins bien payés. Mais nos adhérents s'inquiètent. Si les voyageurs ne paient plus rien, qui comblera la différence ? Nous craignons d'être les premiers sollicités.

choices: Il fustige la gratuité et refuse tout versement mobilité.
Il se rallie sans réserve au projet de la métropole.
Il minimise le coût du versement mobilité.
Il reconnaît l'intérêt de la gratuité pour les salariés, mais craint que les entreprises paient davantage.
questions.explanation: "C'est bon pour nos salariés" … "Mais nos adhérents s'inquiètent … d'être les premiers sollicités": an ambivalent position. He doesn't condemn the project outright, doesn't rally to it without reservation, and doesn't play down the levy.

questions.stem: Listen to extract 5. How does the economist respond to the comparison with a library?

audio.text: Thomas Weber : Il y a aussi une question symbolique. Un titre de transport, même bon marché, rappelle que le service a un coût. Ce qui est gratuit est moins respecté, et finit par être moins financé. Céline Arnaud : Personne ne dit cela d'une bibliothèque municipale. Elle est gratuite, et personne ne la méprise. Thomas Weber : La comparaison ne tient pas. Une bibliothèque n'est pas saturée à huit heures du matin, et elle ne coûte pas ce que coûte un réseau de bus.

choices: He rejects it: a library is neither overcrowded at rush hour nor as costly as a bus network.
He accepts it and changes his mind.
He ironises about libraries in general.
He says libraries should charge a fee.
questions.explanation: "La comparaison ne tient pas", with two reasons: he récuse the analogy. He doesn't accept it, mock libraries or ask for fees.

questions.stem: Listen to extract 6. What is the sticking point that remains?

audio.text: Fatou Diallo : Monsieur Lebrun, je crois que pour une fois nous sommes d'accord : il faut d'abord plus de bus. Marc Lebrun : Plus de bus, plus souvent, oui. Mes adhérents le demandent depuis des années. Fatou Diallo : Alors la vraie question, c'est le calendrier. La métropole veut la gratuité à la rentrée, et les nouveaux bus dans deux ans. Marc Lebrun : C'est bien là que le bât blesse. Faire l'inverse serait plus raisonnable.

choices: whether more buses are needed
the timing: free fares now and new buses later, or the reverse
whether employers should pay anything at all
whether the network should include trams
questions.explanation: Both agree on more, more frequent buses; "la vraie question, c'est le calendrier" and "c'est bien là que le bât blesse" (that's where the shoe pinches) point to the order of the measures, le point d'achoppement.

questions.stem: Who pays the versement mobilité in France?
choices: passengers, as part of the fare
the national government only
employers, private or public, with at least eleven employees, where the transport authority has adopted it
car drivers, through fuel tax
questions.explanation: It is a payroll tax on employers, private or public (at least eleven employees), inside the area of a transport authority that has adopted it, and one of the main sources of funding for urban public transport.

questions.stem: Which is correct about the real cases cited in the lesson?
choices: Dunkirk made its buses free in 2023.
Montpellier made its network free for everyone, residents or not, in 2018.
Luxembourg's free transport is for residents only.
Luxembourg made public transport free nationwide in March 2020.
questions.explanation: Luxembourg: nationwide, 1 March 2020, for residents, cross-border workers and tourists (first class still paid). Dunkirk: September 2018. Montpellier: December 2023, for residents.

questions.stem: In the model debate, how does Malik answer the question about the cost of full free transport?
choices: He says the debate didn't give the figure, refuses to invent one, and offers a known point instead.
He gives an estimate to sound precise.
He changes the subject to Luxembourg.
He says the question is unfair.
questions.explanation: "Le débat ne donnait pas ce chiffre, et je ne vais pas en inventer un. Ce que l'on sait, c'est que …": admit and offer (lesson 23).

questions.stem: Rewrite with récuser, in the present: "L'économiste refuse d'accepter la comparaison avec les bibliothèques."
accept: L'économiste récuse la comparaison avec les bibliothèques
L'économiste récuse la comparaison avec la bibliothèque
L'économiste récuse la comparaison avec une bibliothèque
questions.explanation: Récuser takes a direct object: récuser une comparaison, un chiffre, un argument. It means refusing to accept, which is what the economist does ("La comparaison ne tient pas").

questions.stem: Type the French noun, with its article, for a regular-interval (clockface) timetable.
questions.explanation: Le cadencement: buses or trains at the same minutes every hour (un horaire cadencé).

questions.stem: Match each word to its meaning.
choices: the ticketing system
the fare structure
a fare dodger
the body in charge of a local network
overcrowding
a free ticket for tourists
questions.explanation: La billettique: machines, cards, software; la tarification: the set of fares; le fraudeur, la fraudeuse: someone who travels without paying; l'autorité organisatrice (de la mobilité): a city, metropolitan area or region; la saturation: full to capacity.

questions.stem: Which checks belong to the lesson's self-assessment against the C2 descriptors? Select all that apply.
choices: I rendered every speaker's position and attitude, including the shifts.
My talk's plan was audible and its main points easy to recall.
I gave an exact figure for every question, even if I had to guess.
I held my position under objections and answered hostile questions tactfully.
My grammar held while I was thinking hard about the argument.
questions.explanation: Rendering stances and shifts, an audible plan, tactful firmness and accuracy under pressure are all on the list. Guessing figures is what the lessons warn against.

questions.stem: Put the parts of the model compte rendu in order.
choices: Le document que j'ai écouté est un débat radiophonique consacré à la gratuité des transports publics.
Quatre intervenants s'y opposent, puis s'y rapprochent.
Je rendrai compte de ce débat en trois temps.
Les arguments en faveur de la gratuité, d'abord : la justice et le coût de la billettique.
Ce débat dépasse le cas de Rivemont : je voudrais à présent discuter une question plus large.
questions.explanation: Document, then speakers (y refers to the debate), then the announced plan, then the first part (d'abord), then the transition to the point of view.

cards.back: Jean-Baptiste Poquelin, baptised 15 January 1622 at Saint-Eustache, Paris; died at home on 17 February 1673, after being taken ill during the fourth performance of Le Malade imaginaire.
Illustre Théâtre with the Béjarts (1643, bankrupt); touring the provinces from 1646; before Louis XIV on 24 October 1658; Petit-Bourbon, then the Palais-Royal (1661).
One-act prose comedy: two provincial girls reject plain suitors, who send their valets disguised as noblemen. A quiproquo mocks the excesses of préciosité.
The refined speech and feeling of the 17th-century salons (Rambouillet from about 1608; Scudéry after 1650; the Carte de Tendre in Clélie). Satirised by Somaize (1660) and Molière.

cards.front: L'honnête homme and le bel esprit
