vocab.exampleEn: The alliteration on s imitates the whistling of the wind.

vocab.note: feminine (une assonance): a repeated vowel sound.
vocab.example: Une assonance en ou donne à la phrase sa douceur.
vocab.exampleEn: An assonance on ou gives the sentence its softness.

vocab.note: feminine (une euphonie). The t of a-t-il and the l' of si l'on are there for euphony.
vocab.example: Le t de « viendra-t-il » est là pour l'euphonie.
vocab.exampleEn: The t in "viendra-t-il" is there for euphony.

vocab.note: A harsh run of sounds in a sentence; also, everyday, a noisy confusion (la cacophonie des klaxons).
vocab.example: « Ton thé t'a-t-il ôté ta toux ? » est une cacophonie célèbre.
vocab.exampleEn: "Ton thé t'a-t-il ôté ta toux?" is a well-known cacophony.

vocab.note: masculine; same form in the plural; le hiatus is also found. Two vowels meeting, within a word or between words: il a été, il alla à Arles.
vocab.example: « Il alla à Arles » accumule les hiatus.
vocab.exampleEn: "Il alla à Arles" piles up hiatuses.

vocab.note: feminine (une asyndète): items or clauses side by side with no linking word (Il vint, il vit, il vainquit). The opposite, the repeated et, is la polysyndète.
vocab.example: L'asyndète accélère le récit.
vocab.exampleEn: Asyndeton speeds up the narrative.

vocab.note: Clauses placed side by side without subordination: Il pleuvait. Elle partit. The adjective is paratactique.
vocab.example: La parataxe donne à ce passage un ton sec et heurté.
vocab.exampleEn: Parataxis gives this passage a dry, jerky tone.

vocab.note: feminine (une hypotaxe): subordination, one clause depending on another (Comme il pleuvait, elle partit).
vocab.example: Proust est un maître de l'hypotaxe.
vocab.exampleEn: Proust is a master of hypotaxis.

vocab.note: A sentence built around a noun, without a conjugated verb: Silence. Puis un cri. Common in headlines, descriptions and stage directions.
vocab.example: Le texte s'ouvre sur une phrase nominale : « Novembre, déjà. »
vocab.exampleEn: The text opens with a verbless sentence: "November, already."

vocab.note: Same form in the feminine: une phrase ternaire, un rythme ternaire.
vocab.example: Le rythme ternaire donne à la phrase son ampleur.
vocab.exampleEn: The three-part rhythm gives the sentence its breadth.

vocab.note: Same form in the feminine. Also, in arguments, simplistic (un raisonnement binaire: everything is black or white).
vocab.example: Un rythme binaire équilibre les deux moitiés de la phrase.
vocab.exampleEn: A two-part rhythm balances the two halves of the sentence.

vocab.example: On admire la musicalité de sa prose plus que ses intrigues.
vocab.exampleEn: People admire the musicality of her prose more than her plots.

vocab.note: feminine chatoyante. Of fabric, colours, a style: changing with the light (des soies chatoyantes). The verb is chatoyer.
vocab.example: Les vitrines jetaient sur le trottoir des reflets chatoyants.
vocab.exampleEn: The shop windows cast shimmering reflections on the pavement.

vocab.note: Same form in the feminine. Literary: letting light through (un voile diaphane); of skin, very pale and delicate.
vocab.example: Une brume diaphane montait du fleuve.
vocab.exampleEn: A translucent mist rose from the river.

vocab.note: feminine blafarde. Pale and dull, usually of light or a face: la lumière blafarde des néons.
vocab.example: Les néons de la gare répandaient une lumière blafarde.
vocab.exampleEn: The station's neon lights gave off a pallid light.

vocab.note: Of sounds and atmospheres: soft, as if through felt (des pas feutrés, une ambiance feutrée). Le feutre is felt, or a felt-tip pen.
vocab.example: Dans la librairie, les voix devenaient feutrées.
vocab.exampleEn: In the bookshop, voices became hushed.

vocab.note: Same form in the feminine. From le crépuscule (B1 honors): la lumière crépusculaire. Figuratively, of an end or a decline (un régime crépusculaire).
vocab.example: La lumière crépusculaire adoucissait les façades.
vocab.exampleEn: The twilight softened the façades.

vocab.note: feminine mordorée. A warm brown with gold glints: des feuilles mordorées.
vocab.example: Le fleuve prenait des reflets mordorés.
vocab.exampleEn: The river took on bronze-gold glints.

forms.present: ruisselle/ruissèle, ruisselles/ruissèles, ruisselle/ruissèle, ruisselons, ruisselez, ruissellent/ruissèlent

vocab.note: Double l before a silent e: il ruisselle, il ruissellera; the 1990 recommendations also allow il ruissèle, il ruissèlera. Ruisseler de: les vitres ruisselaient de pluie. Mostly in the third person; no imperative drill.
vocab.example: La pluie ruisselait sur les pavés.
vocab.exampleEn: The rain streamed down the cobbles.

vocab.note: Regular. Of stars, lights, water. Mostly in the third person; no imperative drill.
vocab.example: Les premières étoiles scintillaient au-dessus des toits.
vocab.exampleEn: The first stars were twinkling above the roofs.

vocab.note: Rare outside the third person: les feuilles bruissent, la fontaine bruissait. Literary; no imperative drill. The noun is le bruissement.
vocab.example: Les platanes bruissaient doucement au-dessus du quai.
vocab.exampleEn: The plane trees rustled softly above the embankment.

vocab.note: A soft, confused sound of leaves, water, wings or voices.
vocab.example: On n'entendait que le bruissement de la fontaine.
vocab.exampleEn: All you could hear was the murmur of the fountain.

vocab.note: A heavy, sleepy numbness, of a person or a place: la ville sortait de sa torpeur.
vocab.example: Après la chaleur du jour, la rue sortait lentement de sa torpeur.
vocab.exampleEn: After the heat of the day, the street was slowly coming out of its torpor.

vocab.note: Usually plural. Dictionaries give it as masculine (un effluve); the feminine is also found in usage. Pleasant or not: des effluves de jasmin, des effluves d'essence.
vocab.example: Des effluves de pain chaud s'échappaient de la boulangerie.
vocab.exampleEn: Scents of warm bread drifted out of the bakery.

vocab.note: Usually of smoke (des volutes de fumée); in architecture, the spiral of an Ionic capital.
vocab.example: Des volutes de fumée montaient des cheminées.
vocab.exampleEn: Swirls of smoke rose from the chimneys.

vocab.note: A text written in the manner of an author, a genre or a period. The verb is pasticher.
vocab.example: Ce pastiche du roman-feuilleton a remporté le concours.
vocab.exampleEn: This pastiche of the serial novel won the competition.

vocab.note: Regular. Pasticher un auteur, un style. The noun is le pastiche.
vocab.example: Elle s'amuse à pasticher les circulaires de son ministère.
vocab.exampleEn: She has fun writing pastiches of her ministry's circulars.

vocab.note: Parodier is the verb.
vocab.example: Le sketch est une parodie des journaux télévisés.
vocab.exampleEn: The sketch is a send-up of the TV news.

vocab.note: Regular, with ii in the imparfait and the subjunctive: nous parodiions, que vous parodiiez. La parodie is the noun.
vocab.example: Les chansonniers parodiaient volontiers les discours officiels.
vocab.exampleEn: The cabaret singers were fond of parodying official speeches.

vocab.note: Also an adjective (un film burlesque, slapstick). In literature, a noble subject told in a low, familiar style.
vocab.example: Le burlesque fait parler les héros antiques comme des charretiers.
vocab.exampleEn: Burlesque makes ancient heroes talk like carters.

vocab.note: Plural héroï-comiques; same form in the feminine. A trivial subject told in the noble style of the epic.
vocab.example: Il raconte une dispute de voisins sur un ton héroï-comique.
vocab.exampleEn: He tells of a quarrel between neighbours in a mock-heroic tone.

vocab.note: feminine (une emphase). False friend: it means pomposity, not emphasis (emphasis = l'insistance, la mise en relief). Parler avec emphase = to speak pompously.
vocab.example: Il déclama son discours avec une emphase ridicule.
vocab.exampleEn: He declaimed his speech with ridiculous pomposity.

vocab.note: feminine grandiloquente. The noun is la grandiloquence.
vocab.example: Le préambule grandiloquent cache un projet très modeste.
vocab.exampleEn: The high-flown preamble hides a very modest project.

vocab.note: feminine ampoulée. Of style only: swollen with pompous words (un style ampoulé). Not related in sense to une ampoule (a bulb, a blister).
vocab.example: Son style ampoulé fatigue le lecteur dès la deuxième page.
vocab.exampleEn: His turgid style tires the reader by the second page.

vocab.note: feminine boursouflée. 1990 spelling boursoufflé. Of a style: inflated; of a face: puffy.
vocab.example: La critique trouva le roman boursouflé.
vocab.exampleEn: The critics found the novel overblown.

vocab.note: In style, an affected, over-refined manner. In art history, Mannerism (16th century). The adjective is maniéré (affected).
vocab.example: Le maniérisme de ses dernières nouvelles a lassé ses lecteurs.
vocab.exampleEn: The affectation of her last short stories wore out her readers.

vocab.note: A word or phrase someone repeats without noticing (du coup, en fait, voilà). A pastiche exaggerates an author's tics.
vocab.example: Le pasticheur repère d'abord les tics de langage de son modèle.
vocab.exampleEn: The pastiche writer first spots the pet phrases of the model.

vocab.note: A fake product or the offence of copying a protected work, mark or design (in French law, la contrefaçon includes copyright infringement).
vocab.example: La reproduction d'un roman sans autorisation est une contrefaçon.
vocab.exampleEn: Reproducing a novel without permission is an infringement.

vocab.note: Un, une faussaire. Someone who makes forgeries (paintings, documents, letters).
vocab.example: Le faussaire avait imité l'écriture de la romancière.
vocab.exampleEn: The forger had imitated the novelist's handwriting.

vocab.note: masculine; feminine l'imitatrice. On stage, someone who imitates famous voices.
vocab.example: L'imitateur reprend les tics de langage des ministres.
vocab.exampleEn: The impressionist copies the ministers' pet phrases.

vocab.note: In literature, retelling a noble work in a low style (the burlesque travestissement of Virgil). Also, dressing up or disguise.
vocab.example: Ce travestissement de l'Iliade fait des héros des marchands de bestiaux.
vocab.exampleEn: This travesty of the Iliad turns the heroes into cattle dealers.

vocab.note: A shared understanding between two people, often unspoken (un sourire de connivence). In a pastiche, the complicity between writer and reader who both know the model. Also complicity in wrongdoing (être de connivence avec).
vocab.example: Le pastiche repose sur une connivence avec le lecteur.
vocab.exampleEn: Pastiche relies on a shared understanding with the reader.

vocab.note: Un procédé stylistique = a stylistic device. Procéder à (C1) is the verb phrase.
vocab.example: L'accumulation est le procédé favori de l'héroï-comique.
vocab.exampleEn: Accumulation is the favourite device of the mock-heroic.

vocab.note: feminine (une outrance). À outrance = to excess (la publicité à outrance).
vocab.example: La parodie vit d'outrance ; le pastiche, de justesse.
vocab.exampleEn: Parody lives on overstatement; pastiche, on accuracy.

vocab.note: feminine outrancière. Excessive in words or behaviour: des propos outranciers.
vocab.example: Son imitation est volontairement outrancière.
vocab.exampleEn: Her imitation is deliberately over the top.

vocab.note: masculine (un anachronisme). In a pastiche, a modern word slipped into a period style, by mistake or for comic effect.
vocab.example: Le mot « parking » dans un pastiche de Rabelais est un anachronisme voulu.
vocab.exampleEn: The word "parking" in a pastiche of Rabelais is a deliberate anachronism.

meanings: mise en abyme (story within a story)
vocab.note: A work inside the work that mirrors it (a play within a play, a painting inside a painting). Also spelled la mise en abîme.
vocab.example: Le roman contient sa propre mise en abyme : un écrivain qui écrit ce roman.
vocab.exampleEn: The novel contains its own mise en abyme: a writer writing this novel.

vocab.note: Also a photograph (informal, or technical: a negative). The genre's clichés are the pastiche writer's raw material.
vocab.example: Le roman-feuilleton aligne les clichés : la nuit noire, le cri déchirant.
vocab.exampleEn: The serial novel lines up clichés: the pitch-dark night, the piercing scream.

vocab.note: feminine pompeuse. Same form in the masculine plural.
vocab.example: Le ton pompeux de la circulaire fit rire tout le service.
vocab.exampleEn: The pompous tone of the circular made the whole department laugh.

vocab.note: Same form in the feminine. Sweet and sentimental without force: une romance mièvre.
vocab.example: Les dialogues amoureux sont un peu mièvres.
vocab.exampleEn: The love scenes are a little soppy.

vocab.note: Le détournement d'un texte, d'un slogan, d'une affiche: reusing it to say something else. Also the hijacking of a plane and embezzlement (le détournement de fonds).
vocab.example: Le détournement d'un slogan publicitaire sert souvent la satire.
vocab.exampleEn: Subverting an advertising slogan often serves satire.

vocab.note: masculine (un alexandrin). Also an adjective: le vers alexandrin.
vocab.example: La plupart des tragédies classiques sont écrites en alexandrins.
vocab.exampleEn: Most classical tragedies are written in alexandrines.

vocab.note: masculine (un hémistiche). Each half of an alexandrine, six syllables on either side of the caesura.
vocab.example: Le second hémistiche répond au premier.
vocab.exampleEn: The second half-line answers the first.

vocab.note: The pause inside a line; in the classical alexandrine, after the sixth syllable.
vocab.example: La césure tombe après la sixième syllabe.
vocab.exampleEn: The caesura falls after the sixth syllable.

vocab.note: Pronouncing two touching vowels as two syllables (li-on, pas-si-on) to fill the count or slow the line.
vocab.example: La diérèse sur « passion » donne douze syllabes au vers.
vocab.exampleEn: The diaeresis on "passion" gives the line twelve syllables.

meanings: synaeresis (in verse: lion as one syllable)
vocab.note: Pronouncing two touching vowels as one syllable (lion in one), as in everyday speech.
vocab.example: Avec une synérèse, « hier » ne compte qu'une syllabe.
vocab.exampleEn: With a synaeresis, "hier" counts as only one syllable.

vocab.note: masculine (un enjambement). The sentence runs on past the end of the line; a short word carried over into the next line is un rejet.
vocab.example: L'enjambement prolonge la phrase au-delà du vers.
vocab.exampleEn: The enjambment carries the sentence beyond the line.

vocab.note: abba: the second rhyme is enclosed by the first. Usually in the plural: des rimes embrassées.
vocab.example: Les quatrains du sonnet classique ont des rimes embrassées.
vocab.exampleEn: The quatrains of the classical sonnet have enclosed rhymes.

vocab.note: abab. Usually in the plural: des rimes croisées. Rimes plates (aabb) pair the lines.
vocab.example: Ce quatrain est en rimes croisées.
vocab.exampleEn: This quatrain is in alternate rhyme.

vocab.note: A group of lines set off by a blank line. Le couplet is the word for a song.
vocab.example: Le poème compte quatre strophes.
vocab.exampleEn: The poem has four stanzas.

vocab.note: A stanza of four lines.
vocab.example: Le sonnet commence par deux quatrains.
vocab.exampleEn: The sonnet begins with two quatrains.

vocab.note: A stanza of three lines.
vocab.example: Les deux tercets apportent la chute du sonnet.
vocab.exampleEn: The two tercets bring the sonnet's twist.

vocab.note: Fourteen lines: two quatrains and two tercets.
vocab.example: Elle a écrit un sonnet en alexandrins.
vocab.exampleEn: She wrote a sonnet in alexandrines.

vocab.note: masculine (un aumônier); feminine l'aumônière for a lay chaplain. A priest attached to a prison, a hospital, a school or the army.
vocab.example: L'aumônier de la prison vient le voir malgré son refus.
vocab.exampleEn: The prison chaplain comes to see him in spite of his refusal.

meanings: closing speech (for the defence: la plaidoirie)
vocab.note: The lawyer's speech for the defence; the prosecutor's speech is le réquisitoire (C1 honors).
vocab.example: La plaidoirie de son avocat ne convainc pas les jurés.
vocab.exampleEn: His lawyer's closing speech doesn't convince the jurors.

vocab.note: feminine (une insolation). Attraper une insolation = to get sunstroke.
vocab.example: Sous ce soleil, il risque l'insolation.
vocab.exampleEn: Under that sun, he risks sunstroke.

vocab.note: An inquiry that re-examines an earlier one. Kamel Daoud's novel is Meursault, contre-enquête.
vocab.example: Le roman de Daoud se présente comme une contre-enquête.
vocab.exampleEn: Daoud's novel presents itself as a counter-investigation.

vocab.note: Formal for la peine de mort, abolished in France in 1981.
vocab.example: L'avocat général réclame la peine capitale.
vocab.exampleEn: The prosecutor calls for capital punishment.

vocab.note: feminine (une indifférence). The adjective is indifférent.
vocab.example: On lui reproche surtout son indifférence à l'enterrement.
vocab.exampleEn: Above all, he is blamed for his indifference at the funeral.

vocab.note: Emotional distance (avec détachement). Also a group of soldiers, or a civil servant's secondment.
vocab.example: Il raconte la scène avec un détachement troublant.
vocab.exampleEn: He tells the scene with a disturbing detachment.

vocab.note: Seeing things clearly, without illusions. The adjective is lucide.
vocab.example: Pour Camus, la lucidité est la première vertu de l'homme absurde.
vocab.exampleEn: For Camus, clear-sightedness is the first virtue of the absurd man.

vocab.note: The belief that what happens can't be avoided. The adjective is fataliste.
vocab.example: Son fatalisme exaspère son avocat.
vocab.exampleEn: His fatalism exasperates his lawyer.

vocab.note: masculine; feminine l'avocate générale. In a French cour d'assises (B2) the prosecution is represented by an avocat général (a magistrate, not a lawyer); le procureur is the general word.
vocab.example: L'avocat général a requis vingt ans de réclusion.
vocab.exampleEn: The prosecutor asked for twenty years' imprisonment.

vocab.note: feminine la jurée. Le jury (B2 honors) is the whole panel.
vocab.example: Les jurés se retirent pour délibérer.
vocab.exampleEn: The jurors withdraw to deliberate.

vocab.note: feminine. Accorder des circonstances atténuantes = to allow mitigating circumstances.
vocab.example: Le jury ne lui accorde pas de circonstances atténuantes.
vocab.exampleEn: The jury doesn't grant him mitigating circumstances.

vocab.note: feminine la bailleresse. Legal; in everyday French le propriétaire (A1 honors). Donner à bail = to let under a lease.
vocab.example: Le bailleur est tenu de remettre une quittance au locataire qui la demande.
vocab.exampleEn: The lessor must give a rent receipt to a tenant who asks for one.

vocab.note: feminine la preneuse. Legal; in everyday French le locataire (A1 honors).
vocab.example: Le preneur est tenu de payer le loyer aux termes convenus.
vocab.exampleEn: The lessee must pay the rent on the agreed dates.

meanings: other party (to a contract: le cocontractant)
vocab.note: feminine la cocontractante. Legal: each party is the other's cocontractant.
vocab.example: Chaque partie doit informer son cocontractant de tout changement d'adresse.
vocab.exampleEn: Each party must inform the other party of any change of address.

vocab.note: masculine (un alinéa). A paragraph of an article of law: l'article 22, alinéa 2. In typography, a new line or indent.
vocab.example: Le délai de restitution figure à l'alinéa 3 de l'article.
vocab.exampleEn: The time limit for return is in subparagraph 3 of the article.

vocab.note: Formal, legal: nonobstant toute clause contraire (whatever the contract says). + noun; nonobstant que + clause is archaic. Malgré and en dépit de (B2) are the everyday and neutral equivalents.
vocab.example: La majoration est due nonobstant toute clause contraire du bail.
vocab.exampleEn: The increase is owed notwithstanding any contrary clause in the lease.

vocab.note: masculine (un ayant droit); plural les ayants droit. Someone who holds a right through another person: an heir, a family member, a member of a social-security scheme.
vocab.example: Les ayants droit de l'auteur touchent les droits sur ses livres.
vocab.exampleEn: The author's rightful claimants receive the royalties on his books.

vocab.note: The body of court decisions. Une jurisprudence constante = a settled line of decisions. Not jurisprudence in the English sense of legal philosophy.
vocab.example: Selon une jurisprudence constante, le locataire ne répond pas de la vétusté.
vocab.exampleEn: According to settled case law, the tenant is not liable for wear due to age.

vocab.note: Un, une justiciable. Anyone who may come before the courts; the word used when talking about justice from the citizen's side.
vocab.example: Les décisions doivent être lisibles pour le justiciable.
vocab.exampleEn: Decisions must be readable for the people who come before the courts.

vocab.note: A court in general; le tribunal (B2) is one kind of juridiction, la cour d'appel another. Also a court's competence: relever de la juridiction de.
vocab.example: La juridiction compétente est celle du lieu où se trouve le logement.
vocab.exampleEn: The competent court is the one where the home is located.

vocab.note: Legal: débouter quelqu'un de sa demande (the person is the object; the claim follows de). A claim itself is rejetée. Regular -er verb; the imperative isn't used.
vocab.example: Le tribunal a débouté la locataire de sa demande de dommages et intérêts.
vocab.exampleEn: The court dismissed the tenant's claim for damages.

vocab.note: Legal; faire appel (B2) is the everyday phrase. Interjeter appel d'un jugement; the deadline is usually counted from the formal service of the judgment.
vocab.example: Le bailleur a interjeté appel du jugement dans le délai d'un mois.
vocab.exampleEn: The landlord lodged an appeal against the judgment within a month.

vocab.note: feminine la défenderesse. Civil cases; le prévenu (B2) is the defendant in a criminal court. The other side is le demandeur, la demanderesse.
vocab.example: Le défendeur conclut au rejet de toutes les demandes.
vocab.exampleEn: The respondent asks for all the claims to be rejected.

vocab.note: Statuer sur un litige, sur une demande. Formula: le tribunal, statuant publiquement … Regular -er verb; the imperative isn't used.
vocab.example: Le juge statuera sur la demande le mois prochain.
vocab.exampleEn: The judge will rule on the claim next month.

vocab.note: Plural les clauses résolutoires. The clause of a contract that ends it automatically if one party fails to meet an obligation (unpaid rent in a lease).
vocab.example: Le bail contient une clause résolutoire en cas de loyers impayés.
vocab.exampleEn: The lease contains a termination clause for unpaid rent.

meanings: free of charge (formal: à titre gracieux)
vocab.note: Formal; gratuitement is everyday. The opposite is à titre onéreux (for payment).
vocab.example: La cave est mise à disposition à titre gracieux.
vocab.exampleEn: The cellar is made available free of charge.

vocab.note: Legal: without anyone having to ask a judge. Le bail est résilié de plein droit.
vocab.example: La majoration s'applique de plein droit en cas de retard.
vocab.exampleEn: The increase applies automatically in case of delay.

meanings: at the end (of a text: in fine)
vocab.note: Latin, written without accents: l'article 22 in fine (the end of article 22). Loosely, and criticised by some, "in the end, ultimately".
vocab.example: La règle figure à l'article 22 in fine.
vocab.exampleEn: The rule is at the end of article 22.

vocab.note: Latin, written without accents: in fact, whatever the rules say. Its opposite is de jure (by law).
vocab.example: En gardant tout le dépôt, il a de facto fait payer les travaux à la locataire.
vocab.exampleEn: By keeping the whole deposit, he in fact made the tenant pay for the work.

vocab.note: feminine (une astreinte). A sum per day of delay that a court adds to an order until it is obeyed: sous astreinte de 20 euros par jour. In work French, being on call: être d'astreinte.
vocab.example: Le juge a ordonné la remise des documents sous astreinte.
vocab.exampleEn: The judge ordered the documents handed over, with a daily penalty for delay.

vocab.note: feminine caduque. Legal: no longer valid (une offre caduque); in general use, obsolete (un raisonnement caduc).
vocab.example: Faute de réponse dans le délai, l'offre est devenue caduque.
vocab.exampleEn: With no answer within the time limit, the offer lapsed.

vocab.note: Plural les voies de recours. Appeal and pourvoi en cassation are voies de recours. Le recours (B2) is a single appeal or recourse.
vocab.example: Le jugement indique les voies de recours possibles.
vocab.exampleEn: The judgment states the possible means of appeal.

vocab.note: feminine la requérante. The person who applies to a court, often by requête (written application).
vocab.example: La requérante demande la restitution de son dépôt de garantie.
vocab.exampleEn: The applicant asks for her deposit to be returned.

vocab.note: Plural les dépôts de garantie. The legal term; la caution (A1 honors) is the everyday word (and, strictly, also means a guarantor).
vocab.example: Le dépôt de garantie ne peut dépasser un mois de loyer pour un logement vide.
vocab.exampleEn: The security deposit can't exceed one month's rent for an unfurnished home.

vocab.note: The noun of résilier (B2 honors): la résiliation du bail, d'un abonnement.
vocab.example: La résiliation du contrat prend effet à la fin du mois.
vocab.exampleEn: The termination of the contract takes effect at the end of the month.

meanings: appeal to the Cour de cassation (pourvoi en cassation)
vocab.note: Plural les pourvois en cassation. The Cour de cassation checks only whether the law was applied correctly; it doesn't rehear the facts. Verb: se pourvoir en cassation.
vocab.example: Un jugement rendu en dernier ressort ne peut faire l'objet que d'un pourvoi en cassation.
vocab.exampleEn: A judgment given at final instance can only be challenged by an appeal to the Cour de cassation.

vocab.note: masculine, plural only (des dommages et intérêts élevés). Also written les dommages-intérêts.
vocab.example: Elle réclame 1 500 euros de dommages et intérêts.
vocab.exampleEn: She is claiming 1,500 euros in damages.

vocab.note: The wires above an electrified railway line; trains take their power from it through the pantographe.
vocab.example: La ligne n'a pas de caténaire : les trains roulent au diesel.
vocab.exampleEn: The line has no overhead wires: the trains run on diesel.

vocab.note: The folding arm on the roof of an electric train or tram that touches the caténaire.
vocab.example: Le pantographe se lève dès que le train entre sur la section électrifiée.
vocab.exampleEn: The pantograph rises as soon as the train enters the electrified section.

vocab.note: Every vehicle that runs on the rails. Le matériel = equipment; a material is un matériau.
vocab.example: Le matériel roulant doit être homologué avant la mise en service.
vocab.exampleEn: The rolling stock must be approved before entry into service.

vocab.note: The vehicle of a train that carries the motors (TGV: deux motrices encadrent les voitures).
vocab.example: La pile à combustible est installée sur le toit de la motrice.
vocab.exampleEn: The fuel cell is mounted on the roof of the power car.

vocab.note: A train that runs as one fixed unit (une rame de métro, de TGV). Also an oar, and a ream of paper.
vocab.example: Deux rames à hydrogène circulent sur la ligne.
vocab.exampleEn: Two hydrogen trainsets run on the line.

vocab.note: masculine (un aiguillage). The movable rails that send a train from one track to another; figuratively, a choice of direction (une erreur d'aiguillage).
vocab.example: Sur une voie unique, les trains se croisent grâce aux aiguillages des gares.
vocab.exampleEn: On a single track, trains pass each other thanks to the points at the stations.

vocab.note: Plural les voies uniques. A line with one track for both directions; trains pass only at stations or loops. À voie unique (adjectival).
vocab.example: La ligne est à voie unique sur soixante kilomètres.
vocab.exampleEn: The line is single-track for sixty kilometres.

vocab.note: Railway signalling (the system that keeps trains apart), and road or building signage.
vocab.example: Aucune modification de la signalisation n'est nécessaire.
vocab.exampleEn: No change to the signalling is needed.

vocab.note: Plural les piles à combustible. It produces electricity from a fuel (hydrogen) as long as fuel is supplied; une batterie (A2) stores electricity.
vocab.example: La pile à combustible convertit l'hydrogène en électricité.
vocab.exampleEn: The fuel cell converts hydrogen into electricity.

vocab.note: feminine (une électrolyse). Splitting a substance, such as water, with an electric current.
vocab.example: L'hydrogène est produit par électrolyse de l'eau.
vocab.exampleEn: The hydrogen is produced by electrolysis of water.

vocab.note: masculine (l'hydrogène vert = hydrogen made with renewable electricity).
vocab.example: Le train consomme environ un quart de kilo d'hydrogène par kilomètre.
vocab.exampleEn: The train uses about a quarter of a kilo of hydrogen per kilometre.

vocab.note: Efficiency of a machine (le rendement d'un moteur), yield of a crop, return on an investment. Not la performance.
vocab.example: Le rendement global de la chaîne hydrogène est d'environ 26 %.
vocab.exampleEn: The overall efficiency of the hydrogen chain is about 26%.

vocab.note: In railways, what moves the train: la traction électrique, thermique (diesel), hydrogène.
vocab.example: La ligne est exploitée en traction thermique.
vocab.exampleEn: The line is run with diesel traction.

vocab.note: Building and running a model (often a computer model) of a system. Verb: modéliser.
vocab.example: La modélisation de l'exploitation porte sur trois scénarios.
vocab.exampleEn: The modelling of the line's operation covers three scenarios.

vocab.note: Same form in the feminine. A result another team can obtain again by repeating the protocol.
vocab.example: Une expérience doit être reproductible pour être publiée.
vocab.exampleEn: An experiment must be reproducible to be published.

vocab.note: The quality of being reproductible; the aim of the méthodes section of an article.
vocab.example: La faible dispersion des mesures confirme la reproductibilité du protocole.
vocab.exampleEn: The small spread of the measurements confirms that the protocol is reproducible.

vocab.note: A quantity that varies in a model or an experiment. Also an adjective (variable: changing).
vocab.example: La variable déterminante est le prix de l'hydrogène.
vocab.exampleEn: The decisive variable is the price of hydrogen.

vocab.note: A quantity fixed for a given case in a model; loosely, any factor to take into account.
vocab.example: Les autres paramètres n'ont qu'une influence marginale.
vocab.exampleEn: The other parameters have only a marginal influence.

vocab.note: In physics, any measurable quantity (speed, mass, energy); also size, and greatness (la grandeur d'un pays).
vocab.example: La vitesse est une grandeur qui se mesure en mètres par seconde.
vocab.exampleEn: Speed is a quantity measured in metres per second.

vocab.note: masculine; plural les ordres de grandeur. A size to the nearest power of ten; du même ordre de grandeur = comparable.
vocab.example: L'écart est du même ordre de grandeur que dans les études précédentes.
vocab.exampleEn: The gap is of the same order of magnitude as in earlier studies.

meanings: state of the art (in research: l'état de l'art)
vocab.note: masculine; also l'état des connaissances. In a research paper, the review of what is already known; also the most advanced level of a technology.
vocab.example: L'introduction présente l'état de l'art sur les trains à hydrogène.
vocab.exampleEn: The introduction reviews the literature on hydrogen trains.

vocab.note: Plural les bancs d'essai. Equipment for testing a machine outside its real conditions; figuratively, a test (le banc d'essai des smartphones).
vocab.example: La chaîne de traction a été testée sur banc d'essai.
vocab.exampleEn: The traction system was tested on a test bench.

vocab.note: Plural les mises en service. The moment a line, a train or a machine starts working for real (mettre en service).
vocab.example: La mise en service commerciale est prévue pour 2029.
vocab.exampleEn: Commercial entry into service is planned for 2029.

vocab.note: feminine (une homologation). Official approval by an authority that a vehicle or product meets the rules. Verb: homologuer.
vocab.example: L'homologation du matériel exige un an d'essais en ligne.
vocab.exampleEn: Approval of the trains requires a year of trials on the line.

vocab.note: A device that measures a quantity (temperature, pressure, speed) and turns it into a signal.
vocab.example: Le banc d'essai est équipé de 48 capteurs.
vocab.exampleEn: The test bench is fitted with 48 sensors.

vocab.note: Also le freinage par récupération. Braking that turns the train's motion back into electricity, stored or sent back to the line.
vocab.example: Le freinage régénératif récupère une partie de l'énergie de traction.
vocab.exampleEn: Regenerative braking recovers part of the traction energy.

vocab.note: A general and lasting fall in prices; the opposite of l'inflation (B2).
vocab.example: La déflation pousse les ménages à reporter leurs achats.
vocab.exampleEn: Deflation pushes households to put off their purchases.

meanings: key interest rate (central bank: taux directeur)
vocab.note: Plural les taux directeurs. The rates a central bank sets for lending to banks and for their deposits with it; in the euro area, set by the BCE.
vocab.example: La BCE a relevé ses taux directeurs pour freiner l'inflation.
vocab.exampleEn: The ECB raised its key interest rates to curb inflation.

vocab.note: Run by a central bank (la BCE for the euro area), mainly through its taux directeurs. Fiscal policy is la politique budgétaire.
vocab.example: La politique monétaire vise la stabilité des prix.
vocab.exampleEn: Monetary policy aims at price stability.

vocab.note: The cash a firm actually has, or its cash management. Une entreprise rentable peut manquer de trésorerie.
vocab.example: La trésorerie ne couvrait plus que trois semaines d'activité.
vocab.exampleEn: The cash only covered three more weeks of business.

vocab.note: masculine (un endettement excessif). Endetté (B2) is the adjective; le surendettement (B2) is the over-indebtedness of a household.
vocab.example: L'endettement de l'entreprise a doublé en deux ans.
vocab.exampleEn: The company's debt load doubled in two years.

vocab.note: masculine or feminine: un, une actionnaire. Owner of shares (les actions) in a company.
vocab.example: Les actionnaires familiaux ont renoncé à tout dividende.
vocab.exampleEn: The family shareholders gave up any dividend.

vocab.note: masculine. The share of the profit paid to shareholders: verser un dividende.
vocab.example: L'entreprise ne versera pas de dividende cette année.
vocab.exampleEn: The company won't pay a dividend this year.

vocab.note: Plural les capitalisations boursières. The share price times the number of shares.
vocab.example: Sa capitalisation boursière a fondu de moitié en un an.
vocab.exampleEn: Its market capitalisation halved in a year.

meanings: listing (on the stock exchange: la cotation)
vocab.note: A firm's listing on the stock exchange, or the quoted price of a share; la cotation est suspendue = trading is suspended.
vocab.example: La cotation du titre a été suspendue avant l'annonce.
vocab.exampleEn: Trading in the share was suspended before the announcement.

meanings: income statement (profit and loss: compte de résultat)
vocab.note: Plural les comptes de résultat. Income (les produits) and costs (les charges) over a financial year, and the result. Le bilan is the balance sheet.
vocab.example: Le compte de résultat affiche une perte de 4,2 millions d'euros.
vocab.exampleEn: The income statement shows a loss of 4.2 million euros.

vocab.note: Plural les levées de fonds. Raising capital from investors: boucler une levée de fonds auprès d'un fonds d'investissement.
vocab.example: La start-up a bouclé une levée de fonds de 12 millions d'euros.
vocab.exampleEn: The start-up closed a 12-million-euro fundraising round.

vocab.note: feminine (une introduction en Bourse); plural les introductions en Bourse. Bourse takes a capital letter for the stock exchange.
vocab.example: La direction a renoncé à l'introduction en Bourse.
vocab.exampleEn: The management gave up the stock market flotation.

vocab.note: Two companies become one (une fusion-acquisition: a merger or takeover). Also melting (le point de fusion) and nuclear fusion.
vocab.example: Le groupe propose une fusion plutôt qu'un rachat.
vocab.exampleEn: The group is proposing a merger rather than a buyout.

vocab.note: feminine (une acquisition). One company buys another; une fusion joins two into one.
vocab.example: L'acquisition de la PME par le groupe a été approuvée.
vocab.exampleEn: The group's acquisition of the small firm was approved.

vocab.note: Plural les redressements judiciaires. A court procedure for a firm in cessation des paiements whose recovery is possible: an observation period, then a plan, a sale or liquidation.
vocab.example: Le tribunal a placé l'entreprise en redressement judiciaire.
vocab.exampleEn: The court placed the company in receivership.

vocab.note: Plural les liquidations judiciaires. Ordered when recovery is clearly impossible: the assets are sold and the firm closes.
vocab.example: Faute de repreneur, la liquidation judiciaire a été prononcée.
vocab.exampleEn: With no buyer, compulsory liquidation was ordered.

vocab.note: Everyday: faire faillite = to go bankrupt. French law speaks of redressement or liquidation judiciaire. Figuratively, failure (la faillite d'une politique).
vocab.example: Sans cet accord, l'entreprise aurait fait faillite.
vocab.exampleEn: Without this agreement, the company would have gone bankrupt.

vocab.note: feminine la créancière. The person or firm that is owed money; the opposite is le débiteur.
vocab.example: Les créanciers ont accepté d'étaler les remboursements.
vocab.exampleEn: The creditors agreed to spread the repayments.

vocab.note: feminine la débitrice. The person or firm that owes money; the opposite is le créancier.
vocab.example: Nos débiteurs ont payé avec retard.
vocab.exampleEn: Our debtors paid late.

vocab.note: The ability to pay one's debts; the adjective is solvable.
vocab.example: Les agences de notation évaluent la solvabilité des États.
vocab.exampleEn: Rating agencies assess the creditworthiness of states.

vocab.note: masculine (un excédent). Le déficit (C1) is the opposite. Adjective: excédentaire (la balance commerciale est excédentaire).
vocab.example: Le budget de la région présente un léger excédent.
vocab.exampleEn: The region's budget shows a small surplus.

vocab.note: feminine conjoncturelle. Tied to the current state of the economy; la conjoncture (C1) is the noun. Opposite: structurel.
vocab.example: Le recul des ventes est conjoncturel : il devrait s'inverser.
vocab.exampleEn: The fall in sales is cyclical: it should reverse.

vocab.note: feminine structurelle. Tied to how an economy or a firm is built; the opposite of conjoncturel (un déficit structurel).
vocab.example: Le chômage structurel ne baisse pas avec la reprise.
vocab.exampleEn: Structural unemployment doesn't fall with the recovery.

vocab.note: feminine (une agence de notation); plural les agences de notation. A downgrade (une dégradation de la note) makes borrowing dearer.
vocab.example: Une agence de notation a abaissé la note de l'entreprise.
vocab.exampleEn: A rating agency lowered the company's rating.

vocab.note: Plural les plus-values. The gain made by selling an asset for more than it cost; the loss is une moins-value. Also value added (une plus-value pour l'équipe).
vocab.example: Le fonds espérait réaliser une plus-value importante.
vocab.exampleEn: The fund hoped to make a large capital gain.

vocab.note: From German. A sudden collapse of share prices: le krach de 1929.
vocab.example: Le krach de 1929 a ouvert une longue crise.
vocab.exampleEn: The crash of 1929 opened a long crisis.

vocab.note: feminine (une essence). In philosophy, what makes a thing what it is; in everyday French, petrol (faire le plein d'essence).
vocab.example: Le philosophe cherche l'essence de la justice.
vocab.exampleEn: The philosopher looks for the essence of justice.

vocab.note: feminine (une ontologie). The study of being: what exists, and how. Adjective: ontologique.
vocab.example: L'ontologie se demande ce qui existe vraiment.
vocab.exampleEn: Ontology asks what really exists.

vocab.note: feminine (une épistémologie). The theory of knowledge; in French especially the philosophy of science. Un, une épistémologue.
vocab.example: L'épistémologie étudie la manière dont la science établit ses résultats.
vocab.exampleEn: Epistemology studies how science establishes its results.

vocab.note: A model or framework of thought. Un changement de paradigme, after Thomas Kuhn (1962).
vocab.example: La découverte a provoqué un changement de paradigme.
vocab.exampleEn: The discovery caused a paradigm shift.

vocab.note: feminine (une aporie). A problem with no way out in the terms set; adjective aporétique.
vocab.example: Le débat semble aboutir à une aporie.
vocab.exampleEn: The debate seems to end in an impasse.

vocab.note: Reasoning through opposition (thesis, antithesis, a new position). Also an adjective: une démarche dialectique. Le plan dialectique (C1) is the essay plan.
vocab.example: La dialectique permet de dépasser une opposition apparente.
vocab.exampleEn: Dialectic makes it possible to go beyond an apparent opposition.

vocab.note: A starting point one asks the reader to grant, unproved and open to dispute. Verb: postuler.
vocab.example: L'idée de progrès repose sur un postulat.
vocab.exampleEn: The idea of progress rests on a postulate.

vocab.note: masculine (un axiome). A starting point accepted without proof, often as self-evident; in mathematics, a basic rule of a system.
vocab.example: Pour Condorcet, la perfectibilité est presque un axiome.
vocab.exampleEn: For Condorcet, perfectibility is almost an axiom.

vocab.note: A statement that says the same thing twice and so says nothing; adjective tautologique. La redondance (C1) is any needless repetition.
vocab.example: « Le progrès, c'est aller de l'avant » est une tautologie.
vocab.exampleEn: "Progress is moving forward" is a tautology.

vocab.note: feminine (une antinomie). A contradiction between two claims that each seem justified.
vocab.example: Il y a une antinomie entre liberté totale et égalité parfaite.
vocab.exampleEn: There is a contradiction between total freedom and perfect equality.

vocab.note: The view that everything has causes that make it necessary; opposed to le libre arbitre (C1).
vocab.example: Un déterminisme strict laisse peu de place à la liberté.
vocab.exampleEn: A strict determinism leaves little room for freedom.

vocab.note: masculine (un empirisme). All knowledge comes from experience; opposed to le rationalisme.
vocab.example: L'empirisme fait de l'expérience la source de toute connaissance.
vocab.exampleEn: Empiricism makes experience the source of all knowledge.

vocab.note: Reason can know some truths without experience; opposed to l'empirisme.
vocab.example: Le rationalisme accorde à la raison un pouvoir propre.
vocab.exampleEn: Rationalism gives reason a power of its own.

vocab.note: masculine (un universalisme). Some values hold for every human being; opposed to le relativisme (C1 honors).
vocab.example: L'universalisme défend des droits valables pour tous.
vocab.exampleEn: Universalism defends rights that hold for everyone.

vocab.note: feminine transcendante. Beyond the world or experience; spelt -ant. Transcendantal (Kant) is a different word. Opposite: immanent.
vocab.example: Pour certains croyants, la morale a une source transcendante.
vocab.exampleEn: For some believers, morality has a transcendent source.

vocab.note: feminine immanente. Within, belonging to the thing itself; the opposite of transcendant. Not imminent (about to happen).
vocab.example: Il voit dans l'histoire une logique immanente.
vocab.exampleEn: He sees an immanent logic in history.

vocab.note: feminine inhérente. Inhérent à: part of the nature of (les risques inhérents à toute innovation).
vocab.example: Ce risque est inhérent à toute recherche.
vocab.exampleEn: This risk is inherent in all research.

vocab.note: Same form in the feminine. In itself, independent of anything else; the opposite is extrinsèque.
vocab.example: La valeur intrinsèque d'une œuvre ne dépend pas de son prix.
vocab.exampleEn: The intrinsic value of a work doesn't depend on its price.

vocab.note: Received opinion, what everyone accepts without examining it; slightly pejorative.
vocab.example: L'essai prend le contre-pied de la doxa.
vocab.exampleEn: The essay goes against received opinion.

vocab.note: Plural les lieux communs. An idea everyone repeats; slightly pejorative.
vocab.example: Dire que le progrès est une illusion est devenu un lieu commun.
vocab.exampleEn: Saying that progress is an illusion has become a commonplace.

vocab.note: feminine (une altérité). The fact that the other is not me, and the respect it calls for.
vocab.example: La rencontre de l'altérité oblige à se décentrer.
vocab.exampleEn: Meeting otherness forces us to shift our point of view.

vocab.note: The condition of a limited being, especially in time: humans die, and know it.
vocab.example: La conscience de notre finitude donne du prix au temps.
vocab.exampleEn: Awareness of our finitude makes time precious.

vocab.note: masculine. The philosophy associated with Sartre: human beings have no nature given in advance and make themselves by their choices.
vocab.example: L'existentialisme a marqué l'après-guerre.
vocab.exampleEn: Existentialism left its mark on the post-war years.

vocab.note: The view that no value or meaning holds; un nihilisme de salon = a fashionable, comfortable nihilism.
vocab.example: Le nihilisme refuse toute valeur.
vocab.exampleEn: Nihilism rejects all values.

vocab.note: Philosophy: matter comes first, mind depends on it; opposed to l'idéalisme. Everyday: caring about possessions.
vocab.example: Le matérialisme explique la pensée par le cerveau.
vocab.exampleEn: Materialism explains thought by the brain.

vocab.note: masculine (un idéalisme). Philosophy: ideas or mind come first; opposed to le matérialisme. Everyday: having ideals.
vocab.example: L'idéalisme fait de l'esprit la réalité première.
vocab.exampleEn: Idealism makes mind the primary reality.

vocab.note: Plural les charges utiles. What a launcher carries: satellites, a probe, a capsule.
vocab.example: La charge utile est protégée par la coiffe pendant la traversée de l'atmosphère.
vocab.exampleEn: The payload is protected by the fairing as it passes through the atmosphere.

vocab.note: Plural les pas de tir.
vocab.example: Le lanceur a été transféré sur le pas de tir la veille du lancement.
vocab.exampleEn: The launcher was moved to the launch pad the day before the launch.

vocab.note: Plural les mises à feu. Lighting a rocket's engines; also firing a charge.
vocab.example: La mise à feu du moteur principal a lieu sept secondes avant le décollage.
vocab.exampleEn: The main engine is ignited seven seconds before liftoff.

vocab.note: Plural les mises en orbite. Verb phrase: mettre en orbite.
vocab.example: La mise en orbite du satellite a été confirmée.
vocab.exampleEn: The satellite's placing in orbit has been confirmed.

vocab.note: feminine (l'orbite, B2). About 36,000 km above the equator; a satellite there seems still from the ground.
vocab.example: Les satellites de télévision sont placés en orbite géostationnaire.
vocab.exampleEn: Television satellites are placed in geostationary orbit.

vocab.note: Un, une spationaute. A French coinage used mainly for French and European crews; l'astronaute (B2) is more common and is FranceTerme's headword, with spationaute as its synonym.
vocab.example: La spationaute a passé six mois à bord de la station.
vocab.exampleEn: The astronaut spent six months on board the station.

vocab.note: The nose cone that protects the payload, then is jettisoned. In everyday French, a traditional headdress (la coiffe bretonne).
vocab.example: Le largage de la coiffe intervient au-dessus de cent kilomètres.
vocab.exampleEn: The fairing is jettisoned above a hundred kilometres.

vocab.note: The force of a rocket's engines; also a push, and a surge (une poussée de fièvre).
vocab.example: La poussée des propulseurs diminue après deux minutes.
vocab.exampleEn: The boosters' thrust falls after two minutes.

vocab.note: masculine (un amarrage). Docking in space; mooring a boat (amarrer).
vocab.example: L'amarrage à la station est intervenu à 10 h 08.
vocab.exampleEn: Docking with the station took place at 10.08.

vocab.note: Plural les rentrées atmosphériques. The return through the atmosphere, when the capsule heats up and slows down.
vocab.example: La rentrée atmosphérique est la phase la plus délicate du retour.
vocab.exampleEn: Atmospheric re-entry is the most delicate phase of the return.

vocab.note: Usually plural: les débris spatiaux (dead satellites, spent stages, fragments).
vocab.example: Les débris spatiaux menacent les satellites en activité.
vocab.exampleEn: Space debris threatens working satellites.

vocab.note: Gathering scattered rules into one ordered, written code. Verb: codifier.
vocab.example: La codification de 1804 a unifié le droit civil français.
vocab.exampleEn: The codification of 1804 unified French civil law.

vocab.note: Plural les droits coutumiers. Before 1804, the law of northern France, based on local customs (la coutume, C1 honors) written down over time.
vocab.example: Le nord de la France relevait du droit coutumier.
vocab.exampleEn: Northern France came under customary law.

vocab.note: feminine la législatrice. In legal writing, the abstract author of the law: le législateur a voulu protéger le locataire.
vocab.example: Le législateur ne peut pas tout prévoir.
vocab.exampleEn: The lawmaker can't foresee everything.

vocab.note: masculine (un usufruit). The right to use a thing owned by another and take its income, while keeping it intact; the owner keeps la nue-propriété. Holder: l'usufruitier.
vocab.example: Le conjoint survivant a reçu l'usufruit de la maison.
vocab.exampleEn: The surviving spouse received the usufruct of the house.

vocab.note: The legal link between a child and its parents; also the line of descent of ideas (la filiation d'une doctrine).
vocab.example: Depuis 2005, le Code ne distingue plus filiation légitime et filiation naturelle.
vocab.exampleEn: Since 2005 the Code no longer distinguishes legitimate and natural parentage.

vocab.note: Plural les régimes matrimoniaux. The rules on who owns what in a marriage; the default is la communauté réduite aux acquêts.
vocab.example: Ils ont choisi leur régime matrimonial chez le notaire.
vocab.exampleEn: They chose their marriage settlement at the notary's.

vocab.note: feminine. Exercised by both parents in the child's interest; it replaced la puissance paternelle in 1970.
vocab.example: Les deux parents exercent en commun l'autorité parentale.
vocab.exampleEn: Both parents exercise parental authority jointly.

vocab.note: Historical; replaced by l'autorité parentale by the law of 4 June 1970.
vocab.example: Le Code de 1804 reposait sur la puissance paternelle.
vocab.exampleEn: The Code of 1804 rested on paternal authority.

vocab.note: Un, une juriste. Anyone trained in law (an in-house lawyer, a legal scholar); l'avocat is a lawyer admitted to the bar.
vocab.example: Une juriste d'entreprise relit tous les contrats.
vocab.exampleEn: An in-house lawyer reads every contract.

vocab.note: The act that makes a law official and enforceable; promulguer (B2 honors) is the verb.
vocab.example: La promulgation du Code civil date du 21 mars 1804.
vocab.exampleEn: The Code civil was promulgated on 21 March 1804.

vocab.note: The law of ancient Rome, as compiled under Justinian; the basis of le droit écrit in southern France.
vocab.example: L'usufruit vient du droit romain.
vocab.exampleEn: Usufruct comes from Roman law.

vocab.note: feminine (une essencerie). Senegal, also heard elsewhere in West Africa; recorded in a Dakar press glossary of Senegalese French. In France: la station-service. Recognition: reviewed French to English only.
vocab.example: On fait le plein à l'essencerie avant de quitter Dakar.
vocab.exampleEn: We fill up at the petrol station before leaving Dakar.

vocab.note: Côte d'Ivoire: an open-air eating place, often with music (aller au maquis). In France le maquis is scrubland, and the armed Resistance of 1940-1944 that hid in it. Plural unchanged. Recognition: reviewed French to English only.
vocab.example: Ce soir, on dîne au maquis du quartier.
vocab.exampleEn: Tonight we're having dinner at the local open-air restaurant.

meanings: tea circle (Mali, Burkina Faso: le grin)
group of friends who meet over tea
vocab.note: Mali and Burkina Faso: a group of friends, usually young men, who meet every day to talk over tea; also the place where they meet. Labelled Mali in a Wiktionnaire-based dictionary; used in the same sense in reports from Burkina Faso. Recognition: reviewed French to English only.
vocab.example: Après le travail, il passe deux heures à son grin.
vocab.exampleEn: After work he spends two hours with his tea circle.

vocab.note: Plural les taxis-brousse. A shared car or minibus between towns in Africa (and Madagascar) that leaves when it is full. Known and used in France to describe African transport.
vocab.example: Le taxi-brousse n'est parti qu'une fois plein.
vocab.exampleEn: The bush taxi only left once it was full.

vocab.note: Standard French. Each member pays the same sum regularly and each in turn takes the whole pot; very common in Africa.
vocab.example: Grâce à la tontine, elle a pu ouvrir sa boutique.
vocab.exampleEn: Thanks to the savings club she was able to open her shop.

vocab.note: A long, wide, flowing robe worn by men and women in West Africa; un grand boubou is the formal version.
vocab.example: Il portait un grand boubou bleu pour la fête.
vocab.exampleEn: He wore a long blue boubou for the celebration.

vocab.note: A length of printed cloth wrapped as a skirt (un pagne wax); in older French also a loincloth.
vocab.example: Elle m'a offert un pagne aux couleurs vives.
vocab.exampleEn: She gave me a brightly coloured wrapper.

forms.present: ambiance, ambiances, ambiance, ambiançons, ambiancez, ambiancent

vocab.note: West and Central Africa, informal; from l'ambiance (in Congolese and Ivorian French: a party). Also s'ambiancer (to have fun). A -cer verb: nous ambiançons, j'ambiançais. Recognition: reviewed French to English only.
vocab.example: Le DJ a ambiancé toute la terrasse.
vocab.exampleEn: The DJ got the whole terrace going.

meanings: life and soul of the party (ambianceur)
vocab.note: masculine (un ambianceur); feminine l'ambianceuse. West and Central Africa, informal; the OQLF's GDT notes it was created in Africa and is common in Ivorian French. Recognition: reviewed French to English only.
vocab.example: Sans notre ambianceur, la fête serait triste.
vocab.exampleEn: Without our party man the party would be dull.

vocab.note: Informal and judgemental: a man's mistress (literally the second office). Common in Central Africa (the two Congos) and elsewhere in West and Central Africa. Historical in France: le Deuxième Bureau, the old military intelligence service. Recognition only: reviewed French to English.
vocab.example: Tout le quartier savait qu'il avait un deuxième bureau.
vocab.exampleEn: The whole neighbourhood knew he had a mistress.

meanings: to give a present to (Africa: cadeauter)
vocab.note: Africa (Larousse labels it Africa), especially West Africa: cadeauter quelqu'un. Regular -er verb; the participle agrees with a direct object before it: elle m'a cadeautée. In France: offrir un cadeau à quelqu'un. Recognition: reviewed French to English only.
vocab.example: Mon oncle a cadeauté tous ses neveux à Noël.
vocab.exampleEn: My uncle gave all his nephews presents at Christmas.

vocab.note: Standard French, especially frequent in African usage and press: la cherté de la vie (the high cost of living).
vocab.example: Les syndicats dénoncent la cherté de la vie.
vocab.exampleEn: The unions protest against the high cost of living.

vocab.note: Common in Africa and Québec; in France it is often felt as old-fashioned or regional, and actuellement or en ce moment is usual. Recognition: reviewed French to English only.
vocab.example: Le directeur n'est pas là présentement.
vocab.exampleEn: The director isn't here at the moment.

vocab.note: Senegal: a stall or small restaurant selling grilled mutton, usually traced to débiter (to cut up meat), probably through Wolof dibi (grilled meat); recorded in a Dakar press glossary. Recognition: reviewed French to English only.
vocab.example: On a mangé du mouton grillé dans une dibiterie de Dakar.
vocab.exampleEn: We ate grilled mutton at a grilled-meat stall in Dakar.

vocab.note: A Muslim holy man and teacher, often the head of a religious community in West Africa; in some countries also a healer or a fortune teller (and, in France, ads for fortune tellers use the word).
vocab.example: Il rend visite chaque année au marabout de sa famille.
vocab.exampleEn: Every year he visits his family's marabout.

vocab.note: Usually feminine and often plural (des palabres = endless talk); l'arbre à palabres is the tree under which a village debates. Masculine in some African usage.
vocab.example: La palabre a duré tout l'après-midi sous le grand arbre.
vocab.exampleEn: The village discussion went on all afternoon under the big tree.

vocab.note: A language used between speakers of different first languages: Wolof in Senegal, Lingala in Kinshasa, French in many towns.
vocab.example: À Dakar, le wolof sert de langue véhiculaire.
vocab.exampleEn: In Dakar, Wolof serves as a lingua franca.

vocab.note: The language of a community, learned at home and used among its own speakers. Compare la langue véhiculaire.
vocab.example: Chaque village parle sa langue vernaculaire.
vocab.exampleEn: Each village speaks its vernacular.

vocab.note: The use of several languages by a person or a society. Le bilinguisme (B1 honors) is the use of two.
vocab.example: Le plurilinguisme est la règle dans les villes africaines.
vocab.exampleEn: Multilingualism is the rule in African cities.

vocab.note: Côte d'Ivoire's urban youth language, born in the streets of Abidjan and now heard in music and advertising. Recognition only: reviewed French to English.
vocab.example: Le slogan de la publicité est en nouchi.
vocab.exampleEn: The advertising slogan is in Nouchi.

vocab.note: Cameroon's mixed urban slang, built from French, English, Cameroon Pidgin English and local languages. Recognition only: reviewed French to English.
vocab.example: Les jeunes de Douala parlent souvent camfranglais entre eux.
vocab.exampleEn: Young people in Douala often speak Camfranglais to each other.

vocab.note: The language; also an adjective (la langue wolof, la musique wolof) and the people (les Wolofs). The main lingua franca of Senegal.
vocab.example: Mon chauffeur passe du wolof au français sans s'en apercevoir.
vocab.exampleEn: My driver switches from Wolof to French without noticing.

vocab.note: masculine (un africanisme). A word or use of French typical of Africa: essencerie, cadeauter, gâter (to break down). Also the study of Africa.
vocab.example: Le dictionnaire signale cet africanisme par une marque géographique.
vocab.exampleEn: The dictionary marks this Africanism with a regional label.

vocab.note: A status a state gives to languages it recognises as belonging to the country; it may or may not make them official.
vocab.example: Le Sénégal reconnaît plusieurs langues nationales.
vocab.exampleEn: Senegal recognises several national languages.

vocab.note: Côte d'Ivoire (Abidjan): a crowded minibus linking the districts, with a young conductor (l'apprenti) at the door. Recognition: reviewed French to English only.
vocab.example: Le gbaka était tellement bondé qu'on ne pouvait plus bouger.
vocab.exampleEn: The minibus was so packed you couldn't move.

vocab.note: Côte d'Ivoire (Abidjan): a shared taxi on a fixed route at a fixed fare; also written wôrô-wôrô. Plural les woro-woro or les woro-woros: both are found. Recognition: reviewed French to English only.
vocab.example: Pour aller au marché, prends un woro-woro.
vocab.exampleEn: To get to the market, take a shared taxi.

vocab.note: feminine (une alternance codique). Switching between languages within a conversation or a sentence; the English code-switching is also used in French.
vocab.example: L'alternance codique est une compétence des locuteurs bilingues.
vocab.exampleEn: Code-switching is a skill of bilingual speakers.

vocab.note: Informal, from Maghrebi Arabic (village, country). For families from the Maghreb, le bled is also the home country (partir au bled). Neutral: un village perdu, le pays d'origine.
vocab.example: Ils habitent un bled sans gare ni boulangerie.
vocab.exampleEn: They live in the back of beyond, with no station and no bakery.

meanings: six of one, half a dozen of the other
vocab.note: Informal and invariable, from Arabic: c'est kif-kif. Neutral: c'est pareil.
vocab.example: Le train ou le car, c'est kif-kif : on arrivera en retard.
vocab.exampleEn: Train or coach, same difference: we'll be late.

vocab.note: Informal, from Arabic (a chief's household and camp). Toute la smala = the whole family. Neutral: la famille.
vocab.example: Il est venu avec toute sa smala.
vocab.exampleEn: He came with his whole tribe.

vocab.note: Informal, from Arabic (blessing): avoir la baraka = to be lucky. La chance (A2) is neutral.
vocab.example: Il n'a même pas été blessé : il a la baraka.
vocab.exampleEn: He wasn't even hurt: he has luck on his side.

vocab.note: Informal, from Arabic (leader); also a gang leader. Pronounced in two syllables: ca-ïd. Faire le caïd = to act tough.
vocab.example: Arrête de faire le caïd devant tes copains.
vocab.exampleEn: Stop acting the big shot in front of your friends.

vocab.note: Informal, from Maghrebi Arabic (a little): un chouïa de sel. Pronounced chou-ya. Neutral: un peu.
vocab.example: Tu peux baisser la musique un chouïa ?
vocab.exampleEn: Can you turn the music down a tad?

vocab.note: Informal, from Maghrebi Arabic (dog); the final bs sounds like ps. Plural unchanged. Le chien (A1) is neutral.
vocab.example: Le clebs du voisin aboie toute la nuit.
vocab.exampleEn: The neighbour's mutt barks all night.

vocab.note: Algeria: a young unemployed man, usually explained from Algerian Arabic hit (wall): one who spends the day leaning against a wall. Recognition: reviewed French to English only.
vocab.example: Dans les années 1990, beaucoup de diplômés étaient devenus hittistes.
vocab.exampleEn: In the 1990s many graduates had become young unemployed men hanging around.

vocab.note: A soup of meat, vegetables and spices from the Maghreb, often served during Ramadan; spelling varies (chorba, chorbah, chourba).
vocab.example: Ma grand-mère prépare une chorba pour toute la famille.
vocab.exampleEn: My grandmother is making a chorba for the whole family.

vocab.note: The communities of a people living outside their country of origin: la diaspora maghrébine, la diaspora sénégalaise.
vocab.example: La diaspora envoie chaque année des sommes importantes au pays.
vocab.exampleEn: The diaspora sends large sums home every year.

vocab.note: masculine or feminine (un arabophone, une arabophone); also an adjective (les pays arabophones). Compare francophone, créolophone.
vocab.example: Les arabophones du Maghreb parlent la darija au quotidien.
vocab.exampleEn: Arabic speakers in the Maghreb use darija every day.

vocab.note: masculine (l'amazigh); also an adjective (la culture amazighe). Le tamazight is also used for the language. Official in Morocco (2011) and Algeria (2016).
vocab.example: Elle apprend à écrire l'amazigh.
vocab.exampleEn: She is learning to write Amazigh.

vocab.note: The spoken Arabic of daily life in the Maghreb, different in each country and different from standard Arabic.
vocab.example: La publicité marocaine utilise de plus en plus la darija.
vocab.exampleEn: Moroccan advertising uses darija more and more.

vocab.note: Plural les pieds-noirs; feminine la pied-noir (une pied-noir); also an adjective (la cuisine pied-noir). The Europeans of French Algeria, most of whom left in 1962.
vocab.example: Son grand-père, pied-noir, a quitté Oran en 1962.
vocab.exampleEn: His grandfather, a pied-noir, left Oran in 1962.

meanings: harki (Algerian auxiliary in the French army)
vocab.note: Plural les harkis. An Algerian who served as an auxiliary in the French army during the war of independence (1954-1962). A sensitive historical subject: use the word factually.
vocab.example: Les harkis arrivés en France ont souvent vécu dans des camps.
vocab.exampleEn: The harkis who reached France often lived in camps.

vocab.note: feminine (une arabisation). Policies replacing French with Arabic in schools and administration after independence.
vocab.example: L'arabisation de l'école a commencé dans les années 1960.
vocab.exampleEn: The Arabisation of schools began in the 1960s.

vocab.note: The language in which pupils are taught, which may differ from their home language.
vocab.example: Dans ce pays, la langue de scolarisation a changé deux fois en cinquante ans.
vocab.exampleEn: In that country, the language of schooling has changed twice in fifty years.

vocab.note: A borrowed word still felt as foreign, often printed in italics and explained. Compare l'emprunt (B1 honors).
vocab.example: Dans cet article, le mot chorba est encore un xénisme.
vocab.exampleEn: In this article, the word chorba is still a foreign word.

vocab.note: feminine (une interférence). In linguistics, a feature of one language carried into another (a pronunciation, a construction); also interference in general.
vocab.example: Dire je suis chaud pour j'ai chaud est une interférence de l'anglais.
vocab.exampleEn: Saying je suis chaud for j'ai chaud is interference from English.

vocab.note: In linguistics, an earlier language whose traces survive in the one that replaced it: le substrat gaulois du français.
vocab.example: On retrouve un substrat amazigh dans l'arabe du Maghreb.
vocab.exampleEn: An Amazigh substrate can be found in the Arabic of the Maghreb.

vocab.note: The popular French of the pieds-noirs of Algeria, coloured by Spanish, Italian, Maltese and Arabic; descriptions differ on its exact mix and on the origin of its name.
vocab.example: Son oncle racontait encore des histoires en pataouète.
vocab.exampleEn: His uncle still told stories in pataouète.

vocab.note: Informal, from Arabic; feminine maboule. Neutral: fou, folle.
vocab.example: Il faut être maboul pour conduire aussi vite.
vocab.exampleEn: You have to be nuts to drive that fast.

vocab.note: The old walled town of a North African city: la médina de Fès, de Tunis.
vocab.example: On s'est perdus dans les ruelles de la médina.
vocab.exampleEn: We got lost in the alleys of the medina.

vocab.note: Belonging to two cultures at once; also avoir une double culture.
vocab.example: Sa double culture est une richesse dans son métier.
vocab.exampleEn: Her dual culture is an asset in her job.

vocab.note: A souk: a market in the Arab world (neutral). Informal: c'est le souk = it's chaos.
vocab.example: Range ta chambre, c'est le souk !
vocab.exampleEn: Tidy your room, it's chaos!

vocab.note: Québec, informal: ma blonde = my girlfriend (whatever her hair colour). In France: la petite amie (A2), la copine. In France la blonde is a blonde woman. Recognition: reviewed French to English only.
vocab.example: Il est parti en vacances avec sa blonde.
vocab.exampleEn: He went on holiday with his girlfriend.

vocab.note: Québec, informal: to freak out, with joy or panic (j'capote !). In France capoter = to overturn (a car, a boat) or to fall through (a deal). Regular -er verb. Recognition: reviewed French to English only.
vocab.example: Quand elle a vu le prix, elle a capoté.
vocab.exampleEn: When she saw the price, she freaked out.

vocab.note: Québec, informal: to fool around, to waste time; niaiser quelqu'un = to tease, to pull someone's leg (Arrête de niaiser !). Regular -er verb. Recognition: reviewed French to English only.
vocab.example: Arrête de niaiser, on a du travail.
vocab.exampleEn: Stop fooling around, we've got work to do.

vocab.note: Québec: to chat, without malice. In France jaser = to gossip (Ça va faire jaser). Regular -er verb. Recognition: reviewed French to English only.
vocab.example: On a jasé jusqu'à minuit sur la galerie.
vocab.exampleEn: We chatted on the porch until midnight.

vocab.note: Québec, informal: to bother, to pester (Mon voisin m'achale). Neutral: embêter, déranger. Regular -er verb. Recognition: reviewed French to English only.
vocab.example: Les maringouins nous ont achalés toute la soirée.
vocab.exampleEn: The mosquitoes bothered us all evening.

vocab.note: Québec, informal, after pas: pas pantoute = pas du tout (from pas en tout). Recognition: reviewed French to English only.
vocab.example: J'ai pas aimé ce film pantoute.
vocab.exampleEn: I didn't like that film one bit.

vocab.note: Québec, informal: a dollar; also spelt la piastre (from the old Spanish coin). Neutral: le dollar. Recognition: reviewed French to English only.
vocab.example: Ça m'a coûté vingt piasses.
vocab.exampleEn: It cost me twenty bucks.

vocab.note: feminine dispendieuse. Common and neutral in Québec (un loyer dispendieux); in France it exists but is usually described as formal, and cher is usual. Recognition: reviewed French to English only.
vocab.example: Les loyers sont devenus dispendieux à Montréal.
vocab.exampleEn: Rents have become pricey in Montreal.

vocab.note: Québec: collège d'enseignement général et professionnel, between secondary school and university; also written Cégep or CÉGEP. Recognition: reviewed French to English only.
vocab.example: Elle étudie les sciences au cégep.
vocab.exampleEn: She is studying science at CEGEP.

vocab.note: A Québec dish of chips (fries) with cheese curds and gravy, now known far beyond Québec.
vocab.example: Après le match, on a mangé une poutine.
vocab.exampleEn: After the game we had a poutine.

vocab.note: feminine (une infolettre). Québec: the French term recommended for newsletter; in France la lettre d'information or, informally, la newsletter. Recognition: reviewed French to English only.
vocab.example: Abonnez-vous à notre infolettre.
vocab.exampleEn: Subscribe to our newsletter.

vocab.note: Québec: online chat, from clavier + bavardage, proposed by the OQLF in 1997. In France the official term is le dialogue en ligne; most people say le chat or le tchat. Recognition: reviewed French to English only.
vocab.example: Le service client répond par clavardage.
vocab.exampleEn: Customer service answers by online chat.

vocab.note: Québec: to chat online (OQLF term); regular -er verb. In France: chatter, tchatter (informal). Recognition: reviewed French to English only.
vocab.example: On a clavardé une heure avant de se rencontrer.
vocab.exampleEn: We chatted online for an hour before we met.

vocab.note: The working-class French of Montreal, named after the way cheval sounds in it; a literary language since Michel Tremblay's Les Belles-sœurs (1968).
vocab.example: La pièce est écrite en joual.
vocab.exampleEn: The play is written in joual.

vocab.note: The French of many young Acadians in and around Moncton (New Brunswick), mixed with English words and structures. Recognition of the variety only.
vocab.example: Au café, elle a entendu parler chiac.
vocab.exampleEn: At the café she heard chiac being spoken.

vocab.note: Québec: a swear word built on a word of Catholic worship (the words themselves are explained in the lesson, never listed). Standard French: a coronation (le sacre de Napoléon). Recognition: reviewed French to English only.
vocab.example: Il a lâché un sacre en se cognant le pied.
vocab.exampleEn: He let out a swear word when he stubbed his toe.

vocab.note: feminine (en Acadie). The French colony of the Maritimes, and today the francophone communities of New Brunswick, Nova Scotia and Prince Edward Island.
vocab.example: L'Acadie n'est pas une province, mais une communauté.
vocab.exampleEn: Acadia isn't a province but a community.

vocab.note: feminine acadienne; with a capital as a noun: les Acadiens.
vocab.example: La musique acadienne est très vivante à Moncton.
vocab.exampleEn: Acadian music is very lively in Moncton.

vocab.note: The deportation of the Acadians by the British, which began in 1755 and lasted for years.
vocab.example: Le Grand Dérangement a dispersé les Acadiens jusqu'en Louisiane.
vocab.exampleEn: The Great Upheaval scattered the Acadians as far as Louisiana.

vocab.note: The French of the Cajuns of Louisiana, descendants of deported Acadians (Cajun comes from Acadien); also an adjective (la cuisine cajun, invariable or cajune).
vocab.example: Son grand-père parlait encore le cajun.
vocab.exampleEn: His grandfather still spoke Cajun French.

vocab.note: Québec: the ordinary word for a mobile phone (informal le cell). Le portable (A2) in France. Recognition: reviewed French to English only.
vocab.example: J'ai oublié mon cellulaire dans l'auto.
vocab.exampleEn: I left my cell phone in the car.

vocab.note: Québec: to hitchhike (from the raised thumb). In France: faire du stop, faire de l'auto-stop. Recognition: reviewed French to English only.
vocab.example: Ils ont fait du pouce jusqu'à Tadoussac.
vocab.exampleEn: They hitchhiked to Tadoussac.

meanings: to be fed up (Québec, informal: être tanné)
vocab.note: Québec, informal: être tanné (de quelque chose) = to be fed up (with it); feminine tannée. Neutral: en avoir assez. Recognition: reviewed French to English only.
vocab.example: Je suis tannée de l'hiver.
vocab.exampleEn: I'm fed up with winter.

vocab.note: Québec, informal: worn out, battered (of a person or a thing); feminine maganée. Neutral: abîmé, épuisé. Recognition: reviewed French to English only.
vocab.example: Après le déménagement, j'étais complètement magané.
vocab.exampleEn: After the move I was completely worn out.

vocab.note: The reforms of the 1960s that built a modern Québec state and took schools, health care and social services out of the Church's hands.
vocab.example: La Révolution tranquille a transformé l'école québécoise.
vocab.exampleEn: The Quiet Revolution transformed Québec schools.

vocab.note: Québec: the standard word for a ferry (le traversier Québec-Lévis). In France: le ferry, le bac. Recognition: reviewed French to English only.
vocab.example: On a pris le traversier pour traverser le fleuve.
vocab.exampleEn: We took the ferry across the river.

vocab.note: Belgium, informal: a student party, a night out drinking. Recognition: reviewed French to English only.
vocab.example: Il y a une guindaille au cercle jeudi soir.
vocab.exampleEn: There's a student party at the club on Thursday night.

vocab.note: Belgium: the weeks of intensive study before exams (être en blocus). Elsewhere a blockade; in France also a protest blocking a school. Plural unchanged. Recognition: reviewed French to English only.
vocab.example: Pendant le blocus, elle ne sort plus de son kot.
vocab.exampleEn: During the study period she doesn't leave her room.

vocab.note: Belgium: a folder or ring binder. In France: le classeur, la chemise. Recognition: reviewed French to English only.
vocab.example: Range tes notes de cours dans ta farde.
vocab.exampleEn: Put your lecture notes in your folder.

vocab.note: Belgium: the tuition fee paid to a university or college. In France: les frais d'inscription. Recognition: reviewed French to English only.
vocab.example: Les étudiants manifestent contre la hausse du minerval.
vocab.exampleEn: Students are protesting against the rise in tuition fees.

vocab.note: Belgium, administrative: endéans les trente jours = within thirty days. In France: dans un délai de, sous. Recognition: reviewed French to English only.
vocab.example: Veuillez répondre endéans les quinze jours.
vocab.exampleEn: Please reply within fifteen days.

vocab.note: Belgium, also northern France: a door handle or latch. In most of France: la poignée (de porte). Recognition: reviewed French to English only.
vocab.example: Appuie sur la clenche, la porte est ouverte.
vocab.exampleEn: Push the handle down, the door's open.

vocab.note: Belgium and northern France (also reported in Switzerland); l'endive in most of France. Des chicons au gratin is a Belgian classic. Recognition: reviewed French to English only.
vocab.example: Ce soir, on mange des chicons au gratin.
vocab.exampleEn: Tonight we're having endives au gratin.

vocab.note: Belgium: a commuter (from la navette, the shuttle); feminine la navetteuse. Recognition: reviewed French to English only.
vocab.example: Des milliers de navetteurs prennent le train pour Bruxelles.
vocab.exampleEn: Thousands of commuters take the train to Brussels.

vocab.note: Switzerland, informal: clutter, a mess (Quel cheni !); also spelt chenit. Recognition: reviewed French to English only.
vocab.example: Range ce cheni avant que tes grands-parents arrivent.
vocab.exampleEn: Tidy up this mess before your grandparents arrive.

vocab.note: Switzerland: a paper or plastic carrier bag. Elsewhere un cornet is a cone (un cornet de glace, de frites). Recognition: reviewed French to English only.
vocab.example: Vous voulez un cornet pour vos achats ?
vocab.exampleEn: Would you like a bag for your shopping?

vocab.note: Switzerland, informal: faire la poutze = to give the place a thorough clean (from German putzen); the verb is poutzer. Recognition: reviewed French to English only.
vocab.example: Samedi, on fait la poutze dans tout l'appartement.
vocab.exampleEn: On Saturday we're giving the whole flat a big clean.

vocab.note: Switzerland (Vaud, for example): upper secondary school; in Geneva the same school is le collège. Elsewhere a gym. Recognition: reviewed French to English only.
vocab.example: Ma fille entre au gymnase l'an prochain.
vocab.exampleEn: My daughter starts upper secondary school next year.

vocab.note: Switzerland: the school-leaving exam that opens university (informally la matu), like the French baccalauréat; also maturity in general. Recognition: reviewed French to English only.
vocab.example: Il a réussi sa maturité avec mention.
vocab.exampleEn: He passed his school-leaving exam with distinction.

vocab.note: feminine. Switzerland: 100,000 citizens can sign to put a change to the federal constitution to the vote (within eighteen months).
vocab.example: L'initiative populaire a recueilli plus de cent mille signatures.
vocab.exampleEn: The popular initiative collected more than a hundred thousand signatures.

vocab.note: Switzerland has twenty-six cantons, each with its own constitution and parliament; in France a canton is an electoral district.
