vocab.example: Chaque canton a ses propres écoles.
vocab.exampleEn: Each canton has its own schools.

vocab.note: feminine cantonale; masculine plural cantonaux: les impôts cantonaux.
vocab.example: Le parlement cantonal a voté le budget.
vocab.exampleEn: The cantonal parliament has voted the budget.

vocab.note: feminine romande: la Suisse romande, la presse romande; les Romands (noun) are the French-speaking Swiss.
vocab.example: Les journaux romands ont commenté la votation.
vocab.exampleEn: The French-speaking Swiss papers commented on the vote.

vocab.note: masculine (un échevin); feminine l'échevine. Belgium: a member of the commune's executive, each in charge of an area, working with the bourgmestre; roughly the French adjoint au maire. Recognition: reviewed French to English only.
vocab.example: L'échevine des travaux a inauguré la nouvelle rue.
vocab.exampleEn: The alderwoman for public works opened the new street.

vocab.note: The written standard shared by the whole francophone world: international news, treaties, textbooks.
vocab.example: Les journalistes de tous les pays écrivent un français de référence.
vocab.exampleEn: Journalists from every country write reference French.

vocab.note: feminine. Speakers' feeling that their own French is not good French.
vocab.example: L'insécurité linguistique pousse certains à cacher leur accent.
vocab.exampleEn: Linguistic insecurity drives some people to hide their accent.

vocab.note: Same form in the masculine and feminine: une langue pluricentrique, with several standard centres.
vocab.example: L'anglais est une langue pluricentrique, et le français le devient.
vocab.exampleEn: English is a pluricentric language, and French is becoming one.

vocab.note: In linguistics, any form of a language shared by a group (le français de Belgique est une variété du français); also variety in general.
vocab.example: Aucune variété du français n'est meilleure qu'une autre.
vocab.exampleEn: No variety of French is better than another.

vocab.note: Same form in the masculine and feminine: une norme endogène, set from inside a community. Opposite: exogène.
vocab.example: Le Québec a développé une norme endogène.
vocab.exampleEn: Québec has developed an endogenous norm.

vocab.note: Same form in the masculine and feminine: une norme exogène, imported from outside. Opposite: endogène.
vocab.example: Longtemps, la norme était exogène : elle venait de Paris.
vocab.exampleEn: For a long time the norm was exogenous: it came from Paris.

meanings: glottophobia (prejudice against an accent or language)
vocab.note: A term proposed by the sociolinguist Philippe Blanchet, set out in his book Discriminations : combattre la glottophobie (2016).
vocab.example: Se moquer d'un accent en entretien d'embauche, c'est de la glottophobie.
vocab.exampleEn: Mocking an accent in a job interview is glottophobia.

vocab.note: A word, meaning or construction typical of one region: septante, le cornet, présentement. Also, in politics, regionalism.
vocab.example: Ce dictionnaire marque chaque régionalisme par un pays.
vocab.exampleEn: This dictionary marks each regionalism with a country.

vocab.note: The language (a Mande language) and, with a capital, the people (les Malinkés); also an adjective (un prince malinké).
vocab.example: Kourouma fait entendre le malinké sous son français.
vocab.exampleEn: Kourouma lets Malinke be heard beneath his French.

vocab.note: The office and territory of a traditional chief.
vocab.example: La chefferie de Togobala n'a plus aucun pouvoir réel.
vocab.exampleEn: The chieftaincy of Togobala no longer has any real power.

vocab.note: The only party allowed in a state, and the system built on it.
vocab.example: Après l'indépendance, le parti unique contrôle tout.
vocab.exampleEn: After independence the single party controls everything.

vocab.note: feminine. Replacing colonial staff, models or forms with African ones, in administration as in culture and language.
vocab.example: L'africanisation des cadres a suivi l'indépendance.
vocab.exampleEn: The Africanisation of senior staff followed independence.

vocab.note: A line of rulers from the same family.
vocab.example: Fama est le dernier héritier de sa dynastie.
vocab.exampleEn: Fama is the last heir of his dynasty.

vocab.note: Infertility of a person or couple; also, figuratively, barrenness (la stérilité d'un débat).
vocab.example: Dans le roman, la stérilité du couple annonce la fin d'une lignée.
vocab.exampleEn: In the novel, the couple's infertility foreshadows the end of a line.

vocab.note: An object believed to have protective or magical power; also a lucky charm (un objet fétiche).
vocab.example: Salimata essaie tous les fétiches pour avoir un enfant.
vocab.exampleEn: Salimata tries every charm to have a child.

vocab.note: masculine (un enfant-soldat), also feminine for a girl (une enfant-soldat); plural les enfants-soldats.
vocab.example: Le narrateur d'Allah n'est pas obligé est un enfant-soldat.
vocab.exampleEn: The narrator of Allah n'est pas obligé is a child soldier.

vocab.note: A colonial settler; the feminine la colone is rare. Le colonialisme is the system.
vocab.example: Fama a combattu les colons en espérant retrouver son pouvoir.
vocab.exampleEn: Fama fought the settlers in the hope of getting his power back.

vocab.note: feminine. In literature, a text that draws on two cultures or languages at once.
vocab.example: La critique souligne l'hybridité de son écriture.
vocab.exampleEn: Critics stress the hybridity of his writing.

vocab.note: The Caribbean identity defined in Éloge de la créolité (Bernabé, Chamoiseau, Confiant, 1989): a mixed identity centred on the creole language.
vocab.example: Les auteurs de la créolité refusent de choisir entre l'Europe et l'Afrique.
vocab.exampleEn: The writers of Creoleness refuse to choose between Europe and Africa.

vocab.note: Édouard Glissant's word for the open, unfinished mixing of cultures in contact; in linguistics, the birth of a creole.
vocab.example: Pour Glissant, le monde entier entre en créolisation.
vocab.exampleEn: For Glissant, the whole world is undergoing creolisation.

vocab.note: Same form in the masculine and feminine; also a noun: les créolophones (Creole speakers).
vocab.example: La Martinique est une île créolophone et francophone.
vocab.exampleEn: Martinique is a Creole-speaking and French-speaking island.

vocab.note: A simplified contact language with no native speakers; compare le créole (B1 honors), which has them.
vocab.example: Un pidgin sert surtout au commerce.
vocab.exampleEn: A pidgin is used mainly for trade.

vocab.note: Two varieties in one society with different roles: a high one (school, law) and a low one (home, friends).
vocab.example: Haïti est un exemple classique de diglossie.
vocab.exampleEn: Haiti is a classic example of diglossia.

vocab.note: The escape of enslaved people from the plantation, alone or in free communities (les marrons).
vocab.example: Le marronnage était une forme de résistance à l'esclavage.
vocab.exampleEn: Marronage was a form of resistance to slavery.

vocab.note: masculine (l'esclavage est aboli). L'esclave (enslaved person) is the person.
vocab.example: L'esclavage a été aboli dans les colonies françaises en 1848.
vocab.exampleEn: Slavery was abolished in the French colonies in 1848.

vocab.note: feminine (une abolition): l'abolition de l'esclavage (1848 in the French colonies), l'abolition de la peine de mort.
vocab.example: L'abolition est commémorée chaque année dans les départements d'outre-mer.
vocab.exampleEn: Abolition is commemorated every year in the overseas departments.

vocab.note: A large colonial farm (sugar, coffee, cotton) worked by enslaved people; also any planting.
vocab.example: Les créoles sont nés sur les plantations.
vocab.exampleEn: The creoles were born on the plantations.

vocab.note: The language that supplies most of a creole's vocabulary: French for Haitian Creole.
vocab.example: Le français est la langue lexificatrice du créole haïtien.
vocab.exampleEn: French is the lexifier of Haitian Creole.

vocab.example: Survolez d'abord les titres et les sources de chaque document.
vocab.exampleEn: First skim the titles and sources of each document.
vocab.note: Regular -er verb. survoler un texte, a question (to skim, to touch on lightly); also literal: l'avion survole les Alpes.

vocab.example: Un survol de dix minutes suffit pour repérer les documents utiles.
vocab.exampleEn: A ten-minute skim is enough to spot the useful documents.
vocab.note: le survol du dossier: the first quick read of the paratext; also a flight over (le survol de Paris).

vocab.example: La partialité de ce blog n'est pas un défaut caché : il appartient à un fabricant.
vocab.exampleEn: This blog's bias is no hidden flaw: it belongs to a manufacturer.
vocab.note: The noun of partial (C1); the opposite is l'impartialité.

vocab.example: J'ai écarté le document 3, qui ne servait pas mon sujet.
vocab.exampleEn: I set aside document 3, which didn't serve my subject.
vocab.note: Regular -er verb. écarter une hypothèse (to rule out); s'écarter du sujet (to stray from the subject).

vocab.example: La hiérarchisation des arguments décide de l'ordre du plan.
vocab.exampleEn: Ranking the arguments decides the order of the plan.
vocab.note: hiérarchiser (B2 honors) is the verb. Aspirated h, as in la hiérarchie: la hiérarchisation, never l'hiérarchisation.

vocab.example: Le balayage permet de retrouver vite les chiffres dont on a besoin.
vocab.exampleEn: Scanning lets you quickly find the figures you need.
vocab.note: le balayage d'un texte: running your eyes over it for one piece of information; also sweeping (with a broom).

vocab.example: Le repérage des mots clés se fait crayon en main.
vocab.exampleEn: Spotting the keywords is done pencil in hand.
vocab.note: From repérer (to spot). In film, faire des repérages: to scout locations.

vocab.example: La légende de l'infographie précise que les chiffres datent de 2025.
vocab.exampleEn: The infographic's caption says the figures date from 2025.
vocab.note: The text under a picture (caption) or the key of a chart or map; also a legend (story).

vocab.example: L'infographie compare la durée de vie de six appareils.
vocab.exampleEn: The infographic compares the lifespan of six appliances.
vocab.note: feminine (une infographie)

vocab.example: Une bonne contextualisation dit d'où vient le document et quand il a paru.
vocab.exampleEn: Good contextualisation says where the document comes from and when it appeared.

vocab.example: L'obsolescence programmée est un délit en France depuis 2015.
vocab.exampleEn: Planned obsolescence has been an offence in France since 2015.
vocab.note: feminine (une obsolescence)

vocab.example: La réparabilité d'un téléphone dépend du prix de ses pièces.
vocab.exampleEn: A phone's repairability depends on the price of its parts.

vocab.example: L'indice de réparabilité est affiché sur l'étiquette depuis 2021.
vocab.exampleEn: The repairability index has been shown on the label since 2021.
vocab.note: masculine (un indice). France, from 1 January 2021: a mark out of 10 shown on some electrical products; replaced in 2025 by l'indice de durabilité for televisions and washing machines.

vocab.example: Elle a acheté un ordinateur reconditionné, garanti un an.
vocab.exampleEn: She bought a refurbished computer with a one-year guarantee.
vocab.note: feminine reconditionnée. Also a noun: le reconditionné (refurbished goods as a market).

vocab.example: Le réemploi d'un meuble évite d'en fabriquer un neuf.
vocab.exampleEn: Reusing a piece of furniture avoids making a new one.
vocab.note: réutiliser (A2 honors) is the verb. In waste law, le réemploi is using a product again for the same purpose.

vocab.example: Le fabricant ne vend plus de pièces détachées pour ce modèle.
vocab.exampleEn: The manufacturer no longer sells spare parts for this model.
vocab.note: plural les pièces détachées

vocab.example: L'auteur oppose la sobriété au consumérisme.
vocab.exampleEn: The author contrasts restraint with consumerism.
vocab.note: Two senses: a society built on buying (the usual sense in debate) and, older, the defence of consumers' interests.

vocab.example: Les rasoirs jetables finissent à la poubelle au bout d'une semaine.
vocab.exampleEn: Disposable razors end up in the bin after a week.
vocab.note: feminine jetable (same form)

vocab.example: L'indice de durabilité note aussi la solidité de l'appareil.
vocab.exampleEn: The durability index also rates how sturdy the appliance is.
vocab.note: Of an object: how long it lasts; of a policy: sustainability (le développement durable).

vocab.example: L'économie circulaire cherche à garder les objets en usage le plus longtemps possible.
vocab.exampleEn: The circular economy tries to keep objects in use as long as possible.
vocab.note: feminine (une économie)

vocab.example: La durée de vie moyenne d'un lave-linge dépasse dix ans.
vocab.exampleEn: The average lifespan of a washing machine is over ten years.

vocab.example: Grâce au bonus réparation, la facture a baissé de quelques dizaines d'euros.
vocab.exampleEn: Thanks to the repair bonus, the bill went down by a few dozen euros.
vocab.note: France, since 15 December 2022: a discount on the repair of an electrical or electronic appliance by a labelled repairer, paid by the producers' eco-organisations. The amounts have changed over time.

vocab.example: Le réparateur a changé la batterie en vingt minutes.
vocab.exampleEn: The repairer changed the battery in twenty minutes.
vocab.note: feminine la réparatrice

vocab.example: Le rayon électroménager propose désormais des appareils reconditionnés.
vocab.exampleEn: The household-appliance department now offers refurbished machines.
vocab.note: masculine (le gros électroménager: washing machines, fridges; le petit électroménager: kettles, toasters). Also an adjective: un appareil électroménager.

vocab.example: L'écoconception commence par des vis plutôt que de la colle.
vocab.exampleEn: Eco-design starts with screws rather than glue.
vocab.note: feminine (une écoconception)

vocab.example: Une part des déchets électroniques part encore à l'étranger.
vocab.exampleEn: Some electronic waste is still shipped abroad.
vocab.note: plural les déchets électroniques; the official term is les déchets d'équipements électriques et électroniques (DEEE).

vocab.example: Le surtitre « Mobilité » situe l'article dans la rubrique.
vocab.exampleEn: The strapline "Mobility" places the article in its section.
vocab.note: The short line above the headline that gives the topic or the place.

vocab.example: Un intertitre tous les trois paragraphes aide le lecteur pressé.
vocab.exampleEn: A subheading every three paragraphs helps the hurried reader.
vocab.note: masculine (un intertitre)

vocab.example: Son billet d'humeur sur les trottinettes a fait rire toute la rédaction.
vocab.exampleEn: Her opinion column on scooters made the whole newsroom laugh.
vocab.note: plural les billets d'humeur. Short, personal, often ironic; signed by one writer, unlike the éditorial.

vocab.example: Les embouteillages des vacances sont un marronnier de l'été.
vocab.exampleEn: Holiday traffic jams are a summer evergreen story.
vocab.note: Press: a story that comes back every year at the same date (back to school, the first heatwave). Also a horse-chestnut tree.

vocab.example: Le chapô résume l'article en deux phrases.
vocab.exampleEn: The standfirst sums up the article in two sentences.
vocab.note: Press spelling of le chapeau (A1: hat): the bold paragraph under the headline. Both spellings are found; journalists write chapô.

vocab.example: La titraille doit donner envie de lire sans trahir l'article.
vocab.exampleEn: The headings must make people want to read without betraying the article.
vocab.note: The whole set of titles of an article: surtitre, titre, sous-titre, chapô, intertitres.

vocab.example: Un titre accrocheur promet ; l'article doit tenir la promesse.
vocab.exampleEn: A catchy headline makes a promise; the article must keep it.
vocab.note: plural les titres accrocheurs

vocab.example: Les chiffres clés sont dans un encadré, à droite de l'article.
vocab.exampleEn: The key figures are in a box to the right of the article.
vocab.note: masculine (un encadré): a boxed text beside an article (figures, a definition, a portrait).

vocab.example: Le bandeau de la une annonce le supplément du week-end.
vocab.exampleEn: The front-page banner announces the weekend supplement.
vocab.note: A strip across the top of a page or a screen (a breaking-news banner); also a headband.

vocab.example: L'accident n'a eu droit qu'à un filet en page six.
vocab.exampleEn: The accident got only a short item on page six.
vocab.note: Press: an item of a few lines; also a net, a fillet (of fish or meat) and a thin line (typography).

vocab.example: Tu as lu ce qu'ils racontent dans ton canard ?
vocab.exampleEn: Have you read what they're saying in that rag of yours?
vocab.note: Informal for a newspaper, often affectionate rather than rude (Le Canard enchaîné takes its name from it). Also a duck.

vocab.example: Il traite le quotidien régional de feuille de chou.
vocab.exampleEn: He calls the regional daily a local rag.
vocab.note: Informal and dismissive: a paper of little value; plural les feuilles de chou.

vocab.example: Le bouclage est à 22 heures : l'éditorial doit être prêt avant.
vocab.exampleEn: The paper goes to bed at 10 p.m.: the editorial must be ready before then.
vocab.note: The moment an issue is closed for printing; also a police cordon (le bouclage d'un quartier).

meanings: to put to bed (an issue: boucler)
vocab.example: La rédaction a bouclé le numéro à minuit.
vocab.exampleEn: The newsroom put the issue to bed at midnight.
vocab.note: Regular -er verb. Press: boucler un numéro; also boucler sa ceinture (to buckle up), boucler un quartier (to seal off), boucler ses fins de mois (to make ends meet).

vocab.example: Le reportage suit une livreuse à vélo pendant une journée.
vocab.exampleEn: The feature follows a bike courier for a day.
vocab.note: A piece built on what the journalist saw on the spot; le reporter (la reporter) writes it.

vocab.example: L'autosolisme reste la règle pour aller travailler en périphérie.
vocab.exampleEn: Driving alone is still the rule for commuting in the suburbs.
vocab.note: masculine (un autosolisme). Transport jargon, now common in the press; l'autosoliste is the lone driver.

vocab.example: La ville consacre un quart de son budget de voirie à la mobilité douce.
vocab.exampleEn: The city spends a quarter of its roads budget on active travel.
vocab.note: Walking, cycling and the like; official texts now also say les mobilités actives.

vocab.example: Il emmène ses deux enfants à l'école en vélo-cargo.
vocab.exampleEn: He takes his two children to school by cargo bike.
vocab.note: plural les vélos-cargos

meanings: shared space (street: la zone de rencontre)
vocab.example: Dans la zone de rencontre, les voitures roulent au pas.
vocab.exampleEn: In the shared space, cars drive at walking pace.
vocab.note: France: a street or area where pedestrians have priority and vehicles are limited to 20 km/h (Code de la route, since 2008).

meanings: school street (closed to cars at school times)
vocab.example: Devant l'école, la rue scolaire est fermée aux voitures de 8 h à 9 h.
vocab.exampleEn: In front of the school, the school street is closed to cars from 8 to 9 a.m.
vocab.note: A street by a school closed to motor traffic at the start and end of the school day; usage is local, set by each town.

vocab.example: Les travaux de voirie bloquent le centre jusqu'en mars.
vocab.exampleEn: Roadworks are blocking the centre until March.
vocab.note: The network of public roads and the department that runs it (le service de la voirie).

vocab.example: Londres a instauré un péage urbain en 2003.
vocab.exampleEn: London introduced a congestion charge in 2003.
vocab.note: plural les péages urbains; le péage alone is a motorway toll.

vocab.example: Les automobilistes ont un mois pour s'habituer au nouveau plan.
vocab.exampleEn: Motorists have a month to get used to the new scheme.
vocab.note: masculine or feminine: un, une automobiliste (same form)

vocab.example: La cyclologistique livre déjà la moitié des colis du centre.
vocab.exampleEn: Cycle logistics already delivers half the parcels in the centre.

vocab.example: Le stationnement payant s'étend désormais au quartier de la gare.
vocab.exampleEn: Paid parking now extends to the station district.

meanings: freelance work (paid per piece: la pige)
vocab.example: Elle vit de la pige depuis la fermeture de son journal.
vocab.exampleEn: She has lived on freelance work since her paper closed.
vocab.note: travailler à la pige: to be paid per article; le pigiste (B2) is the freelance journalist. Also a single paid piece (une pige).

meanings: commissioning body (of a report: le commanditaire)
vocab.example: Le rapport s'adresse à son commanditaire, la mairie.
vocab.exampleEn: The report is addressed to the body that commissioned it, the town hall.
vocab.note: un, une commanditaire. Also the backer of a business and, in crime reporting, the person who orders a crime.

vocab.example: La lettre de mission fixe le périmètre et la date de remise du rapport.
vocab.exampleEn: The terms of reference set the scope and the date the report is due.

vocab.example: Il ressort de l'enquête que la moitié des classes dépassent 30 °C en juin.
vocab.exampleEn: It emerges from the survey that half the classrooms go above 30 °C in June.
vocab.note: il ressort de + noun + que + indicative (a finding). Formal, typical of reports.

vocab.example: Eu égard à son coût, cette mesure ne peut être que progressive.
vocab.exampleEn: In view of its cost, this measure can only be gradual.
vocab.note: Formal (reports, law). eu is invariable here: eu égard aux contraintes.

vocab.example: La ville a végétalisé six cours d'école l'été dernier.
vocab.exampleEn: The city planted greenery in six school playgrounds last summer.
vocab.note: Regular -er verb. la végétalisation (C1) is the noun.

vocab.example: Trois tilleuls offrent un ombrage précieux aux élèves.
vocab.exampleEn: Three lime trees give the pupils precious shade.
vocab.note: masculine (un ombrage). Literary: prendre ombrage de (to take offence at).

vocab.example: Le confort thermique des classes se dégrade dès la fin mai.
vocab.exampleEn: Thermal comfort in the classrooms worsens from late May.

vocab.example: La rénovation thermique de l'école coûterait deux millions d'euros.
vocab.exampleEn: The energy renovation of the school would cost two million euros.
vocab.note: plural les rénovations thermiques

vocab.example: Le rapport classe les écoles selon leur vulnérabilité à la chaleur.
vocab.exampleEn: The report ranks the schools by their vulnerability to heat.

vocab.example: Le pilotage du plan sera confié à la direction des écoles.
vocab.exampleEn: Steering the plan will be entrusted to the schools department.

vocab.example: Le comité de pilotage se réunira chaque trimestre.
vocab.exampleEn: The steering committee will meet every quarter.
vocab.note: abbreviated le COPIL (also written le copil)

vocab.example: Chaque préconisation est accompagnée d'un chiffrage.
vocab.exampleEn: Each recommendation comes with a costing.
vocab.note: From chiffrer (to cost, to put a figure on).

vocab.example: Une étude de faisabilité précédera les travaux.
vocab.exampleEn: A feasibility study will come before the work.

vocab.example: À brève échéance, seules des mesures légères sont possibles.
vocab.exampleEn: In the short term, only light measures are possible.
vocab.note: feminine (une échéance). à court, moyen, long terme / échéance; also a repayment (les échéances d'un prêt) and an election date (l'échéance de 2027).

vocab.example: La cour d'école, toute en bitume, atteint 50 °C au soleil.
vocab.exampleEn: The school playground, all asphalt, reaches 50 °C in the sun.
vocab.note: plural les cours d'école; also la cour de récréation, la cour (A2).

vocab.example: Le nombre de jours au-dessus de 28 °C servira d'indicateur.
vocab.exampleEn: The number of days above 28 °C will serve as an indicator.
vocab.note: masculine (un indicateur). Also a police informer, in crime novels.

vocab.example: Le plan d'action s'étale sur cinq ans.
vocab.exampleEn: The action plan stretches over five years.
vocab.note: plural les plans d'action

vocab.example: Le retour d'expérience des villes voisines est précieux.
vocab.exampleEn: The lessons learned by neighbouring towns are valuable.
vocab.note: abbreviated le REX or le retex (jargon): what an organisation learns from a project once it is done.

vocab.example: Un parangonnage avec trois villes a guidé nos choix.
vocab.exampleEn: Benchmarking against three cities guided our choices.
vocab.note: The recommended French term for benchmarking (from parangon, a model); many reports still say le benchmark.

meanings: remit (scope of a study: le périmètre)
vocab.example: Les crèches n'entrent pas dans le périmètre de l'étude.
vocab.exampleEn: Nurseries are outside the scope of the study.
vocab.note: Also perimeter (geometry, a security zone).

vocab.example: La mesure phare du plan est la plantation de cent arbres.
vocab.exampleEn: The plan's flagship measure is planting a hundred trees.
vocab.note: plural les mesures phares (phare used as an adjective agrees in usage; some write les mesures phare)

vocab.example: Le surcoût des matériaux clairs est faible.
vocab.exampleEn: The extra cost of light-coloured materials is small.
vocab.note: 1990 spelling le surcout

vocab.example: La désimperméabilisation de la cour laisse la pluie rejoindre le sol.
vocab.exampleEn: De-sealing the playground lets the rain soak into the ground.

vocab.example: Les salles orientées au sud sont les plus exposées à la surchauffe.
vocab.exampleEn: South-facing rooms are the most exposed to overheating.
vocab.note: Also of an economy: la surchauffe de l'économie.

vocab.example: Toutes les parties prenantes ont été entendues : élus, enseignants, parents.
vocab.exampleEn: All the stakeholders were heard: councillors, teachers, parents.
vocab.note: Usually plural: les parties prenantes.

vocab.example: Nous avons mené douze entretiens semi-directifs avec des directeurs d'école.
vocab.exampleEn: We conducted twelve semi-structured interviews with head teachers.
vocab.note: masculine (un entretien); plural les entretiens semi-directifs

vocab.example: Le maire a porté un toast à la nouvelle ligne.
vocab.exampleEn: The mayor proposed a toast to the new line.
vocab.note: porter un toast à quelqu'un, à quelque chose

vocab.example: Son discours s'acheva sur une envolée lyrique.
vocab.exampleEn: His speech ended on a flight of lyricism.
vocab.note: feminine (une envolée lyrique). Also a surge: l'envolée des prix.

vocab.example: L'oratrice a galvanisé la salle en trois phrases.
vocab.exampleEn: The speaker roused the hall in three sentences.
vocab.note: Regular -er verb. Also technical: to galvanise (coat with zinc).

vocab.example: Le tracé de la ligne suit la rivière sur vingt kilomètres.
vocab.exampleEn: The line's route follows the river for twenty kilometres.
vocab.note: The route of a railway or a road on the ground; also an outline, a drawn line.

vocab.example: Le viaduc franchit la vallée à soixante mètres de haut.
vocab.exampleEn: The viaduct crosses the valley sixty metres up.

vocab.example: La nouvelle ligne désenclave enfin la vallée.
vocab.exampleEn: The new line finally opens up the valley.
vocab.note: Regular -er verb. le désenclavement (B2) is the noun: ending a region's isolation.

vocab.example: Je veux dire ma gratitude aux ouvriers du chantier.
vocab.exampleEn: I want to express my gratitude to the workers on the site.

vocab.example: Votre présence nous honore.
vocab.exampleEn: Your presence honours us.
vocab.note: Regular -er verb with a mute h: j'honore, nous honorons. Also honorer un engagement, une facture (to honour, to pay).

vocab.example: La vallée rejoint la ligne à grande vitesse en quarante minutes.
vocab.exampleEn: The valley now reaches the high-speed line in forty minutes.
vocab.note: abbreviated la LGV

vocab.example: Une brève récapitulation aide l'auditoire à suivre.
vocab.exampleEn: A short summing-up helps the audience follow.
vocab.note: From récapituler. Informal: le récap.

vocab.example: « Mes chers compatriotes », commença le président.
vocab.exampleEn: "My fellow citizens," the president began.
vocab.note: The opening formula of a head of state's address to the nation; a mayor would say Mes chers concitoyens.

vocab.example: Le pathos du discours a ému une partie de la salle et agacé l'autre.
vocab.exampleEn: The speech's pathos moved part of the hall and irritated the rest.
vocab.note: In rhetoric, the appeal to the audience's feelings; in everyday French often pejorative (trop de pathos: overdone emotion).

vocab.example: Ancienne cheminote, l'oratrice avait un ethos tout trouvé.
vocab.exampleEn: A former railway worker, the speaker had a ready-made credibility.
vocab.note: masculine (un ethos): the image of the speaker the speech builds (competence, honesty, goodwill).

vocab.example: Les chiffres du trafic relèvent du logos.
vocab.exampleEn: The traffic figures belong to the appeal to reason.
vocab.note: In rhetoric, the appeal to reason: facts, figures, logical steps.

vocab.example: L'apostrophe aux cheminots disparus a saisi la salle.
vocab.exampleEn: The direct address to the railwaymen who had died gripped the hall.
vocab.note: feminine (une apostrophe). The figure of turning to address someone (present, absent or dead) or something; also the punctuation mark (').

meanings: prosopopoeia (making the absent or dead speak)
vocab.example: Par une prosopopée, l'orateur fait parler la vieille gare.
vocab.exampleEn: Through prosopopoeia, the speaker makes the old station speak.

vocab.example: Sa captatio benevolentiae tenait en une plaisanterie sur sa propre lenteur.
vocab.exampleEn: Her captatio benevolentiae was one joke about her own slowness.
vocab.note: Latin, written without accents: winning over the audience at the start of a speech.

vocab.example: Son ami de toujours prononça l'éloge funèbre.
vocab.exampleEn: His lifelong friend delivered the eulogy.
vocab.note: masculine (un éloge); l'éloge (C1) is praise in general.

vocab.example: Le portrait tourne au panégyrique : pas un défaut, pas une ombre.
vocab.exampleEn: The portrait turns into a panegyric: not one flaw, not one shadow.
vocab.note: A speech or text of lavish praise; often ironic today (uncritical praise).

vocab.example: Le maître de cérémonie appela la préfète au pupitre.
vocab.exampleEn: The master of ceremonies called the prefect to the lectern.
vocab.note: feminine la maîtresse de cérémonie; 1990 spelling maitre

vocab.example: Il y a six ans, nous posions la première pierre de cette gare.
vocab.exampleEn: Six years ago, we were laying the foundation stone of this station.
vocab.note: Also figurative: poser la première pierre d'une réforme.

vocab.example: La ministre coupera le ruban à midi.
vocab.exampleEn: The minister will cut the ribbon at noon.
vocab.note: The gesture that opens a new building or line (l'inauguration).

vocab.example: Elle posa ses feuillets sur le pupitre et leva les yeux.
vocab.exampleEn: She put her notes on the lectern and looked up.
vocab.note: Also a school desk (old-fashioned) and a music stand.

vocab.example: Sans prompteur, il a perdu le fil.
vocab.exampleEn: Without an autocue, he lost his thread.

vocab.example: Son discours de réception rendait hommage à son prédécesseur.
vocab.exampleEn: Her inaugural speech paid tribute to her predecessor.
vocab.note: At the Académie française: the new member's first speech, which praises the member whose seat he or she takes.

vocab.example: Rendons grâce à ceux qui ont cru à ce projet.
vocab.exampleEn: Let us give thanks to those who believed in this project.
vocab.note: Formal: rendre grâce à quelqu'un de quelque chose. Also written rendre grâces.

vocab.example: Les signataires sont médecins, urbanistes et élus.
vocab.exampleEn: The signatories are doctors, town planners and councillors.
vocab.note: un, une signataire (same form)

vocab.example: Deux cents chercheurs ont cosigné la tribune.
vocab.exampleEn: Two hundred researchers co-signed the op-ed.
vocab.note: Regular -er verb (nous cosignons). Also written co-signer.

vocab.example: Le mouvement a publié son manifeste en 1971.
vocab.exampleEn: The movement published its manifesto in 1971.
vocab.note: Also an adjective: manifeste (obvious), as in une erreur manifeste.

vocab.example: Le quotidien leur a ouvert sa tribune libre.
vocab.exampleEn: The daily opened its op-ed pages to them.
vocab.note: plural les tribunes libres; in a newspaper also simply la tribune (C1 honors: rostrum).

vocab.example: La presse joue son rôle de contre-pouvoir.
vocab.exampleEn: The press plays its role as a check on power.
vocab.note: plural les contre-pouvoirs

vocab.example: La loi protège désormais mieux les lanceurs d'alerte.
vocab.exampleEn: The law now protects whistleblowers better.
vocab.note: feminine la lanceuse d'alerte

vocab.example: La tribune réunit des voix de la société civile.
vocab.exampleEn: The op-ed brings together voices from civil society.

forms.present: m'insurge, t'insurges, s'insurge, nous insurgeons, vous insurgez, s'insurgent

vocab.example: Les signataires s'insurgent contre la suppression des bancs.
vocab.exampleEn: The signatories protest strongly against the removal of benches.
vocab.note: s'insurger contre; elle s'est insurgée (direct se: the participle agrees). -ger verb: nous nous insurgeons, je m'insurgeais.

vocab.example: La présence d'une ancienne ministre apporte une caution morale au texte.
vocab.exampleEn: A former minister's presence gives the text moral backing.
vocab.note: la caution alone is a deposit or a guarantor.

forms.present: fédère, fédères, fédère, fédérons, fédérez, fédèrent

vocab.example: La cause des bancs a fédéré des associations très diverses.
vocab.exampleEn: The cause of benches has brought together very different associations.
vocab.note: é → è before a silent ending: je fédère, nous fédérons; future je fédérerai (1990 also fédèrerai).

vocab.example: La pétition en ligne a recueilli cent mille signatures en une semaine.
vocab.exampleEn: The online petition gathered a hundred thousand signatures in a week.
vocab.note: plural les pétitions en ligne

vocab.example: Le commentaire composé s'organise en axes, pas ligne à ligne.
vocab.exampleEn: The commentaire composé is organised in axes, not line by line.
vocab.note: plural les commentaires composés. School exercise; today's lycée exam calls it simply le commentaire.

vocab.example: Le champ lexical de l'eau traverse tout le passage.
vocab.exampleEn: The lexical field of water runs through the whole passage.
vocab.note: plural les champs lexicaux

meanings: overall tone (of a text: la tonalité)
vocab.example: La tonalité du passage est élégiaque.
vocab.exampleEn: The passage's overall tone is elegiac.
vocab.note: In literature, the effect a text aims at (lyrique, pathétique, épique, comique …), also called le registre; in music, the key.

vocab.example: La première personne et les exclamations donnent au texte une tonalité lyrique.
vocab.exampleEn: The first person and the exclamations give the text a lyrical tone.
vocab.note: feminine lyrique (same form). Also l'art lyrique: opera.

vocab.example: La scène des adieux est pathétique : le lecteur partage la douleur du personnage.
vocab.exampleEn: The farewell scene is full of pathos: the reader shares the character's pain.
vocab.note: feminine pathétique (same form). In literature: moving, arousing pity; in everyday speech: pathetic (pitiful).

vocab.example: Le combat prend une dimension épique.
vocab.exampleEn: The fight takes on an epic dimension.
vocab.note: feminine épique (same form); informal: un voyage épique (eventful).

vocab.example: Le ton élégiaque dit la perte et le regret.
vocab.exampleEn: The elegiac tone speaks of loss and regret.
vocab.note: feminine élégiaque (same form); from l'élégie (a lament).

vocab.example: Faites d'abord le relevé des verbes de mouvement.
vocab.exampleEn: First list the verbs of movement.
vocab.note: Also a statement (le relevé bancaire) and a reading (le relevé du compteur); le relevé de notes (C1) is a transcript.

vocab.example: « Une cigarette nerveuse » est une hypallage : c'est le fumeur qui est nerveux.
vocab.exampleEn: "A nervous cigarette" is a hypallage: it is the smoker who is nervous.
vocab.note: feminine (une hypallage)

vocab.example: La focalisation interne nous fait voir le village par les yeux de Jeanne.
vocab.exampleEn: Internal focalisation makes us see the village through Jeanne's eyes.
vocab.note: focalisation zéro (omniscient), interne, externe (Genette's terms).

vocab.example: L'étude de l'énonciation cherche qui parle, à qui, et d'où.
vocab.exampleEn: Studying the enunciation asks who speaks, to whom, and from where.
vocab.note: feminine (une énonciation)

vocab.example: Le candidat doit restituer les positions de chaque intervenant sans les déformer.
vocab.exampleEn: The candidate must render each speaker's position without distorting it.
vocab.note: Regular: je restitue, nous restituons. Also to give back (restituer un objet volé) and to restore (restituer un texte ancien). Rendre compte de = to report on.

vocab.example: La restitution du débat doit être fidèle et ordonnée.
vocab.exampleEn: The report of the debate must be faithful and well ordered.
vocab.note: Also the returning of something (la restitution des œuvres d'art, des biens confisqués). In the DALF compte rendu: the faithful rendering of a recording's content.

vocab.example: La riveraine ironise sur les promesses de la mairie.
vocab.exampleEn: The resident is ironic about the town hall's promises.
vocab.note: ironiser sur quelque chose. L'ironie (B2 honors) is the noun; ironique (B2 honors) the adjective.

vocab.example: La maire minimise l'ampleur des plaintes.
vocab.exampleEn: The mayor plays down the scale of the complaints.
vocab.note: Its opposite in a debate: exagérer, grossir (to blow up). Minimiser les risques = to minimise the risks.

meanings: to reject (an argument, a witness: récuser)
vocab.example: Elle récuse le chiffre avancé par la maire.
vocab.exampleEn: She rejects the figure put forward by the mayor.
vocab.note: Legal: récuser un juge, un juré = to challenge a judge or a juror. Not réfuter (B1 honors), to prove an argument false: you récuse by refusing to accept.

vocab.example: Les nuisances sonores nocturnes sont la première cause de plaintes dans le quartier.
vocab.exampleEn: Noise at night is the leading cause of complaints in the area.
vocab.note: Often in the plural: les nuisances sonores. La nuisance (B1) is any nuisance (noise, smells, pollution).

vocab.example: Trois décibels de plus, c'est deux fois plus d'énergie sonore.
vocab.exampleEn: Three decibels more means twice as much sound energy.
vocab.note: Symbol dB. The scale is logarithmic: +3 dB doubles the sound energy.

vocab.example: Castelbrune est fière de sa vie nocturne, mais ses riverains dorment mal.
vocab.exampleEn: Castelbrune is proud of its nightlife, but its residents sleep badly.
vocab.note: Nocturne (adjective) = of the night: le tapage nocturne, un bus nocturne. Usually singular.

meanings: breach of the peace at night
vocab.example: Les voisins ont appelé la police pour tapage nocturne.
vocab.exampleEn: The neighbours called the police about a disturbance at night.
vocab.note: In France a minor offence (une contravention): service-public.fr describes it as noise at night, between 10 p.m. and 7 a.m. Le tapage alone = a racket, a din.

vocab.example: La maire parle de cohabitation plutôt que de conflit.
vocab.exampleEn: The mayor speaks of coexistence rather than conflict.
vocab.note: In French politics also a power-sharing government, when the president and the parliamentary majority come from opposing sides (la cohabitation de 1986). cohabiter = to live together, to coexist.

vocab.example: L'acoustique des rues étroites amplifie les voix.
vocab.exampleEn: The acoustics of narrow streets amplify voices.
vocab.note: feminine (une acoustique). Also an adjective: une guitare acoustique, l'isolation acoustique. L'acousticien, l'acousticienne = acoustician.

vocab.example: À trois heures du matin, les derniers noctambules quittent la place.
vocab.exampleEn: At three in the morning, the last night owls leave the square.
vocab.note: un noctambule, une noctambule (same form). Someone who goes out at night; also an adjective (une foule noctambule).

vocab.example: Je n'ai pas perdu le fil du raisonnement malgré les interruptions.
vocab.exampleEn: I didn't lose the thread of the argument despite the interruptions.
vocab.note: suivre, perdre le fil du raisonnement. Le fil conducteur (B2 honors) is the common thread of a whole text or talk.

vocab.example: Restituez la teneur de chaque intervention, pas les mots exacts.
vocab.exampleEn: Render the gist of each contribution, not the exact words.
vocab.note: Also the content of a substance: la teneur en sucre, en alcool (sugar, alcohol content).

vocab.example: On note une inflexion de sa position en fin de débat.
vocab.exampleEn: There is a shift in her position at the end of the debate.
vocab.note: feminine (une inflexion). Of the voice: its rise and fall; of a policy or position: a change of direction.

vocab.example: Le gérant accueille la fermeture des terrasses avec réticence.
vocab.exampleEn: The manager greets the closing of the terraces with reluctance.
vocab.note: réticent (adjective) = reluctant. Often plural: des réticences (reservations).

vocab.example: Son ambivalence tient à ses intérêts : il veut des rues calmes et des clients tardifs.
vocab.exampleEn: His ambivalence comes from his interests: he wants quiet streets and late customers.
vocab.note: feminine (une ambivalence). Ambivalent (adjective) is in this lesson too.

vocab.example: Sa position sur la fermeture des terrasses est ambivalente.
vocab.exampleEn: His position on closing the terraces is ambivalent.
vocab.note: feminine ambivalente. Ambivalence (noun) is in this lesson too.

meanings: to distance yourself from (prendre ses distances avec)
vocab.example: Le gérant prend ses distances avec le projet de la maire.
vocab.exampleEn: The manager distances himself from the mayor's plan.
vocab.note: Also prendre ses distances vis-à-vis de, par rapport à. Close to se démarquer de (C1), to set oneself apart from. Garder ses distances = to keep one's distance.

vocab.example: La radio a organisé une table ronde sur la vie nocturne.
vocab.exampleEn: The radio station held a round table on nightlife.
vocab.note: A discussion between several guests, led by a moderator (l'animateur, l'animatrice).

forms.present: fustige, fustiges, fustige, fustigeons, fustigez, fustigent

vocab.example: La riveraine fustige l'inaction de la police.
vocab.exampleEn: The resident castigates the police's failure to act.
vocab.note: Formal. Spelling: g → ge before a and o: nous fustigeons, je fustigeais.

meanings: to come round to (se rallier à)
vocab.example: Elle s'est finalement ralliée à l'idée des médiateurs.
vocab.exampleEn: She finally came round to the idea of the mediators.
vocab.note: Agrees in compound tenses: elle s'est ralliée, ils se sont ralliés. se rallier à un avis, à une proposition, à un camp.

vocab.example: L'économie de la nuit fait vivre des centaines de salariés.
vocab.exampleEn: The night-time economy provides a living for hundreds of employees.
vocab.note: feminine. Bars, clubs, restaurants, concert halls, night transport and the jobs they create.

vocab.example: La ville a installé des sonomètres sur la place principale.
vocab.exampleEn: The town has installed sound level meters on the main square.
vocab.note: It measures the sound level in decibels.

vocab.example: L'isolation phonique des immeubles anciens est souvent insuffisante.
vocab.exampleEn: The soundproofing of old buildings is often inadequate.
vocab.note: feminine. Also l'isolation acoustique; insonoriser = to soundproof (une salle insonorisée). L'isolation thermique = heat insulation.

vocab.example: L'acousticien apporte un contrepoint technique au débat.
vocab.exampleEn: The acoustician brings a technical counterpoint to the debate.
vocab.note: en contrepoint = as a counterpoint, by contrast. Also counterpoint in music.

vocab.example: Un indice n'est pas une démonstration.
vocab.exampleEn: A clue is not a proof.
vocab.note: Also a demonstration of a product (une démonstration culinaire). A street protest is la manifestation (A2 honors).

vocab.example: Traiter les riverains de grincheux, c'est un argument ad hominem.
vocab.exampleEn: Calling the residents grumps is an ad hominem argument.
vocab.note: masculine (un argument ad hominem). Latin, no accents; ad hominem is invariable. It attacks the person instead of the claim.

vocab.example: Par un raisonnement par l'absurde, elle montre où mènerait une interdiction totale.
vocab.exampleEn: Through a reductio ad absurdum, she shows where a total ban would lead.
vocab.note: Suppose the opposite view, follow it to its end and show the end is absurd. In mathematics, proof by contradiction.

vocab.example: L'analogie avec un immeuble éclaire le problème, sans le résoudre.
vocab.exampleEn: The analogy with a block of flats sheds light on the problem without solving it.
vocab.note: feminine (une analogie). par analogie avec = by analogy with.

vocab.example: La déduction va de la règle générale au cas particulier.
vocab.exampleEn: Deduction goes from the general rule to the particular case.
vocab.note: déduire = to deduce. Also a deduction from a sum (une déduction fiscale).

vocab.example: L'induction tire une règle générale de plusieurs cas observés.
vocab.exampleEn: Induction draws a general rule from several observed cases.
vocab.note: feminine (une induction). induire = to infer, to induce. Also induction in physics (une plaque à induction, an induction hob).

vocab.example: Un syllogisme tire une conclusion de deux prémisses.
vocab.exampleEn: A syllogism draws a conclusion from two premises.

vocab.example: Le jury attend des exemples de culture générale, pas d'expert.
vocab.exampleEn: The jury expects examples from general knowledge, not from an expert.
vocab.note: The broad knowledge of an educated adult: history, literature, the arts, current affairs, science.

vocab.example: Si une prémisse est fausse, la conclusion tombe.
vocab.exampleEn: If a premise is false, the conclusion falls.
vocab.note: Spelling: accent and double s. Not to be confused with les prémices (the first signs, the beginnings), a different word.

vocab.example: Elle s'appauvrirait, s'ennuierait, puis se viderait : la gradation clôt le paragraphe.
vocab.exampleEn: It would grow poorer, then bored, then empty: the climax closes the paragraph.
vocab.note: As a figure of speech: three or more terms in order of rising (or falling) force. Also a gradual progression in general.

vocab.example: L'enchaînement des parties doit être audible.
vocab.exampleEn: The linking of the parts must be audible.
vocab.note: masculine (un enchaînement). 1990 spelling: l'enchainement. enchaîner = to link, to go on (to). Le déroulé (C1) is the running order of a talk.

vocab.example: L'exemple de Castelbrune est un indice, pas une preuve probante.
vocab.exampleEn: The Castelbrune example is a clue, not conclusive proof.
vocab.note: feminine probante. Stronger than convaincant (B2): it settles the point. Often in the negative: peu probant, pas très probant.

vocab.example: Le jury attend une position défendue avec conviction.
vocab.exampleEn: The jury expects a position defended with conviction.
vocab.note: Also a firm belief (ses convictions politiques). A criminal conviction is une condamnation.

vocab.example: Si la nuit est un bien commun, elle a un coût : c'en est le corollaire.
vocab.exampleEn: If the night is a common good, it has a cost: that is its corollary.
vocab.note: A consequence that follows directly from what has just been shown. avoir pour corollaire = to have as a consequence.

vocab.example: Mesurez les implications de votre proposition avant de la défendre.
vocab.exampleEn: Weigh the implications of your proposal before defending it.
vocab.note: feminine (une implication). Also involvement (son implication dans l'association); impliquer = to imply, to involve. Le sous-entendu (B2) is an implied meaning, a hint.

vocab.example: Castelbrune est un cas d'école de conflit entre fête et sommeil.
vocab.exampleEn: Castelbrune is a textbook case of conflict between partying and sleep.
vocab.note: An example so typical that it shows the whole problem. Cas does not change in the plural.

vocab.example: Une référence culturelle précise vaut mieux que trois allusions vagues.
vocab.exampleEn: One precise cultural reference is worth more than three vague allusions.
vocab.note: A book, film, event or work you mention to support a point.

vocab.example: Le raisonnement manque de rigueur : la seconde prémisse n'est pas établie.
vocab.exampleEn: The reasoning lacks rigour: the second premise is not established.
vocab.note: rigoureux (A2) = rigorous. Also strictness, harshness (la rigueur de l'hiver); de rigueur = required (la tenue de soirée est de rigueur).

vocab.example: La persuasion s'adresse aux valeurs autant qu'à la raison.
vocab.exampleEn: Persuasion appeals to values as much as to reason.
vocab.note: persuader = to persuade (B1). Usually singular.

vocab.example: Un orateur persuasif sait quand s'arrêter.
vocab.exampleEn: A persuasive speaker knows when to stop.
vocab.note: feminine persuasive. Convaincant (B2) = convincing; persuasif also works on feelings and values.

vocab.example: L'auditeur doit pouvoir suivre votre cheminement de la question à la réponse.
vocab.exampleEn: The listener must be able to follow your line of thought from question to answer.
vocab.note: Literally a progress along a path (cheminer = to make one's way).

vocab.example: L'exemplification fait partie de l'argument : dites ce que chaque exemple montre.
vocab.exampleEn: Exemplification is part of the argument: say what each example shows.
vocab.note: feminine (une exemplification). Formal; exemplifier = to exemplify.

vocab.example: Exposez honnêtement la thèse adverse avant d'y répondre.
vocab.exampleEn: State the opposing view fairly before answering it.
vocab.note: adverse = opposing (la partie adverse, the opposing party in a lawsuit). La thèse (B1) = thesis.

vocab.example: Personne ne conteste le bien-fondé de cette objection.
vocab.exampleEn: Nobody disputes the validity of this objection.
vocab.note: le bien-fondé d'une demande, d'un argument. Usually singular.

vocab.example: Je voudrais apporter un éclairage un peu différent sur la question.
vocab.exampleEn: I'd like to shed a slightly different light on the question.
vocab.note: masculine (un éclairage). apporter un éclairage nouveau = to shed new light. Also lighting (l'éclairage public, street lighting).

vocab.example: Établissons un parallèle entre la rue et un immeuble.
vocab.exampleEn: Let's draw a parallel between the street and a block of flats.
vocab.note: faire, établir un parallèle entre = to draw a parallel between. La comparaison is the general word for a comparison. As a noun in geography, also a line of latitude; la parallèle (feminine) is a parallel line.

vocab.example: L'examinateur s'est fait l'avocat du diable pour tester ma position.
vocab.exampleEn: The examiner played devil's advocate to test my position.
vocab.note: masculine. se faire l'avocat du diable = to play devil's advocate (to defend a view one doesn't hold).

forms.present: désamorce, désamorces, désamorce, désamorçons, désamorcez, désamorcent

vocab.example: Elle a désamorcé la question hostile en la reformulant.
vocab.exampleEn: She defused the hostile question by rephrasing it.
vocab.note: Literally to remove the detonator of a bomb. c → ç before a and o: nous désamorçons, je désamorçais.

meanings: to bounce off (a remark: rebondir sur)
vocab.example: Je rebondis sur votre mot « choisi » : beaucoup n'ont rien choisi.
vocab.exampleEn: I'll pick up on your word "chose": many chose nothing.
vocab.note: rebondir sur une remarque, une question. Rebondir alone = to bounce, and figuratively to bounce back (after a setback).

vocab.example: Votre objection est de bonne guerre, mais elle ne tient pas.
vocab.exampleEn: Your objection is fair enough, but it doesn't hold.
vocab.note: c'est de bonne guerre = that's fair (a fair move in a contest), said of an attack one accepts as legitimate.

vocab.example: C'est un argument fort, j'en conviens.
vocab.exampleEn: It's a strong argument, I grant you.
vocab.note: j'en conviens = I admit it, I grant that. convenir de quelque chose = to admit it (formal); en replaces the point admitted.

vocab.example: Je fais amende honorable : ce chiffre venait de la riveraine, pas de la maire.
vocab.exampleEn: I admit my mistake: that figure came from the resident, not the mayor.
vocab.note: To admit a fault publicly and apologise. Amende has no article in the phrase.

meanings: to stand up to (tenir tête à)
vocab.example: Elle a tenu tête à l'examinateur sans jamais hausser le ton.
vocab.exampleEn: She stood up to the examiner without ever raising her voice.
vocab.note: tenir tête à quelqu'un. Polite firmness in a debate; it can also mean defiance (un enfant qui tient tête à ses parents).

vocab.example: Sur le financement, je ne céderai pas de terrain.
vocab.exampleEn: On funding, I won't give ground.
vocab.note: In the negative: ne pas céder de terrain. The opposite: gagner du terrain (to gain ground).

meanings: to dig your heels in (camper sur ses positions)
vocab.example: Il campe sur ses positions malgré les objections.
vocab.exampleEn: He digs his heels in despite the objections.
vocab.note: Usually critical: firmness without listening. Défendre son point de vue (C1 honors) is the neutral phrase.

vocab.example: Le débat a tourné à la joute verbale entre la maire et la riveraine.
vocab.exampleEn: The debate turned into verbal sparring between the mayor and the resident.
vocab.note: La joute = a joust (medieval), and the water jousts of southern France (les joutes nautiques).

vocab.example: La question piège visait à déstabiliser la candidate.
vocab.exampleEn: The trick question was meant to unsettle the candidate.
vocab.note: Also of a country, a market or an economy: to destabilise. La déstabilisation = destabilisation.

vocab.example: Elle a de la repartie, mais elle ne s'en sert jamais contre le jury.
vocab.exampleEn: She has a ready wit, but she never uses it against the jury.
vocab.note: Also spelled la répartie. avoir de la repartie = to be quick-witted.

vocab.example: Répondre par une généralité, c'est une esquive.
vocab.exampleEn: Answering with a generality is a dodge.
vocab.note: feminine (une esquive). esquiver = to dodge. Also a dodge in boxing or fencing.

vocab.example: Savez-vous combien coûte un médiateur ? C'était une question piège.
vocab.exampleEn: Do you know how much a mediator costs? It was a trick question.
vocab.note: Also written la question-piège (les questions-pièges).

vocab.example: Une brève passe d'armes a opposé l'économiste à la vice-présidente.
vocab.exampleEn: A brief heated exchange set the economist against the vice-president.
vocab.note: Literally a sequence of moves in fencing.

vocab.example: Il a répondu avec aplomb, sans chercher ses mots.
vocab.exampleEn: He answered with self-assurance, without searching for words.
vocab.note: masculine. Can be critical (quel aplomb ! = what nerve!). d'aplomb = upright, steady, or back on one's feet (remettre d'aplomb).

vocab.example: La question l'a d'abord désarçonnée, puis elle a reformulé.
vocab.exampleEn: The question threw her at first, then she rephrased it.
vocab.note: Literally to throw a rider from the saddle (l'arçon). The ç keeps the [s] sound throughout.

vocab.example: Les examinateurs écoutent avec bienveillance, même quand ils objectent.
vocab.exampleEn: The examiners listen with goodwill, even when they object.
vocab.note: bienveillant (adjective) = kindly, well-meaning. Usually singular.

meanings: to muddy the waters (noyer le poisson)
vocab.example: Vous ne répondez pas : vous noyez le poisson.
vocab.exampleEn: You aren't answering: you're muddying the waters.
vocab.note: Everyday, a little informal. To drown a question in details so as to avoid answering it. Botter en touche (C1) is to dodge the question outright.

vocab.example: Dire qu'il faut du dialogue, c'est enfoncer des portes ouvertes.
vocab.exampleEn: Saying that there must be dialogue is stating the obvious.
vocab.note: Literally to break down doors that are already open.

vocab.example: Sous la pression, le ministre a fait machine arrière.
vocab.exampleEn: Under pressure, the minister backpedalled.
vocab.note: Literally to put an engine into reverse. Often critical; limit it to one point: sur ce point précis, oui.

meanings: to take back what you said
to go back on what one said
vocab.example: Elle est revenue sur ses propos après la publication des chiffres.
vocab.exampleEn: She took back what she had said after the figures were published.
vocab.note: Formal. Les propos (plural) = the words someone said.

meanings: to adjust your aim (rectifier le tir)
vocab.example: Je rectifie le tir : c'est une idée répandue, que je n'ai pas vérifiée.
vocab.exampleEn: Let me correct that: it's a common idea that I haven't checked.
vocab.note: Literally to correct the aim of a gun. Correct a claim without abandoning the argument.

vocab.example: Elle a gardé son sang-froid face à une question hostile.
vocab.exampleEn: She kept her composure in the face of a hostile question.
vocab.note: garder, perdre son sang-froid; de sang-froid = in cold blood. The g is silent.

vocab.example: Le vrai point d'achoppement, ce sont les horaires.
vocab.exampleEn: The real sticking point is the hours.
vocab.note: achopper sur = to stumble over (a difficulty).

meanings: to get out of one's depth
vocab.example: Face aux chiffres, il a perdu pied et s'est mis à se justifier.
vocab.exampleEn: Faced with the figures, he floundered and started justifying himself.
vocab.note: Literally to lose touch with the bottom in water. reprendre pied = to regain one's footing.

vocab.example: La passation de l'épreuve orale dure environ trente minutes.
vocab.exampleEn: The oral test takes about thirty minutes to sit.
vocab.note: la passation d'une épreuve, d'un test. La session (B1) is the exam session as a period. Also a handover: la passation de pouvoirs (between two office holders).

vocab.example: Au niveau C2, la justesse compte plus que la rareté des mots.
vocab.exampleEn: At C2, accuracy counts for more than rare words.
vocab.note: The quality of being exactly right (la justesse d'une remarque, d'un mot); la précision (C1) is precision in general. de justesse = only just (gagner de justesse).

vocab.example: Une enseignante chevronnée a relu tous mes textes.
vocab.exampleEn: A seasoned teacher reread all my texts.
vocab.note: feminine chevronnée. From le chevron, a stripe on a soldier's sleeve marking years of service.

vocab.example: Après trois épreuves blanches, elle était plus aguerrie.
vocab.exampleEn: After three mock exams, she was more seasoned.
vocab.note: feminine aguerrie. Literally hardened to war (la guerre); aguerrir = to toughen. The gu is a hard [g].

vocab.example: Après le diplôme, elle a suivi un stage de perfectionnement.
vocab.exampleEn: After the diploma, she took an advanced course.
vocab.note: un cours, un stage de perfectionnement = an advanced or further course. L'amélioration (B1) is improvement in general.

vocab.example: Elle continue à perfectionner son français grâce à la radio.
vocab.exampleEn: She keeps improving her French thanks to the radio.
vocab.note: se perfectionner en français = to improve one's French.

vocab.example: « Noyer le poisson » est une locution figée : on ne dit pas « noyer un poisson ».
vocab.exampleEn: "Noyer le poisson" is a set phrase: you don't say "noyer un poisson".
vocab.note: A phrase whose words can't be changed or reordered without losing the meaning.

vocab.example: Après dix ans en France, elle avait atteint un palier.
vocab.exampleEn: After ten years in France, she had reached a plateau.
vocab.note: Not le plateau (B2). Also a landing on a staircase (mon voisin de palier, my next-door neighbour in a block of flats) and a stage of a progression (par paliers, in stages).

vocab.example: L'admission se décide après l'oral du concours.
vocab.exampleEn: Admission is decided after the oral of the competitive exam.
vocab.note: feminine (une admission). Les aveux (B2) is an admission of guilt. In French concours, l'admissibilité (passing the written papers) comes before l'admission.

vocab.example: Les candidats admissibles passent l'oral en juin.
vocab.exampleEn: The eligible candidates take the oral in June.
vocab.note: In a concours: having passed the written papers, so eligible for the oral. Also acceptable (une réponse admissible). Same form in the feminine.

vocab.example: Dans de nombreux concours, chaque copie fait l'objet d'une double correction.
vocab.exampleEn: In many competitive exams, each paper is double-marked.
vocab.note: Two markers read each paper, and the marks are compared.

vocab.example: Le niveau C2 ne se définit pas par comparaison avec un locuteur natif.
vocab.exampleEn: The C2 level is not defined by comparison with a native speaker.
vocab.note: feminine la locutrice native. Le locuteur (B1 honors) = speaker.

vocab.example: Son français est quasi natif à l'oral.
vocab.exampleEn: His spoken French is near-native.
vocab.note: feminine quasi native. Quasi (= almost) is invariable; a hyphen is used with a noun (la quasi-totalité), not usually with an adjective.

vocab.example: L'idiomaticité tient au choix des collocations plus qu'aux mots rares.
vocab.exampleEn: Idiomaticity comes from the choice of collocations more than from rare words.
vocab.note: feminine. Technical. How natural and idiomatic a person's language is.

vocab.example: « Prendre une décision » est plus idiomatique que « faire une décision ».
vocab.exampleEn: "Prendre une décision" is more idiomatic than "faire une décision".
vocab.note: Same form in the feminine. Une expression idiomatique = an idiom.

vocab.example: La fossilisation menace surtout les locuteurs qui parlent sans être corrigés.
vocab.exampleEn: Fossilisation threatens above all speakers who talk without being corrected.
vocab.note: In language learning: an error that stops changing because nobody corrects it any more. Also the process that turns remains into fossils.

vocab.example: Ses erreurs s'étaient fossilisées au fil des ans.
vocab.exampleEn: Her errors had fossilised over the years.
vocab.note: The se is a direct object, so the participle agrees: elles se sont fossilisées. No imperative in the drills: one doesn't tell someone to fossilise.

meanings: upgrade (catching up: la mise à niveau)
vocab.example: Un cours de mise à niveau l'a préparée à l'examen.
vocab.exampleEn: A refresher course prepared her for the exam.
vocab.note: Also a software or equipment upgrade (la mise à niveau d'un logiciel).

vocab.example: La médiation, au sens du CECRL, consiste à rendre un texte accessible à quelqu'un d'autre.
vocab.exampleEn: Mediation, in the CEFR sense, means making a text accessible to someone else.
vocab.note: As a CEFR activity: summarising, explaining, relaying meaning between texts or people. Also mediation in a dispute (le médiateur, B2).

vocab.example: Chaque descripteur décrit ce qu'un apprenant sait faire à un niveau donné.
vocab.exampleEn: Each descriptor describes what a learner can do at a given level.
vocab.note: A short can-do statement in a framework of levels.

vocab.example: Le CECRL sert de référentiel commun aux examens de langue en Europe.
vocab.exampleEn: The CEFR serves as a common framework for language exams in Europe.
vocab.note: A set of standards or descriptors used as a reference (un référentiel de compétences). Also a frame of reference in physics.

meanings: Common European Framework of Reference for Languages
vocab.example: Le CECRL distingue six niveaux, de A1 à C2.
vocab.exampleEn: The CEFR distinguishes six levels, from A1 to C2.
vocab.note: Cadre européen commun de référence pour les langues (Council of Europe, 2001; Companion Volume 2020). Also written le CECR.

meanings: modal shift (from one transport to another)
vocab.example: Le report modal de l'avion vers le train suppose un train fréquent et abordable.
vocab.exampleEn: A modal shift from plane to train requires a frequent, affordable train.
vocab.note: From one mode of transport to another (de la voiture vers les transports en commun).

vocab.example: L'aérien représente une part croissante des émissions du transport.
vocab.exampleEn: Aviation accounts for a growing share of transport emissions.
vocab.note: masculine: the air transport sector. Aérien (B2 honors) is the adjective (le transport aérien).

vocab.example: Le kérosène est le carburant des avions de ligne.
vocab.exampleEn: Kerosene is the fuel of airliners.
vocab.note: 1990 spelling unchanged. Usually singular.

vocab.example: La compensation carbone ne supprime pas les émissions d'un vol.
vocab.exampleEn: Carbon offsetting doesn't remove a flight's emissions.
vocab.note: Paying for projects (trees, forests) meant to absorb or avoid as much CO2 as one emits. Carbone stays invariable here.

vocab.example: La liaison ferroviaire entre Valbrume et Paris impose un changement.
vocab.exampleEn: The rail link between Valbrume and Paris requires a change of train.
vocab.note: ferroviaire = rail (adjective). Une liaison aérienne = an air link.

vocab.example: Le trafic aérien continue de croître malgré les débats.
vocab.exampleEn: Air traffic keeps growing despite the debates.
vocab.note: le contrôle du trafic aérien = air traffic control.

vocab.example: Les biocarburants peuvent être mélangés au kérosène sans modifier les moteurs.
vocab.exampleEn: Biofuels can be blended with kerosene without changing the engines.
vocab.note: Also l'agrocarburant, used by those who stress that most are made from crops.

vocab.example: Le carburant d'aviation durable coûte encore beaucoup plus cher que le kérosène.
vocab.exampleEn: Sustainable aviation fuel still costs much more than kerosene.
vocab.note: Often abbreviated CAD in French texts; in English SAF.

vocab.example: La honte de prendre l'avion est née en Suède.
vocab.exampleEn: Flight shame was born in Sweden.
vocab.note: A calque of Swedish flygskam. Also la honte de voler.

vocab.example: La région subventionne la ligne aérienne Valbrume–Paris.
vocab.exampleEn: The region subsidises the Valbrume–Paris air route.
vocab.note: A route flown regularly (la liaison aérienne, B2 honors, is the air link itself); also an airline (une ligne aérienne nationale), though la compagnie aérienne (B2 honors) is the usual word for the company.

vocab.example: Tout voyageur doit être muni d'un titre de transport valable.
vocab.exampleEn: Every passenger must hold a valid ticket.
vocab.note: Formal, administrative: covers tickets, passes and season tickets. Le billet, le ticket (A1) are the everyday words.

vocab.example: Les entreprises d'au moins onze salariés paient le versement mobilité.
vocab.exampleEn: Firms with at least eleven employees pay the mobility levy.
vocab.note: France: a tax on the payroll of employers (private or public, at least eleven employees) that funds public transport, collected where the local transport authority has adopted it; it replaced the versement transport in 2019.

vocab.example: La saturation des bus aux heures de pointe décourage les usagers.
vocab.exampleEn: Overcrowded buses at rush hour put passengers off.
vocab.note: saturé = saturated, full to capacity (un réseau saturé).

vocab.example: La gratuité permet d'économiser le coût de la billettique.
vocab.exampleEn: Free transport saves the cost of the ticketing system.
vocab.note: Technical: the machines, cards and software used to sell and check tickets. Not la billetterie (B2), ticket sales or the ticket office.

vocab.example: La fraude coûte cher aux réseaux de transport.
vocab.exampleEn: Fare dodging costs transport networks a lot.
vocab.note: frauder = to cheat, to dodge the fare. la fraude fiscale = tax fraud.

vocab.example: Les contrôleurs ont verbalisé une dizaine de fraudeurs.
vocab.exampleEn: The inspectors fined about ten fare dodgers.
vocab.note: feminine la fraudeuse.

vocab.example: Une aide versée à ceux qui auraient agi de toute façon crée un effet d'aubaine.
vocab.exampleEn: Aid paid to people who would have acted anyway creates a windfall effect.
vocab.note: masculine (un effet d'aubaine). Economics: a benefit that goes to people who would have done the same without it. Une aubaine = a godsend.

vocab.example: La métropole revoit toute sa tarification.
vocab.exampleEn: The metropolitan area is reviewing its whole fare structure.
vocab.note: le tarif = the price, the fare; tarifer = to set the price of.

vocab.example: Le tarif solidaire réduit le prix de l'abonnement selon les revenus.
vocab.exampleEn: The concession fare reduces the cost of the pass according to income.
vocab.note: Reduced fares by income level, set by the local transport authority.

vocab.example: L'autorité organisatrice fixe les tarifs et choisit l'exploitant du réseau.
vocab.exampleEn: The transport authority sets the fares and chooses the network's operator.
vocab.note: feminine. In full l'autorité organisatrice de la mobilité (AOM): a city, a metropolitan area or a region.

vocab.example: Le cadencement fait passer un bus toutes les dix minutes, à heure fixe.
vocab.exampleEn: With a regular-interval timetable, a bus comes every ten minutes, at fixed times.
vocab.note: Trains or buses leaving at the same minutes past every hour; cadencé = regular-interval (un horaire cadencé).

readingList.title: ABC DALF C1/C2 (nouvelle édition, livre + CD + livre-web)
readingList.author: Isabelle Barrière, Fabien Delcambre and Marie-Louise Parizet
readingList.note: A DALF practice book with an audio CD (2021), listed in France Éducation international's own bibliography of DELF and DALF resources (June 2022). Use its C2 papers with lessons 17 and 21–24, and check that they match the current format described in lesson 24 (no choice of domain since 2020).

readingList.title: Préparer le DALF C1 & C2
readingList.author: Anne Debeuckelaere and Hélène Hulin
readingList.note: Method, practice and answers for the writing paper (2018), useful for the dossier and the long text of lessons 17–20 and the mock paper of 24h1. Listed in FEI's bibliography.

readingList.title: Le DALF 100 % réussite C1/C2
readingList.author: Lucile Chapiro, Dorothée Dupleix, Nicolas Frappé, Marina Jung, Jérôme Rambert and Marie Salin
readingList.note: Practice papers with an MP3 CD (2017 edition in FEI's bibliography). Its papers may still show the choice of domain that was removed in 2020 (lesson 24).

readingList.title: Les misérables, tome IV (French text)
readingList.author: Victor Hugo

It contains the barricades of 1832 and, by our reading, the book on argot that honors lesson 91 describes; check the table of contents before you start.
